verdicts.identityTest: The two nodes are cases, not people or companies, so CIN and DIN do not apply. force:case-agustawestland matches the Wikipedia article (12 AW101 helicopters, MoD contract Feb 2010). force:case-tatra matches the Tatra Truck scam stub: Tatra, then Venus Projects (Hong Kong), then Tatra Sipox (UK), both Vectra entities, then BEML, then the Indian Army. Two separate Tatra matters exist and the record should keep them apart. (a) The Tejinder Singh bribe-offer case, which went to chargesheet and trial. (b) The CBI and ED inquiry into the procurement route and pricing through BEML and Vectra/Ravi Rishi. "The CBI case" in the node label is ambiguous between the two. "Foreign supplier" is accurate for Tatra and Tatra Sipox UK. "Public-sector or government buyer" is accurate: BEML is a DPSU and the AgustaWestland buyer was the MoD.
verdicts.baseRate: The claim makes no discriminating assertion, so no base-rate fraction applies. It is the SPEC-mandated control pairing ("AgustaWestland beside Tatra/BEML — identical fields"). Most UPA-II-era defence cases were CBI cases exposed around 2012–13, so "both UPA-era CBI cases" is a matching criterion, not a finding. The one asymmetry the claim reports, dense record versus stub, comes from Wikipedia coverage and from this file's sourcing, not from the cases. Outside the file, Tatra has a substantial record: CBI chargesheet against Tejinder Singh (July 2014), charges framed (2019), Delhi HC dismissal of his challenge (June 2022), and Antony cross-examined as a prosecution witness (Tribune, 2022-09-29). The symmetric reading is that neither case has reached an Indian verdict. The AgustaWestland trial is pending and the Tatra bribe-offer trial was still at cross-examination in 2022.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial was opened in this session, and none is needed because the claim imputes nothing. On record: Tejinder Singh contested the charges, and the Delhi HC dismissed his plea against the framing of charges in June 2022 (Tribune, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/former-defence-minister-a-k-antony-cross-examined-in-tatra-truck-corruption-case-436267). Antony testified that V.K. Singh never filed a written complaint (same source). On AgustaWestland, Christian Michel denied wrongdoing (cited in the Wikipedia article). No one was asked by this project.
verdicts.innocentReading: One case is dense and the other a stub because AgustaWestland had a foreign prosecution (Italian arrests, three tiers of courts) and a political target that produced heavy coverage. Tatra was mostly domestic and slow. Neither fact says anything about guilt. The thinness of Tatra is a gap in this file, not a finding about the case: the Tatra bribe-offer case has a chargesheet, framed charges and an ongoing trial that this file did not open.
verdicts.reason: Not refuted, but corrections are needed. The chronology holds: both cases were exposed in 2012–13 under Antony, and both had CBI cases (Tatra FIR Oct 2012; AgustaWestland FIR 2013-03-13). Analytic is the right tier for a scoping and control claim, and the record carries an innocentReading. The source chain is only partial. The Tatra Wikipedia stub's body never says "CBI" and never names Antony. Those facts appear only in reference titles ("CBI finds no evidence", "CBI gears up to finalise chargesheet", "Antony admitted VK Singh told him about bribe"). "Dense record for one, stub for the other" is true of this file and of Wikipedia. It is false as a statement about the case: Tatra has a chargesheet (July 2014), framed charges (2019), an HC order (June 2022) and Antony's 2022 testimony. The claim text should be scoped so readers do not infer differential treatment of the two cases.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Change text/lab to: "Control pairing: AgustaWestland and Tatra — both exposed 2012–13 under Defence Minister A.K. Antony, both CBI cases (Tatra FIR Oct 2012; AgustaWestland FIR 2013-03-13); this file holds a dense record for one and only a Wikipedia stub for the other."
2. In d, add: "Tatra procurement through BEML ran from the 1980s across several governments including NDA-I; 'UPA-era' refers to the exposure and the CBI case, not to the purchases."
3. In d, replace "with no outcome opened" with "outcome not opened here; reported elsewhere: CBI chargesheet against Lt Gen Tejinder Singh (July 2014), charges framed 2019, Delhi HC upheld 2022, A.K. Antony cross-examined as prosecution witness 2022-09-29; trial pending — neither case has an Indian verdict."
4. Add sources: https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/former-defence-minister-a-k-antony-cross-examined-in-tatra-truck-corruption-case-436267 and https://www.thenewsminute.com/news/tatra-case-cbi-files-chargesheet-against-lt-gen-tejinder-singh-21638.
5. In force:case-tatra, separate (a) the Tejinder Singh bribe-offer case under PC Act s.12 from (b) the CBI/ED inquiry into the Vectra/BEML procurement route, and label which one "the CBI case" means.
6. Mark the Tatra Wikipedia source as supporting the CBI and Antony points only through its reference titles, not its body text.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: the Union of India (through the IT Minister and later a MeitY affidavit) called the Pegasus Project reports baseless on 2021-07-19 and filed a 'limited affidavit' on 2021-08-16. PIB PRID 1736803 is 'Posted On: 19 JUL 2021', so the 2021-07-19 date is right. The SC order (para 8) gives '18th July 2021', which is wrong; that was the date of the media reports. The edge is pointed at claim:literature:c014, the committee findings of 2022-08-25. A statement from 2021 cannot deny a finding made 13 months later. In time order, the Union's position answers the Pegasus Project allegations of 2021-07-18, not the committee's report. Non-cooperation with the committee (2022) is recorded in c014 itself, so it is not part of the Union's 'position'. The c028 label still carries 'non-cooperation recorded by committee', which mixes up who is speaking.
verdicts.identityTest: FAIL. The source node is s = min:ministry-of-home-affairs. Both acts in the sources belong to MeitY. The SC order says the statement came from the 'Minister of Railways, Communications and Electronics and Information Technology' (Ashwini Vaishnaw). It also says the 2021-08-16 limited affidavit was 'filed by the Additional Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Union of India'. The record's own `d` field admits 'not MHA specifically'. One entity should map to one node, and MHA is the wrong one. No MeitY node exists in research/raw. Create min:ministry-of-electronics-and-information-technology, or a Union-of-India party node, rather than reusing MHA as a stand-in.
verdicts.baseRate: Not a discriminating claim. It records a government's stated position, it does not infer anything from a pattern. Refusing to confirm or deny spyware purchases on national-security grounds is the norm among governments named as NSO clients. Most did this, and only a few (Hungary eventually, Poland after its change of government, Germany's BKA) admitted to purchases. Symmetry: the UPA-era answers on Netra/CMS surveillance also relied on the IT Act s.69 / Telegraph Act s.5(2) framework. The same lens reads the same way, so no partisan asymmetry is built into this edge.
verdicts.denialFound: The edge itself records the Union's denial. (1) PIB PRID 1736803, 2021-07-19 (https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1736803). The press reports 'appear to be an attempt to malign the Indian democracy'. 'there can be no factual basis to suggest that a use of the data somehow equates to surveillance'. Note that in the PIB text the words 'no factual basis' appear inside the quoted NSO statement and in the reference to the earlier WhatsApp claims. The SC order turns this into 'the reports published had no factual basis'. (2) Limited affidavit, 2021-08-16, quoted in the SC order (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/39021018/): 'I hereby unequivocally deny any and all of the allegations made against the Respondents'. (3) MoD written reply in the Rajya Sabha, 2021-08-09, MoS Ajay Bhatt to V. Sivadasan: 'Ministry of Defence has not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies' (https://www.theweek.in/news/india/2021/08/09/no-transaction-with-nso-group-defence-ministry-tells-parliament.html; https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/no-transaction-with-nso-group-defence-ministry-in-rajya-sabha-amid-pegasus-snooping-row-295252). The claim leaves this out.
verdicts.innocentReading: The government's position fits a routine national-security stance: no comment on the capabilities of intelligence agencies, plus a reference to the lawful-interception framework (IT Act s.69, Telegraph Act s.5(2)). The SC order itself (para 52) records that the Union does not claim surveillance is allowed outside national-security grounds. A narrow, ministry-specific denial (MoD: no transaction) is also what you would expect if any purchase had gone through a different agency. It would equally be expected if there had been no purchase at all. The record cannot tell these two apart.
verdicts.reason: The core facts hold, and they rest on a primary record. The SC order of 2021-10-27 quotes the minister's 'no factual basis' stand and the 2021-08-16 'limited affidavit', and calls it 'an omnibus and vague denial'. PIB fixes the date as 2021-07-19. That is documented-grade evidence, not merely reported. But the edge as written fails on three points. (a) Wrong node: MHA stands in for MeitY / the Union. (b) The phrase 'neither confirms nor denies acquisition' appears in neither source, and it is partly contradicted. The affidavit 'unequivocally den[ies] any and all of the allegations', and the MoD told the Rajya Sabha on 2021-08-09 that it had no transaction with NSO. What is accurate is that no ministry other than MoD has said anything specific about acquisition. (c) The target is wrong: a 2021 denial cannot contradict c014's 2022 committee finding, and c014 ('no conclusive proof of Pegasus') does not conflict with the denial anyway. The edge has to be re-pointed and re-worded before it can be published.
verdicts.corrections: 1. s: replace min:ministry-of-home-affairs with a new node min:ministry-of-electronics-and-information-technology (or a Union-of-India party node). For the separate denial, add a second contra edge from min:ministry-of-defence (2021-08-09 Rajya Sabha written reply, 'not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies'). 2. t: re-point away from claim:literature:c014. Create a claim recording the Pegasus Project / petitioners' allegations (2021-07-18, ~300 Indian numbers, forensic hits) and attach contra to that, or attach to c009's case node. c014 is a 2022 finding the 2021 denial cannot answer. 3. text/lab: remove 'neither confirms nor denies acquisition'. Replace with: 'affidavit issued an omnibus denial of all allegations (SC: "omnibus and vague"); declined a detailed affidavit on national-security grounds; MoD denied any NSO transaction (2021-08-09); no other ministry or agency has said whether Pegasus was acquired.' Remove 'non-cooperation recorded by committee' from the label, because that belongs to c014. 4. Quote: attribute 'no factual basis' to the SC order's paraphrase (para 8), or quote PIB exactly. In PIB the phrase refers to the earlier WhatsApp claims and appears inside the quoted NSO statement. 5. Date note: PIB has 19 JUL 2021, and the SC order's '18th July 2021' is wrong. Keep from=2021-07-19. 6. srcs: add PIB https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1736803 and the MoD Rajya Sabha reply (via The Week / Tribune, or the sansad.in answer). 7. tier: raise to documented once corrected, since the primary records are the SC order and the PIB release.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated, the claim is: the NDA government (PM Modi, in office from 2014-05-26) inflated the price and steered Dassault's offset partnership to Anil Ambani's Reliance, between the 2015-04-10 Paris announcement and the 2016-09-23 IGA. The actor and the act fall in the same window, so the dates line up. The dates in the record mostly hold up. SC dismissal 2018-12-14: confirmed in the order. Review dismissed 2019-11-14, French judge appointed June 2021 and French ambassador's note of 2023-07-25: all confirmed in Wikipedia. One problem: "Reliance Defence was incorporated days before" is not in either cited source. The SC order says Reliance Aerostructure Ltd "had come into being only on 24th April, 2015", and Wikipedia says it was incorporated "14 days after the announcement". Reliance Defence Ltd (CIN U74999MH2015PLC263178) was incorporated on 2015-03-28, 13 days before the announcement, but that comes from MCA aggregators and press (tofler/zauba, Sify, National Herald), not from the cited sources. A second problem: the 2023 diplomatic note complains about Indian delays on criminal cases "in general" (Wikipedia). It is not specific to Rafale.
verdicts.identityTest: Entity confusion is present. The record says "Reliance Defence" (incorporated 2015-03-28). The SC order speaks of Reliance Aerostructure Ltd (24 April 2015) and the Dassault Reliance Aerospace JV (described in the order as February 2017; the record's case node says it was announced 2016-10-03). These are three different companies, and the narrative uses them interchangeably. More serious: strongestCounter says "Reliance's share of the offsets was stated at ₹6,500 crore of ₹30,000 crore". Wikipedia actually says: "Air Marshal Raghunath Nambiar said that a single company cannot get ₹30000 crore worth of offsets as Dassault's share was only ₹6500 crore." So ₹6,500 crore is Dassault's share of the offsets, not Reliance's. The figure is attributed to the wrong entity. The opposition price figure checks out: Wikipedia says Surjewala "questioned if there was an escalation of per-aircraft cost from ₹526.1 crore to ₹1570 crore."
verdicts.baseRate: Offset-partner choice: under the DPP 2013 Offset Guidelines the vendor picks the partner in every case ("the OEM is free to select any Indian company as its IOP", per the SC order), and Dassault signed with many Indian firms. So "the vendor picked a private firm" does not discriminate. Outcomes of major Indian defence-procurement controversies (Bofors, HDW, Barak, Tatra, Scorpene, AgustaWestland, Rafale): no Indian public servant has been convicted in essentially any of them (0 of 7 on this file's own case list). So "no court found corruption" is true of 80% or more of comparable cases. It is non-discriminating as exculpation and cannot carry the "unsupported" status on its own. What does discriminate is the specific counter-record: the vendor and the French state both denied, Hollande hedged, and the SC found "no substantial material" of favouritism.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and from several parties. (1) The SC order records a GoI clarification of 22 Sept 2018 "reiterat[ing] that it has no role to play in the selection of the IOP". It also notes a "categorical denial, from every side, of the interview given by the former French President" (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/95183857/). (2) Per Wikipedia, the French Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs said French companies had "full freedom" to choose partners, and Dassault said choosing Reliance "was entirely its own" decision. (3) Reliance Defence denied the allegations and threatened to sue; Jaitley said there was "not a grain of truth" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafale_deal_controversy). (4) Hollande partly walked his statement back to AFP: asked whether India had pressured Dassault, he said he was "unaware" and that "only Dassault can comment on this" (https://scroll.in/article/895491/no-french-ex-president-hollande-did-not-deny-his-rafale-remarks-to-afp-heres-what-he-said). The record's strongestCounter leaves this walk-back out.
verdicts.innocentReading: The MMRCA tender stalled over HAL's work-share and warranty terms. A smaller government-to-government purchase replaced it, and the 2007 and 2016 packages differ in their weapons, maintenance and India-specific enhancements, so their prices cannot be compared. The opposition's ₹526 crore vs ₹1,570 crore set a bare-airframe 2007 bid against an all-inclusive 2016 package. Under the offset rules Dassault chose its own partners. Reliance had been courting Dassault since 2012 (the SC notes the "press release suggests ... an arrangement between the parent Reliance company and Dassault starting from the year 2012"). Like other conglomerates entering defence in 2014–15, it set up new subsidiaries quickly. On this reading the incorporation dates are routine corporate structuring, not a signal of favouritism.
verdicts.reason: The overall calibration ("no court or audit has found price inflation or government-directed favouritism") survives. The SC order says plainly: "We do not find any substantial material on record to show that this is a case of commercial favouritism to any party by the Indian Government, as the option to choose the IOP does not rest with the Indian Government", and "it is certainly not the job of this Court to carry out a comparison of the pricing details." But the record as written fails the source and identity checks, for four reasons. (1) It assigns the ₹6,500 crore figure to Reliance when the source gives it as Dassault's offset share. (2) It states a Reliance Defence incorporation date that neither cited source supports. The SC order and Wikipedia instead give Reliance Aerostructure's date, which falls after the announcement. (3) strongestCase is not actually the strongest case for the claim. It leaves out Mediapart's November 2021 published invoices alleging at least €7.5m in secret commissions from Dassault to middleman Sushen Gupta. Mediapart also reported that Gupta held MoD documents on how the negotiators calculated the price, and that CBI/ED had the evidence from Oct 2018 but did not act. It also leaves out the SC's paragraph-25 reliance on a CAG/PAC statement that was factually wrong, and that the French probe covers "corruption and favouritism". (4) strongestCounter leaves out Hollande's own walk-back, which is the best evidence against the "behest" limb. Symmetry check: the Bofors narrative counts documented agent payments as part of its strongest case and is rated "contested". The Rafale narrative leaves out the equivalent agent-payment record. Mediapart dates those payments to 2007–2012, mostly in the UPA era, which itself cuts against a one-government reading. That omission makes the lens asymmetric. Finally, the claim is a conjunction of two limbs with different evidence. The price-inflation limb is unsupported: no audit or court finding, and the CAG figure was not opened. The "at the government's behest" limb rests on one named party's assertion, later hedged and denied by everyone else, which fits "speculative" better than "unsupported".
verdicts.corrections: 1) strongestCounter: replace "Reliance's share of the offsets was stated at ₹6,500 crore of ₹30,000 crore" with "the IAF deputy chief (Air Marshal Nambiar, Sept 2018) said Dassault's own share of the ₹30,000 crore offsets was about ₹6,500 crore, so no single partner could receive ₹30,000 crore". 2) strongestCase: change "Reliance Defence was incorporated days before" to "Reliance Defence Ltd (CIN U74999MH2015PLC263178) was incorporated 2015-03-28, 13 days before the announcement; Reliance Aerostructure Ltd, the JV partner entity, on 2015-04-24 (SC order)". Add an MCA/aggregator source for the CIN, or drop the sentence. 3) strongestCase: add Mediapart (Nov 2021) on the alleged €7.5m in commissions from Dassault to Sushen Gupta (2007–12) through allegedly bogus invoices, the reported MoD price-negotiation documents in his possession, and CBI/ED not acting; tier it reported/alleged and carry Dassault's denial as its contra. Add that the 2018 SC order relied on a CAG/PAC statement the government later sought to correct (already in literature:c005). 4) strongestCounter: add Hollande's AFP walk-back ("unaware", "only Dassault can comment"). 5) The 2023 French note: say it concerns Indian delays on criminal cooperation "in general", as the ambassador's note states. 6) Split the conjunctive narrative in two: (a) "price was inflated": unsupported, the CAG report not opened and the SC declined to compare prices; (b) "Reliance chosen at the Indian government's behest": speculative, resting on one named-party assertion that was later hedged and denied by GoI, the French government and Dassault, with the SC finding no substantial material. 7) Update symmetryCheck to note that the Mediapart payment dates (2007–12) fall mostly in the UPA era, so the Bofors and Rafale agent-payment fields are filled the same way for both.

verdicts.dateTest: As a sentence: the PMO (under PM Modi, from May 2014) held parleys with French officials during the 36-aircraft IGA negotiation (Jan 2016 MoU to Sept 2016 IGA). MoD desk officials recorded their objection in a note dated 2015-11-24. Defence Minister Parrikar replied on 2016-01-11 that the PMO was "monitoring the progress" and that the objection was "an over reaction". The Hindu published the note in Feb 2019. The SC admitted the documents on 2019-04-10 and dismissed the review on 2019-11-14. The dates line up and nothing is anachronistic. The problem is not timing. It is what the record actually says happened.
verdicts.identityTest: The claim is about two actors. (1) "MoD" as the objector. The note came from MoD officials: a Deputy Secretary (Air), endorsed up to the Defence Secretary, G. Mohan Kumar. The head of the ministry, Defence Minister Parrikar, wrote on the file that the objection was an "over reaction" and that the PMO was "monitoring". So "MoD's objection" makes an official-level note into the ministry's position, when the minister's recorded position said the opposite. (2) "Ran parallel negotiations" is the officials' own description. The Defence Minister disputed it, and so did the head of the Indian Negotiating Team, Air Marshal S.B.P. Sinha (ThePrint, 2019-02-08: "No such objections were ever brought to me by anybody from the Ministry of Defence"). The claim is a conjunction: a true fact (officials objected to "parallel parleys") plus a true fact (the SC did not doubt the documents were real) has been turned into a finding no source makes, namely that the PMO ran parallel negotiations. Note also that the Deputy Secretary who signed the note is below the public rank and must not be named.
verdicts.baseRate: PMO oversight of summit-level government-to-government deals is common, and this deal came out of a Modi–Hollande summit. The 36-aircraft purchase was announced by the PM himself in April 2015. So "the PMO was involved" does not single this deal out. What would single it out is an MoD note protesting PMO contact with the French side. That is rare on the record, but it shows a dispute inside government, not where it ended. Symmetry control (Bofors beside Rafale): for Bofors, the PMO's role was established by contemporaneous documents and investigations, and still produced no conviction. Applying the same standard here gives "documented internal dissent, characterisation disputed", not "well-supported".
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, several. (a) Parrikar's file noting of 2016-01-11, read out by Defence Minister Sitharaman in Parliament on 2019-02-08: "It appears that PMO and French President's office are monitoring the progress of the issues which was an outcome of the summit meeting. Para 5 appears to be an over reaction"; Sitharaman called The Hindu's cropped publication unethical (Swarajya, HT, Free Press Journal reports, via https://swarajyamag.com/politics/rafale-story-of-the-day-was-parrikars-name-and-reply-cropped-out-on-purpose). (b) Air Marshal S.B.P. Sinha, head of the Indian Negotiating Team, 2019-02-08: "No such objections were ever brought to me by anybody from the Ministry of Defence. I am hearing about the letter for the first time." (https://theprint.in/defence/nobody-flagged-any-objections-before-me-says-iaf-officer-who-led-rafale-negotiations/189634/). (c) Former Defence Secretary G. Mohan Kumar said the note "had nothing to do with price", and was about the sovereign guarantee and general terms. (d) Deccan Herald headline "PMO did not engage in parallel negotiation in Rafale" (https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india%2Fpmo-did-not-engage-in-parallel-negotiation-in-rafale-732115.html, returned 403 and was not opened). The SC review judgment of 2019-11-14 (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/26499003/) records the parallel-negotiations point only as the petitioners' case ("documents which suggest that there were parallel negotiations being undertaken by the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) which was strenuously objected to by the Indian Negotiating Team") and dismissed the review: "All aspects were considered by the competent authority and the different views expressed considered".
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a summit-originated government-to-government deal. The PMO, and the French President's office on the other side, followed up on unresolved issues: sovereign guarantee, bank guarantee and general terms. Desk officials saw this as cutting across their formal negotiating channel and protested. The minister ruled that it was monitoring, not negotiation, and told the Defence Secretary to settle it with the Principal Secretary to the PM. The formal team (INT) kept negotiating, and the deal went through the DAC and CCS. This reading fits every document in hand as well as "parallel negotiations over MoD's objection" does.
verdicts.reason: Neither cited source says what the claim says. The SC order of 2019-04-10 (indiankanoon doc 126750916) is purely about admissibility. It never mentions "parallel", "PMO" or "negotiat"; it only holds that the three documents were published and their contents were not disputed. The current Wikipedia article on the Rafale deal controversy has no mention of The Hindu documents, the PMO or parallel negotiations. The record admits The Hindu's articles were never opened. On substance, the documented fact is narrower: MoD officials objected to "parallel parleys" by the PMO. The claim's wording, "the PMO ran parallel negotiations over MoD's objection", takes the officials' description as fact and treats the officials as "MoD". But the Defence Minister wrote on the file that it was "monitoring" and called the objection an "over reaction". The head of the negotiating team said no objection ever reached him. The SC review judgment records the point only as the petitioners' allegation and dismissed the review. Calling a contested description from one side of an internal dispute "well-supported" overstates the evidence. It belongs at alleged with a contra. Its documented core, that the note existed and its authenticity was not contested, can be carried as reported.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Reword the claim: "MoD officials, in a note of 2015-11-24 published by The Hindu in Feb 2019, objected to 'parallel parleys' by the PMO with French officials; the then Defence Minister minuted on 2016-01-11 that the PMO was 'monitoring the progress' and the objection was 'an over reaction'." 2. Change status from "well-supported" to "contested", and set the tier to alleged for "PMO ran parallel negotiations". Keep "the note exists and its authenticity was not disputed" at reported/documented. 3. Fix srcs. Drop Wikipedia as support: it does not say this. Keep the 2019-04-10 SC order only for admissibility. Add the SC review judgment https://indiankanoon.org/doc/26499003/ (records the claim as the petitioners' case and dismisses the review), and add The Hindu 2019-02-08 article (N. Ram), or ThePrint/HT coverage, as the actual source for the note. 4. Add contra entries: Parrikar's file noting (via Sitharaman, Lok Sabha 2019-02-08); INT head Air Marshal S.B.P. Sinha (ThePrint 2019-02-08); G. Mohan Kumar ("nothing to do with price"). 5. In strongestCounter, change "the Defence Minister of the day overruled the objection" to quote his words ("monitoring", "over reaction"). 6. Do not name the Deputy Secretary who signed the note (below public rank). 7. whatWouldChangeThis: "Up" needs the PMO's own records of the meetings with French officials, or a CAG/court finding, not just the MoD file.

verdicts.dateTest: Written as a claim: "State police personnel (16 states + Delhi) justify torture / use it routinely, as of Nov 2023 to Jan 2024." SPIR 2025 fieldwork ran Nov 2023 to Jan 2024 (Appendix 2: "conducted by Lokniti ... in the months from November 2023 to January 2024"). SPIR 2018 is a 2017-18 citizen survey (15,562 interviews in 22 states). Both windows support a present-tense attitude claim. The series begins in 2018, so there is no trend and no UPA baseline. The record already lists that as a void. Nothing fails on chronology.
verdicts.identityTest: Partial failure. In SPIR 2025 the actor is state and Delhi police personnel: 8,276 constables, upper subordinates and IPS officers at 82 locations in AP, Assam, Bihar, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Kerala, MP, Maharashtra, Nagaland, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan, TN, UP, WB and Delhi. CAPFs are not covered. The SPIR 2018 figure ("Figure 5.7: Half the respondents condone the use of violence on criminals in police custody") comes from CITIZENS, not police. It cannot support "the police themselves justify it". It is joined to that conjunct as if it were the same actor.
verdicts.baseRate: The property discriminates; it is not near-universal. Across states, the share of police with a "high propensity to justify torture" runs from Kerala 1% to Jharkhand 50% and Gujarat 49%. On the support index, Gujarat is 63% high support, TN 56%, AP and Rajasthan 54%, and Kerala 3% strong support against 72% very low. On the symmetry control, the high-justification states span BJP-run (Gujarat), JMM-run (Jharkhand), DMK-run (TN) and YSRCP-run (AP), and the lowest is LDF-run (Kerala). The lens gives no partisan reading, which is consistent. No UPA-era baseline exists for comparison over time. National aggregate (SPIR 2025 ch. 5 Key Findings): 30% justify third-degree against accused in serious cases, 9% in petty offences, 30% high propensity plus 32% moderate, and 64% justify third-degree in a minor-girl kidnapping scenario.
verdicts.denialFound: None found from the asked parties, and they were not asked. No MHA, state-police or DGP response to SPIR 2025 was found. ThePrint, LiveLaw and National Herald coverage of the 26 March 2025 launch carries none. The record does not show that MHA or any state police was asked. The report itself contains a partial counter: 79% of police rate human-rights training, 71% torture-prevention training and 79% evidence-based interrogation training as very important (SPIR 2025, p. ~139). On counting, NCRB attributes only 1 of 76 custodial deaths in 2020 to physical assault in custody; NCAT, a civil-society compilation, attributes 51 of 111.
verdicts.innocentReading: Survey answers to hypothetical scenarios (a kidnapped minor girl, terrorism cases) measure what respondents say they would endorse under pressure. They are not counts of acts. Saying third-degree is "sometimes justified" is not proof that it is practised routinely. Even the police-reported frequency item (Table 5.8: IOs use third-degree "many times" 11%, "sometimes" 16%, "once or twice" 14%, "never" 52%) is a perception of colleagues' conduct. More than half answer "never", which works against "routine". Citizen condonation (SPIR 2018) describes public opinion, not police conduct.
verdicts.reason: Both halves of the conjunction, and the record's own figures, fail against the source. (1) "Routine" is an incidence claim. The record concedes it holds "as attitude rate, not incidence" but still marks the narrative "well-supported". The closest incidence-like item in SPIR 2025 (Table 5.8) has 52% of police saying IOs "never" use third-degree in serious offences, and NCRB shows 76 custodial deaths in 2020, so "routine" is at most contested. (2) The strongestCase misquotes the source. "About one in ten police personnel justify third-degree methods" is the figure for "uncooperative" WITNESSES (Fig. 5.7, 9%) and petty offences (9%). The headline figure is "Thirty percent police personnel said that 'third-degree methods' are justified towards the accused in serious criminal cases." (3) The strongestCounter is false against the source. "The majority in every item do not justify torture" is contradicted by Fig. 5.9 (19% absolutely + 45% somewhat justified = 64% in the kidnapping scenario), by 63% agreeing it is alright for police to be violent toward suspects for the greater good (22% fully + 41% somewhat), and by the report's own sentence: "In response to each of these various questions on the necessity of torture, the cumulative responses in support of torture are higher than the responses which reject its use." (4) The SPIR 2018 figure is about citizens, not police. The "police justify torture" half survives, and is stronger than the record states, at the reported tier: one academic/NGO survey (Lokniti-CSDS with Common Cause) with a stated sample design. The narrative as written does not survive.
verdicts.corrections:
Fix these fields in /home/user/india-corporate-intelligence/research/raw/force/literature.json, narratives[10]:
(a) Split the claim. Mark "Police personnel themselves justify custodial torture" as well-supported as an attitude rate (tier reported, single survey). Mark "Custodial torture is routine" as contested. The best evidence is Table 5.8, police perception of IO practice: 11% many times, 16% sometimes, 14% once or twice, 52% never. Add NCRB 2020: 76 custodial deaths, 1 attributed to assault, against NCAT 111 with 51 allegedly from torture. None of this is a measured incidence rate.
(b) In strongestCase, replace "about one in ten police personnel justify third-degree methods" with: "30% justify third-degree against the accused in serious criminal cases (9% in petty offences, 9% against uncooperative witnesses); 30% have a high and 32% a moderate propensity to justify torture; 64% justify third-degree in a kidnapped-minor scenario (19% absolutely, 45% sometimes); 11% say hitting an absconding accused's family is absolutely justified and 30% sometimes".
(c) Delete "the majority in every item do not justify torture" from strongestCounter, because the source contradicts it. Replace it with: "majorities on frequency items say IOs never use third-degree (52%); 71–79% rate torture-prevention, human-rights and evidence-based-interrogation training as very important; answers are to hypotheticals and are not incidence".
(d) Relabel the SPIR 2018 item as "half of 15,562 CITIZENS condone violence on criminals in police custody (public attitude, not police)". Move it out of support for the "police themselves justify" conjunct.
(e) Add sample scope: "8,276 state/Delhi police, 82 locations, 16 states + Delhi, Nov 2023–Jan 2024; CAPFs not covered".
(f) Add the state spread and the party-as-text symmetry note: Gujarat, Jharkhand, TN and AP high; Kerala low.
(g) Same correction in claim literature:c023, field d: "almost one in ten justify third-degree methods" applies to uncooperative witnesses, not overall. Add the 30% serious-case figure and the 64% kidnapping figure.
(h) denial: "none found; MHA and state police not asked".

verdicts.dateTest: The claim restated: CAG (Report No. 4 of 2007, "Union Government (Defence Services): Army and Ordnance Factories", pp. 10-11) found that Army QRs caused poor competition, with 60% of audited cases having a single vendor qualified. That covers audit periods up to about 2006, under UPA-I. DAP 2020 (NDA-II) still provides ab-initio single-vendor, IGA and FMS routes. The narrative itself says the figure is from 2007 and not current, and no time window overlaps in a way that would mislead. The same ORF source also cites CAG Report No. 3 of 2019 ("Capital Acquisition in Indian Air Force", pp. 31-32), which covers NDA-era IAF cases. The narrative leaves this out, although it is the more recent and more pointed audit finding.
verdicts.identityTest: The narrative misstates the scope. ORF's sentence is "QRs prepared by the Indian Army for many of its procurements ... caused poor competition with 60 percent of cases having a single vendor qualified." The 60% figure is about Indian Army procurements in an Army and Ordnance Factories report. The file instead describes it as "defence procurement" and "capital acquisitions by the Ministry of Defence" (the force:lit-cag-report-4-2007 node's sub-label) and "60% of audited acquisition cases". The actor is the Army, not MoD-wide procurement. The 2007 report itself was never opened because cag.gov.in was unreachable, so the figure is carried second-hand through ORF.
verdicts.baseRate: Little sole-source or single-offer buying is non-discriminating in defence, because many platforms have one or two makers worldwide. One comparison: GAO-14-395 reports that the US DoD competed only 57% of its obligations in FY2012 and FY2013, so about 43% by value was not competed. GAO-10-833 says one-offer competitions added about 13% in FY2005-09. The units differ (cases versus dollars), but India's 60% single-vendor share of Army cases is in the same range as a large Western buyer and does not on its own show anything was rigged. Inside India, the fleet's CPPP slice shows the rate depends on the type of buyer: works (MES) 0.1%, Air Force HQ 41.6%, Coast Guard 42.5%. The narrative correctly treats this variation as a lead, not a finding. Symmetry: the 2007 audit covers UPA-I and the 2019 audit covers NDA-era IAF cases, and both found QR-driven poor competition, so applying the same lens to both governments gives the same reading.
verdicts.denialFound: None found, not asked. The MoD's replies printed inside CAG Reports 4 of 2007 and 3 of 2019 were not opened because cag.gov.in was unreachable. The ORF author makes no accusation: the article frames the issue as a reform problem (QR drafting, too many approval points, accountability) and never calls procurement rigged.
verdicts.innocentReading: Army staff wrote qualitative requirements that were unrealistic, could not be tested or did not match the global market, so only one vendor's product qualified. On top of that, many weapons have only one or two makers worldwide, and government-to-government (IGA/FMS) deals are single-vendor by design. That produces high single-vendor shares without any favour to a vendor. The CAG's own explanation (as ORF quotes it) is drafting, not collusion.
verdicts.reason: The core verdict holds: "contested", with "rigged" unsupported. The one source opened (ORF, Behera, February 2021) quotes the CAG's 60% single-vendor finding and puts it down to badly drafted QRs. Neither the article nor the audit it quotes names a beneficiary or a mechanism of favour, and the base rate (US DoD about 43% not competed) shows high single-vendor shares are normal in defence buying. But the summary text is wrong in three ways. (1) "prevalence documented 2007" is the wrong tier: the CAG report was not opened, so the figure is reported via ORF, not documented. (2) The prevalence is for Indian Army procurements, not defence procurement as a whole. (3) The strongestCounter says the CAG blamed QRs "not favour", yet the same ORF article quotes CAG Report 3 of 2019 finding IAF QRs "vendor-driven, and subject to repeated changes during the procurement process" with "unwarranted specifications". That is the strongest evidence for the claim, and leaving it out tilts the balance. With these fixes the narrative should stay as a contested, analytic rating.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Summary text: replace "prevalence documented 2007" with "Army single-vendor prevalence reported (CAG 4/2007 via ORF; report unopened)". 2. strongestCase: add "CAG Report No. 3 of 2019 (Capital Acquisition in IAF, pp. 31-32, as quoted by ORF) found QRs 'vendor-driven, and subject to repeated changes during the procurement process' with 'unwarranted specifications' [reported]". 3. strongestCase and the 2007 claim label/d: change "60% of audited cases" and "defence procurement" to "60% of audited Indian Army procurement cases (Report No. 4 of 2007, Army and Ordnance Factories, pp. 10-11)". Fix the force:lit-cag-report-4-2007 sub-label: it is the Army and Ordnance Factories report, not an MoD-wide capital acquisition audit. 4. strongestCounter: change "attributed ... to badly drafted QRs, not favour" to "attributed ... to QR drafting; neither audit as quoted names a beneficiary". The CAG did not make a finding of "not favour". 5. Add a base-rate line: US DoD competed 57% of obligations in FY2012-13 (GAO-14-395, https://www.gao.gov/assets/gao-14-395.pdf), so roughly 43% was not competed. Note that the units differ (cases versus dollars). 6. upgradeIf: open CAG 4/2007 and 3/2019, including the MoD replies printed in them, to record the denial. If opened and confirmed, the prevalence component can move to documented.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, written out: "India (actor) is the largest importer of major arms (property), and so Make in India (launched Sept 2014) has failed, 2020–24." The premise is false for the window the record cites. The SIPRI fact sheet (Mar 2025) says "India was the world's second largest arms importer in 2020–24 with an 8.3 per cent share of global imports", behind Ukraine at 8.8%. The SIPRI fact sheet for 2021–25 (Mar 2026, https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/fs_2603_at_2025.pdf) also has India second, at 8.2%. "Largest" was true only for earlier windows: 2010–14, 2015–19 and 2019–23. That includes 2010–14, a UPA-II window, which is before Make in India existed. Deliveries in 2020–24 also come largely from contracts signed before or soon after 2014 (Russian legacy deals, Rafale 2016, S-400 2018). Delivery-weighted import data therefore lags policy by years and cannot by itself test a 2014 policy. The record's whatWouldChangeThis line ("SIPRI 2021–25 showing imports rising…") is out of date. That data came out in March 2026: imports fell another 4.0%, but SIPRI now warns of "continued and probably increasing reliance on foreign suppliers".
verdicts.identityTest: The entity matches. SIPRI Table 2, row "2 India 8.3 9.1 –9.3 Russia 36 France 33 Israel 13", is the India the record means, and the unit is SIPRI TIV share of global imports of major arms, not rupee spend. Russia's share is right: the fact sheet says 36% in 2020–24, against 55% in 2015–19 and 72% in 2010–14. The fall in imports and its attribution are right: "Indian arms imports decreased by 9.3 per cent between 2015–19 and 2020–24. The drop was at least partly the result of India's increasing ability to design and produce its own weapons." One attribution is wrong. strongestCase says "SIPRI notes continued reliance on imports for combat aircraft", but the cited 2025 fact sheet has no such sentence about India. That wording comes from the 2026 fact sheet ("recent orders or planned orders—including up to 140 combat aircraft from France and 6 submarines from Germany—indicate its continued and probably increasing reliance on foreign suppliers"), which the record does not cite. The second cited source, the milex fact sheet, says nothing about imports.
verdicts.baseRate: Being a top-5 importer does not separate failure from anything else. It tracks how big a country's forces are and the threats it faces. The 2020–24 top five were Ukraine, India, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, and none was judged on indigenisation. Run the same test on UPA-II as the control and it gives the same answer: India was the largest importer in 2010–14, so the lens would equally "prove" UPA indigenisation failed. A test that condemns both governments tells you nothing about Make in India. Better measures would be the domestic share of capital acquisition, DDP production figures and export figures.
verdicts.denialFound: This is a narrative with no accused party, so there is no denial as such. The government's position is on record: PIB says defence production hit an all-time high of about Rs 1.51 lakh crore in FY2024-25 (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2154551) and exports reached Rs 23,622 crore in FY2024-25, up from under Rs 1,000 crore in 2014 (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2117348). These figures are self-reported and use a different metric from SIPRI TIV. The record does not cite them, and the strongestCounter would be stronger if it did.
verdicts.innocentReading: India is a large military facing two hostile neighbours. It buys whole platforms, mainly combat aircraft and submarines, that it cannot yet build, and today's deliveries pay for contracts signed years ago. So a high import rank is compatible with real indigenisation progress: SIPRI itself credits domestic production for part of the decline. It is equally compatible with indigenisation stalling, since SIPRI 2026 also points to big new foreign orders and domestic delays. Rank alone settles neither case.
verdicts.reason: The narrative record holds as a catalogue of a contested claim. Its strongestCase already says India ranks second, not first, and the cited SIPRI PDF confirms 8.3%, the 9.3% fall, Russia going from 72% to 36%, and SIPRI's link to domestic production. Calling it "contested" and laying out both cases is fair. It needs three fixes. First, one strongestCase statement is attributed to a source that does not contain it. Second, the test it set for itself (SIPRI 2021–25) has now been published and is not reflected. Third, "contested" understates the problem with the claim: the "largest" premise is false for both recent windows, and the inference to "failed" does not follow from the data. The same lens applied to UPA-II gives the same verdict, so it cannot single out Make in India. Treat the assessment as analytic (our own inference); SIPRI figures quoted alone can be cited as documented.
verdicts.corrections: 1) strongestCase: remove "SIPRI notes continued reliance on imports for combat aircraft" from the 2025 attribution. Replace it with the 2026 quote ("recent orders or planned orders—including up to 140 combat aircraft from France and 6 submarines from Germany—indicate its continued and probably increasing reliance on foreign suppliers") and add the source ["SIPRI Fact Sheet — Trends in International Arms Transfers, 2025 (PDF, Mar 2026)", "https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2026-03/fs_2603_at_2025.pdf"]. 2) strongestCounter: add the 2021–25 figures (India second at 8.2%; imports down 4.0% from 2016–20; Russia's share 70% in 2011–15, 51% in 2016–20, 40% in 2021–25). Add the UPA-II symmetry point: India was also the largest importer in 2010–14, so rank cannot single out Make in India. Add the delivery lag (2020–24 deliveries reflect contracts signed before or around 2014). 3) whatWouldChangeThis: mark the SIPRI 2021–25 test as resolved (imports did not rise; reliance flagged as likely to increase). Name the next test as SIPRI 2022–26 together with the MoD domestic-procurement share of capital acquisition. 4) status: keep "contested" for the inference, but add a note that the premise "world's largest" is false for 2020–24 and 2021–25 (second, behind Ukraine). Alternatively, reword the claim to "among the world's largest". 5) Remove the milex fact sheet from srcs, or tie it to a specific sentence; it says nothing about imports. 6) Optionally cite the PIB production and export releases as the government's own self-reported counter-position, labelled as such.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, stated as actor, act, thing and date: politicians (CMs and urban-development ministers of Maharashtra, 1999-2010) and serving or retired Army officers (GOC Maharashtra-Gujarat-Goa, Defence Estates officers) got flats allotted in a society on Colaba land, with the Letter of Intent dated 2003-01-18 and the building up by 2010. The tenures overlap. Shinde was CM from May 2003 to Nov 2004 and the LoI is from Jan 2003. Ashok Chavan was revenue minister and later CM. The two retired Major Generals named (Tej Kaul and A.R. Kumar) were arrested by CBI in 2012. Most dates in the record check out against the source: demolition ordered 2016-04-29, sanction quashed 2017-12-22, SC stay 2018, commission report April 2013, tabled and rejected Dec 2013. There is one date problem. "No conviction in fourteen years" rests on Wikipedia's "As of 2024 ... a final verdict has not yet been reached". Today is 2026-10-04, so the record should read "no verdict as of 2024 (source date); status in 2025-26 not checked".
verdicts.identityTest: The named actors match the source. Wikipedia says: "The report indicted 4 former chief ministers: Ashok Chavan, Vilasrao Deshmukh, Sushilkumar Shinde and Shivajirao Nilangekar Patil, 2 former urban development ministers: Rajesh Tope and Sunil Tatkare and 12 top bureaucrats". On the arrests: "CBI carried out eight arrests including two retired Major Generals Tej Kaul and AR Kumar, retired brigadier MM Wanchoo". The "Army brass" label rests on retired generals and a brigadier. The record leaves out the CAG 2011 report and the reported Defence Ministry findings against two former Army chiefs. The thing named is where identity fails. The claim says the flats were "meant for Kargil widows", and the commission that the narrative cites as its strongest case found otherwise. Deccan Herald, reporting the Ministry of Defence's later suit: "The interim report also refuted allegations making rounds that the plot was reserved for Kargil war widows and victims" (interim report, April 2012; it also found the land belonged to Maharashtra). The beneficiary class in the slogan is itself disputed. The source URL redirects to en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adarsh_Housing_Society_scandal.
verdicts.baseRate: "No conviction after more than 10 years" does not discriminate among major Indian corruption cases. Bofors, AgustaWestland, Tatra and the CWG cases were all unresolved or acquitted for a decade or more, so well over 80% share it. It cannot count as a strong counter on its own; it only shows the case is unadjudicated. What does discriminate here is that an adverse judicial-commission finding (25 of 102 members ineligible, 22 benami) sits beside a High Court order that the building was illegally constructed. Few cases have both. Symmetry: everyone indicted is from Congress or NCP, and the case was investigated and then rejected under a Congress-led state government (Prithviraj Chavan). After 2014 a BJP state government sought to reopen the case against Ashok Chavan, and he joined the BJP in Feb 2024. Applied the same way to both sides, the lens gives no partisan asymmetry in the record, but the 2024 party switch should go in the symmetry note. The Adarsh society also pointed to Samata and Nyay Sagar, judges' societies, one of them built on land reserved for the war-disabled, as comparable practice.
verdicts.denialFound: Sushilkumar Shinde, in an affidavit to the Patil Commission (PTI via Deccan Herald, 26 May 2011): "The plot where Adarsh stands is owned by the State of Maharashtra. The plot was not reserved for Defence personnel or Kargil war heroes", and the Jan 2003 LoI followed a July 1999 GR "which did not provide reservation for war heroes". He also "denied allegation of receiving favours" (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/adarsh-land-not-reserved-kargil-2417926). The Patil Commission's interim report (April 2012) "refuted allegations ... that the plot was reserved for Kargil war widows and victims" (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/defence-ministry-claims-adarsh-land-2379247). The Adarsh society's defence that "there are so many like us" (Indian Express, cited on Wikipedia). Ashok Chavan challenged the prosecution sanction and won (Bombay HC, 2017-12-22). The record itself puts none of these denials in a contra. We did not ask the parties ourselves.
verdicts.innocentReading: The boring version that fits the record: a defence-adjacent plot in Colaba, which the state says was its own land allotted under a 1999 GR with no war-hero reservation, went to a cooperative of defence personnel and civilians. Officials from many departments then relaxed the FSI, CRZ and membership rules in a way the commission and the HC found irregular or illegal. On this reading the "Kargil widows" framing was promotional or media framing, not a legal reservation, so nothing was stolen from widows. What was misappropriated was public land and regulatory favour, which is what the CAG 2011 report says ("grab prime government land – a public property – for personal benefit"). This reading is compatible with wrongdoing. It removes the widows, not the irregularity.
verdicts.reason: The rating "contested" survives. The irregular-allotment core has record support: the CAG 2011 audit, the Patil Commission's indictment, and the 2016 Bombay HC finding that the building was illegally constructed. The emotive "Kargil widows" element was rejected by the very commission cited as the strongest case (interim report, April 2012) and denied on affidavit by Shinde. Defence then claimed the land in 2012, which leaves ownership open. So the narrative is a conjunction: "officials and officers irregularly took flats" (supported) plus "the flats were meant for Kargil widows" (refuted by the commission, asserted by the press and the MoD). That is contested, but for a reason the record's strongestCounter leaves out. The single source is a Wikipedia summary (it now redirects). No commission report, CAG report or court order was opened, and the record contains no contra. The tier should be analytic, since the rating is our own inference, with the facts in it marked reported. The record is not upgradable as written.
verdicts.corrections:
1. strongestCounter: lead with the decisive counter. "The Patil Commission's own interim report (April 2012) found the land belonged to Maharashtra and was not reserved for Kargil war widows; Shinde said the same on affidavit (May 2011); MoD claimed the land in 2012 and the question was never finally adjudicated." Cite Deccan Herald 2379247 and 2417926.
2. strongestCounter: replace "The state government rejected the commission report" with "the state cabinet rejected the report in Dec 2013 and then partly accepted it days later (departmental inquiry against 12 officials), after Rahul and Sonia Gandhi objected" (Wikipedia).
3. strongestCounter: replace "no conviction in fourteen years" with "no final verdict as of 2024 (Wikipedia); 2025-26 status not checked". Also note that no-conviction status is the base rate for such cases and does not discriminate.
4. strongestCase: add the CAG 2011 Defence report on Adarsh, a primary audit record. Quote: "a group of select officials, placed in key posts, could subvert rules and regulations in order to grab prime government land". Also add the commission's finding that 25 of 102 members were ineligible.
5. Restate the claim text to separate its parts: "Officials, politicians and military officers irregularly obtained Adarsh flats on government land (supported by commission, CAG and HC); the land was meant for Kargil widows (disputed: rejected by the commission's interim report)."
6. srcs: update the URL to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adarsh_Housing_Society_scandal (the current one redirects). Add the CAG report (archived saiindia PDF) and the two Deccan Herald pieces.
7. Add a contra (Shinde affidavit; Chavan's 2017 HC win) and a symmetry note: all those indicted are Congress/NCP, and Ashok Chavan joined the BJP in Feb 2024.
8. whatWouldChangeThis: add "a final civil ruling on MoD vs State ownership of the plot, and the SC's final decision on the demolition appeal".
9. Mark the tier analytic, with innocentReading as above.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated, the claim reads: the Indian Army bought about 7,000 Tatra trucks through BEML and a Vectra-group intermediary at inflated prices from 1986 to 2012. The Wikipedia stub says "over a period of more than two decades", and the Rediff FAQ it cites (26 Apr 2012) says "Since 1986, the Indian Army has bought over 7,000 Tatra trucks". From 1986 to 2012 is about 26 years, so "25 years" is roughly right, though the source wording is "more than two decades". The record stops in 2012, and it misses what happened afterwards: the CBI filed a closure report in August 2014 citing insufficient evidence (Firstpost, cited on Wikipedia's Ravi Rishi page). On 26 Nov 2019 Special Judge Pulastya Pramachala declined to accept that closure and pulled up the CBI and the Ministry of Defence (order reproduced by PGurus, a partisan outlet). In the separate case over the Rs 14 crore bribe offer, charges were framed in 2019 and the Delhi HC refused to quash them in June 2022 (ThePrint), so that trial is ongoing. The record's line "Nothing opened records the CBI outcome" is therefore a retrieval gap, not the state of the record.
verdicts.identityTest: The actors check out: the buyer is the Indian Army, the channel is BEML (a DPSU), the maker is Tatra AS (Czech), and the intermediaries are Venus Projects (Hong Kong) and Tatra Sipox (UK), both in the Vectra group. That matches the stub. The narrative's phrase "a middleman protected by BEML" (the task text says "protected middleman") does not appear in any source opened. The stub only lays out the chain of resale steps. "Protected by BEML" turns a description of how the trucks were routed into a finding of collusion against a named DPSU, and no primary record supports it. That breaches the refusal "No vendor named as a beneficiary without a primary record naming it", and it attributes intent to BEML on the strength of a stub.
verdicts.baseRate: This is not a test that sorts guilty from innocent. Routing imported platforms through a DPSU as licensee or integrator was normal practice: HAL, BEL and BEML all ran licensed-production arrangements. Large UPA-era defence-corruption allegations that ended in a CBI closure or a stalled trial include Bofors, Barak, Tatra and AgustaWestland. Most of these cases sit unresolved for years, so "CBI case, no conviction" describes nearly all of them and is not evidence either way. The SPEC's AgustaWestland-beside-Tatra pairing is symmetric: same Defence Minister, both surfaced in 2012-13, both CBI cases. The pairing itself survives, but Tatra's half should now record the 2014 closure and the 2019 refusal to accept it.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, a denial exists. BEML CMD V.R.S. Natarajan said in 2012 that the Army chief's assessment was wrong, demanded an apology, threatened a defamation suit, and said the trucks had 60% indigenous content even without transfer of technology (reported in the Ajai Shukla Broadsword post of March 2012 and in Deccan Herald coverage). The CBI's own August 2014 closure report ("insufficient evidence to file chargesheet", Firstpost, cited at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ravi_Rishi) is the institutional counter. Against that: MoD suspended Natarajan in June 2012 and suspended dealings with Vectra (Deccan Herald). None of this is in the record.
verdicts.innocentReading: BEML held a licence and joint-venture arrangement with Tatra and Vectra. Routing purchases through the Hong Kong and UK group entities can be explained by group tax structuring and by the DPSU's integration and indigenisation markup, not only by a protected middleman. After two years the CBI found the evidence insufficient for a chargesheet. The Rs 14 crore offer, alleged by the Army chief, shows that he refused it. It does not show that earlier tranches were corrupt, a point the record's own strongestCounter makes correctly.
verdicts.reason: The one source cited, a Wikipedia stub, supports "about 7,000 trucks over more than two decades" and an alleged overpricing chain through Vectra-group entities. It does not support "a middleman protected by BEML". That phrase names a DPSU as protecting a beneficiary without a primary record, which the force contract forbids. The narrative's strongestCounter and whatWouldChangeThis rest on "no CBI outcome opened", but the outcome is easy to find. The CBI filed a closure report in August 2014, the special court declined to accept it in November 2019, and the bribe-offer case is still on trial (charges framed in 2019, upheld by the HC in 2022). BEML's denial is also on record. Keeping "speculative" because only a stub was read is a retrieval failure, not a finding. Reworded, the claim can stand as an allegation: allegations by the Army chief and by the CBI at FIR stage, with the closure report and BEML's denial as the counter.
verdicts.corrections:
1. narratives/14.claim: delete "protected by BEML" and use: "Tatra: the Army bought about 7,000 Tatra trucks from 1986 through BEML via Vectra-group intermediaries at allegedly inflated prices." Mark it as an allegation, not as a finding against BEML.
2. status: change "speculative" to "contested". The CBI closure report of Aug 2014 cited insufficient evidence, and the special court refused to accept it on 26 Nov 2019.
3. strongestCounter: replace "Nothing opened records the CBI outcome" with the CBI's 2014 closure for insufficient evidence plus BEML CMD Natarajan's 2012 rebuttal.
4. Keep the existing line that the bribe offer shows refusal, not prior corruption.
5. Add as srcs: Firstpost "CBI shuts Tatra case, says insufficient evidence to file chargesheet"; ThePrint, Delhi HC dismissal June 2022 (https://theprint.in/india/tatra-case-hc-dismisses-lt-gen-retd-tejinder-singhs-plea-challenging-framing-of-charges/1050590/); Deccan Herald, MoD suspends dealings with Vectra. Source the 2019 court order from a court or credible outlet, not PGurus alone.
6. entities/26.d and voids/7: note that the closure report and the court's refusal to accept it exist; narrow the void to the text of the closure report and the 2019 order.
7. literature:c027: update "no outcome opened" so the AgustaWestland/Tatra pair carries identical fields (CBI status and court status).
8. Do not name Ravi Rishi (a private individual, deceased 2016) or Vectra as a beneficiary without the primary order.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reduces to "Congress governments (Rajiv Gandhi 1986–89; Narasimha Rao 1991–96; UPA 2004–14) shielded the people who got Bofors money, so the case ended in 1986–2026 with no conviction." The dates line up only in part. Quattrocchi left India in July 1993, under Narasimha Rao's Congress government. The December 2005 request to unfreeze his London accounts, the Argentine extradition that India lost and did not appeal in 2007, the withdrawal of the red corner notice, and the 2009–11 withdrawal of the prosecution all happened under UPA. All of these are Congress-era acts. Against that, the first chargesheet (1999) and the Delhi HC acquittal judgment of 2004-02-04 came under NDA, and Wikipedia calls the judgment "a setback to NDA government". The CBI's 2018 SLP was thrown out for a delay of 4,522 days, also under NDA. The final dismissal on 2026-08-06 came under NDA, on a private petition by Ajay Agrawal: the Court refused an adjournment and decided nothing on the merits (The Federal). So the "buried" part runs across governments of both kinds. The "protected" part does have dated Congress-era acts behind it. Note also that the 1990–91 Chandra Shekhar government, which strongestCounter counts as non-Congress, survived on Congress's outside support.
verdicts.identityTest: The parties match: AB Bofors and the Hinduja brothers are the petitioners in Delhi HC Crl. 2004-02-04, J.D. Kapoor J, 2004(72)DRJ693. But strongestCounter gets one point wrong. It says the court "held the late Prime Minister entitled to be seen as innocent". In the judgment that sentence is a quotation from an earlier Delhi HC PIL ruling, Rajiv Gandhi Ekta Samiti v UOI, cited in para (xiii) of the submissions. It is not Kapoor J's own holding. His own holding is para 140: "the public servants are completely absolved of all the allegations leading to the offences punishable under Section 120B read with Section 420 IPC ... Section 5(1)(d) read with Section 5(2) of the P.C. Act and Section 161 of IPC". The ASG concession can be quoted exactly as recorded: "till date there was none but CBI is on the trail to gather such evidence." A related error sits in literature:c010. The 2004 judgment did not quash the 120B/420 charges against the Hindujas. Para 141(ii) directs that those charges be framed. The Hindujas were discharged later, on 2005-05-31. Win Chadha and Quattrocchi were not petitioners in this case.
verdicts.baseRate: Indian defence-procurement corruption cases (Bofors, HDW submarines, Barak, Tatra, AgustaWestland, Rafale) almost never end with a public servant convicted. Tehelka/Bangaru Laxman is the rare exception. Most of these cases run longer than a single government. So "buried" says nothing that singles out Bofors or Congress. The SPEC control (Bofors beside Rafale, c026) gives the same picture for the BJP era: a document trail, a court that declined to find wrongdoing, and no conviction. What does single out Bofors is the "protected" part, because it rests on specific, dated acts (the London account unfreezing, the red corner notice, the unappealed Argentine ruling, the withdrawal of the prosecution). It does not rest on the outcome alone.
verdicts.denialFound: No Congress response to the 2026-08-06 dismissal was found. I searched for one (The Federal, DNA and TOI reports carry no party statement). Not asked. Congress's long-standing position is the Delhi HC 2004 acquittal ("public servants completely absolved", para 140, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/561739/). Sten Lindström said in 2012 that Rajiv Gandhi did nothing wrong (BBC 2012-04-25, cited on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bofors_scandal). The other side is on record too. Arun Jaitley (BJP) listed the CBI's lapses. CMM Vinod Yadav, on the withdrawal of the case against Quattrocchi, said: "I agree that there are certain malafide intentions in the case and there is no doubt in that" (Wikipedia, "Allegations against CBI").
verdicts.innocentReading: There is a duller explanation that fits the same facts. The evidence was foreign-sourced commercial documents that were hard to prove under Sections 63 and 78(6) of the Evidence Act, which is what Kapoor J held. The key accused died: Rajiv Gandhi in 1991, Bhatnagar and Chadha in 2001, Quattrocchi in 2013. Extradition from Malaysia and Argentina failed on legal grounds. Delay piled up under every government, including the CBI's 4,522-day-late SLP under NDA. On this reading the case ended because the evidence was weak and time ran out, which is The Federal's account, not because anyone was shielded. The UPA-era unfreezing and withdrawal can also be read as the CBI accepting, after 2004, that it could not prove its case.
verdicts.reason: The narrative passes only as "contested". Its own framing claims no more than that, and the record really does split. The agent-side payments are documented. Specific Congress-era acts that benefited the agent Quattrocchi are on record, and a magistrate called the case's handling malafide. Against that, a High Court, after 13 years of CBI investigation, found no evidence that any public servant received money, and governments of both kinds held the file without getting a conviction. The source chain is weaker than the record claims. strongestCase's facts about the 1993 departure and the two failed extraditions are not in either cited source; Wikipedia mentions only Argentina. They are confirmed by The Federal, which is not cited. strongestCounter misattributes the "entitled to be seen as innocent" sentence to the court's own holding. And the actual strongest case (the London account unfreezing, the red corner notice withdrawal, CMM Yadav's malafide remark) is left out, while a single-sourced claim of "government pressure" on The Hindu is put in. As an assertion, "Congress protected recipients" is a named party's allegation (BJP/Jaitley) with a judicial contra, so it belongs in the alleged tier, not higher.
verdicts.corrections: 1. strongestCounter: replace "held the late Prime Minister entitled to be seen as innocent" with Kapoor J's own para 140: "the public servants are completely absolved of all the allegations ...". If the original sentence is kept, attribute it to Rajiv Gandhi Ekta Samiti v UOI, quoted in the judgment. 2. strongestCounter: change "non-Congress governments (1989–91, 1998–2004)" to "V.P. Singh 1989–90; Chandra Shekhar 1990–91 (Congress-supported); NDA 1998–2004 and 2014–26". Add that the CBI's 2018 SLP was dismissed for a 4,522-day delay. 3. strongestCase: add, citing Wikipedia "Allegations against CBI", the December 2005 ASG request to unfreeze Quattrocchi's London accounts (€3m and $1m; ₹210m withdrawn), the withdrawal of the red corner notice, the Argentine ruling left unappealed in 2007, and CMM Vinod Yadav's remark "certain malafide intentions". Mark The Hindu "government pressure" as single-source (Wikipedia/Hoot). 4. Add The Federal (https://thefederal.com/the-federal-special/bofors-scandal-verdict-legal-analysis-252958) to srcs for "left India in 1993" and the failed extraditions from Malaysia and Argentina. The two current sources do not support those facts. 5. Change "CBI sought closure in 2011" to "CBI sought withdrawal in 2009; the Delhi court allowed closure on 2011-03-04". 6. whatWouldChangeThis: the "Down" trigger has now resolved. The 2026-08-06 order dismissed a private petition (Ajay Agrawal) after refusing an adjournment, and decided nothing on the merits, so it moves the narrative neither way. Record this and cite DNA/The Federal. 7. Assertion tier: alleged, with contra to the Delhi HC 2004 para 140. Keep status "contested". 8. Separate fix to literature:c010: it wrongly says the 120B/420 charges against the Hindujas were quashed in 2004. Para 141(ii) directs those charges to be framed, and the Hindujas were discharged on 2005-05-31. Also remove the Indian and Italian agents from the list of petitioners.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: <Union of India (NDA-II)> <used Pegasus on> <opposition politicians, journalists, judges> <c.2017-2019, which is when numbers were added to the leaked list; published 2021-07-18>. The government in office in that window was NDA (2014 onward), so the actor and the window overlap. Two things fail the date test. (1) Justice Arun Mishra, the one "judge" in the reporting (The Wire, Aug 2021): his old Rajasthan number was added to the database in 2019. BSNL records reportedly show it registered to him until 2018-09-19, and Mishra said "The number ... is not with me since 2013-2014." A judge being the target therefore does not survive the dates. (2) The narrative is stale against asOf 2026-10-04. It leaves out the SC hearing of 2025-04-29 (Surya Kant J, Kotiswar Singh J), where the Court said possessing spyware is not wrong, that "against whom" it is used is the question, and that the technical committee report will not be made public.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor, "the Indian government", is never resolved in any source to a specific agency, so attribution to the state is exactly the point in dispute. The record is honest about this and labels it contested. The SC order (indiankanoon 39021018, para 6) names who was on the list: "nearly 300 of these numbers belonged to Indians, many of whom are senior journalists, doctors, political persons, and even some Court staff". It says court staff, not judges. The word "judges" comes only from the Wikipedia lead ("Supreme Court judges"). The Wikipedia body supports only an SC staffer and her family (11 numbers), two SC registry officials, and an old number once registered to Justice Arun Mishra. The "opposition politicians" target class is also not exclusive: the list included BJP ministers Ashwini Vaishnaw and Prahlad Patel (Wikipedia, citing The Wire).
verdicts.baseRate: The leak held about 50,000 numbers across many NSO client countries, and India held about 300 (0.6%). The 300-of-50,000 figure is not discriminating evidence of Indian state use, because a number on the list is not an infection and the list's provenance is contested. On the forensic side, the SC committee found malware on 5 of 29 devices (17%) and conclusively identified Pegasus on 0 of 29. Symmetry: the same lens applies to the BJP's own figures on the list (Vaishnaw, Patel) and to opposition-run states. Fadnavis denied Pegasus use by the Maharashtra government, and WB's Lokur commission was stayed. I found no UPA-II comparison because Pegasus postdates UPA-II, so the SPEC's UPA/NDA control does not apply. That should be stated in symmetryCheck.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and there are more denials than the file records. (a) IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw in Parliament, 2021-07-19: "highly sensational", "no factual basis", and a number on a list is not evidence of use (PIB PRID 1736803, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pegasus_Project_revelations_in_India). (b) The Union's limited affidavit of 2021-08-16, which the SC called "an omnibus and vague denial" with "no specific denial of any of the facts averred" (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/39021018/ para 51). (c) Missing from the file: the MoD written reply in the Rajya Sabha, 2021-08-09 (MoS Ajay Bhatt, answering V. Sivadasan): "Ministry of Defence has not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies" (https://scroll.in/latest/1002445/pegasus-row-defence-ministry-has-not-had-any-transaction-with-nso-group-says-centre). That denial covers MoD only. MHA, which authorises interception, has not denied. (d) Justice Arun Mishra: the number "is not with me since 2013-2014" (https://www.livelaw.in/top-stories/justice-arun-mishras-old-mobile-number-in-list-of-potential-pegasus-surveillance-targets-report-178868). The party was asked, in Parliament and by the SC.
verdicts.innocentReading: The leaked list is a list of numbers of interest, not of infections. Five of 29 phones carried some malware that could not be attributed to Pegasus or to any actor, and other state or criminal actors also deploy spyware. The Union's refusal to file a detailed affidavit is consistent with a standing policy of neither confirming nor denying intelligence capabilities, which governments apply whether or not they used the tool. The list included ruling-party ministers, so the target set is not purely opposition. Lawful interception under s.5(2) of the Telegraph Act / s.69 of the IT Act exists, and the SC said in 2025 that possessing spyware is not in itself wrong. None of this explains the Union declining to answer the yes/no question before the SC. That is why the honest status is contested, not refuted.
verdicts.reason: The narrative is not asserted as fact. It is labelled contested, with both strongestCase and strongestCounter, and both cited sources support that framing. The SC order of 2021-10-27 records about 300 Indian numbers, a prima facie case, and "no specific denial". The committee findings (5 of 29 devices with malware, no conclusive proof of Pegasus, government non-cooperation) are carried at reported tier via Wikipedia, as the file states. So the contested status survives. The claim text goes beyond its primary source on "judges": the SC order says "Court staff". The only judge in the reporting (Arun Mishra) concerns a number he says he gave up in 2013-14, more than 5 years before it was added in 2019. The file also leaves out a direct MoD denial (RS, 2021-08-09) and the 2025-04-29 SC hearing. These are correction-level defects, not refutation. As a narrative carrying a named-party allegation with a contra, the claim belongs at tier alleged.
verdicts.corrections: 1. narrative:3 claim text: change "opposition politicians, journalists and judges" to "opposition politicians, journalists, activists and Supreme Court staff (including an old number once registered to a judge)". Cite SC order para 6: "senior journalists, doctors, political persons, and even some Court staff". 2. strongestCounter: add that the list also included BJP ministers (Vaishnaw, Prahlad Patel). Add the MoD Rajya Sabha reply of 2021-08-09 ("has not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies"), noting it covers MoD only, not MHA or the intelligence agencies. Add Arun Mishra's statement that the number was not his after 2013-14. 3. In force:lit-pegasus-project-2021 and literature:c028: "no government has confirmed or denied purchasing Pegasus" / "neither confirmed nor denied acquiring" is too strong. Change it to "no ministry other than MoD has denied a transaction with NSO; the Union has not stated whether any agency acquired Pegasus". 4. Bring the record up to date: add the 2025-04-29 SC hearing (Surya Kant J, Kotiswar Singh J). The Court said there is nothing wrong with a country possessing spyware and that "against whom" it is used is the question. It said the technical report will not be made public, though individuals may be told whether their own device was found infected. Add any later hearing (listed for 2025-07-30). 5. whatWouldChangeThis: replace "unsealing of the committee report" with "individual disclosures to petitioners under the 2025 direction". 6. symmetryCheck: record that the UPA-II control is not applicable (Pegasus postdates it) and that the list cut across parties. 7. The narrative's tier should read alleged (with contra literature:c028), not a separate "narrative" tier. The 5-of-29 finding stays reported until the 2022-08-25 order is opened.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a statement: AgustaWestland (via middlemen Michel, Haschke and Gerosa) paid bribes to UPA politicians, bureaucrats and the IAF chief, 2005–2010. UPA was in office May 2004 to May 2014. S.P. Tyagi was Chief of Air Staff from Dec 2004 to Mar 2007. The service ceiling was cut from 6,000 m to 4,500 m in 2005–06, the CBI says payments were made in 2006–07, and the contract was signed in Feb 2010. Every alleged act falls inside the UPA term and inside Tyagi's tenure, so the dates pass. Two dated items in the counter are wrong or stale. (a) Tyagi was never a defendant in Italy. In October 2014 Busto Arsizio acquitted Orsi and Spagnolini of corruption and convicted them only of false invoicing, and its reasoning found no proof against Tyagi. Wikipedia's wording ('acquitted ex-IAF Chief S. P. Tyagi of all corruption charges') is the source of this error. (b) 'Indian trial pending after twelve years' should read 'trial not yet commenced'. In February 2025 the Supreme Court granted Michel bail noting the trial 'has yet not commenced', and the FIR (2013-03-13) is now more than 13 years old.
verdicts.identityTest: 'The top of the UPA government' is not tied to any office. The cited page names who is accused. Italian prosecutors allege Ahmed Patel, Sonia Gandhi's political secretary, received kickbacks; he was a party office-holder and Rajya Sabha MP, not a minister, and died in 2020. The Michel note lists Manmohan Singh, Pranab Mukherjee, Moily, Fernandes and M.K. Narayanan as 'key advisors to target', which makes them targets, not recipients. The note's split is 'AF' €6m, 'BUR' €8.4m, 'Pol' €6m and 'AP' €3m. 'The Air Force' means one person: S.P. Tyagi, CAS 2004–07, chargesheeted by the CBI on 2017-09-01. No sitting minister is named as a recipient in any FIR opened here. Everyone named holds or held public rank, so no refusal is triggered. The record therefore supports 'reached senior UPA-era officials, a Congress party office-holder and the former IAF chief (alleged)'. It does not support 'the top of the government' as a finding.
verdicts.baseRate: Indian defence procurement scandals rarely end in a conviction of a senior official: Bofors, HDW, Barak, Tatra, AgustaWestland and Rafale have none, and Tehelka/Bangaru Laxman is the one exception. So 'no Indian verdict after 13 years' is the norm and does not discriminate in either direction.
