verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Fali Homi Major (CAS 2007-03-31 to 2009-05-31) held a role as independent director of Reliance Naval and Engineering "from 2015-03 / 2016-03", with no end date. The primary record says otherwise. RDEL Annual Report FY2015-16 (BSE 533107, https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/annualreport/533107/5331070316.pdf), Directors' Report: "Shri Rahul Sarin, Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) Fali Homi Major, Lt. Gen. (Retd.) Syed Ata Hasnain, Ms. Ryna Karani and Shri Rajendra Chitale, were appointed as Independent Directors for a term of Five years with effect from January 18, 2016 pursuant to the approval of Members of the Company through postal ballot." The attendance-table footnote says the same: "...were appointed on the Board w.e.f. January 18, 2016." He was appointed at the Reliance takeover board meeting. The 20 March 2015 date is the R-Infra MRA, while Pipavav was still under Nikhil Gandhi. Nothing supports an "additional director 2015-03" entry, and the "independent director 2016-03" date is also wrong. End date: RNEL Annual Report FY2017-18 (https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/annualreport/533107/5331070318.pdf): "Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) Fali Homi Major has resigned as Director of the Company w.e.f. January 30, 2018." The board table lists him "(till 30.01.2018)". The true window is 2016-01-18 to 2018-01-30. That starts about 6 years 7 months after retirement, so it is well outside the one-year cooling-off period. The conclusion about cooling-off still holds, but both 'from' and 'to' are wrong.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes. The FY2015-16 report lists "Air Chief Marshal (Retd.) Fali Homi Major", DIN 03026199, as an Independent Director, with a biography: "commissioned in the Indian Air Force on December 31, 1967 ... raising, operationalising & commanding the very first MI-17 Squadron". This matches the retired CAS. The company is the same legal entity under three names: Pipavav Defence and Offshore Engineering, then Reliance Defence and Engineering, then Reliance Naval and Engineering (now Swan Defence and Heavy Industries), CIN L35110GJ1997PLC033193. The node's identity.din is null and should be 03026199. The cited BSE filing of 27 Nov 2024 (FY2022-23 annual report) confirms the CIN but never mentions Major. Its board is the Dec-2023 reconstituted one (Billimoria, Bairagra, Arun Sinha, Patil, Maya Sinha), so it does not support the role.
verdicts.baseRate: This is not discriminating. The same board meeting on 18 Jan 2016 also appointed Vice Adm (Retd) H. S. Malhi (WTD/CEO, formerly CMD of Mazagon Dock) and Lt Gen (Retd) Syed Ata Hasnain. In this file, Avinash Chander sits on the Astra Microwave board. Retired chiefs and senior officers serving as independent directors of licensed private defence vendors (L&T, Tata, Bharat Forge, Reliance) is the normal pattern once the one-year cooling-off has passed. Major also served as an independent director of Air India (a PSU), per Wikipedia. Symmetry: DPSU boards (MDL, GRSE, BEL) also routinely seat retired service officers as directors, so the same lens produces the same reading for the competing DPSU. On UPA vs NDA timing: the appointment is a private board decision tied to the Reliance takeover, not a government appointment.
verdicts.denialFound: none found — not asked. No wrongdoing is alleged in the claim, so no denial is required. The resignation on 30 Jan 2018 (while the company was in financial distress, before insolvency) is on the record without a stated reason.
verdicts.innocentReading: After a change of control, a new promoter rebuilding the board of a warship-licensed shipyard hires a retired Air Chief with helicopter and acquisition experience as one of five independent directors. This happened about 6.6 years after he retired, far outside the one-year cooling-off rule. He was paid sitting fees (Rs 0.40 lakh in FY2015-16, Rs 1.60 lakh in FY2017-18) and resigned after two years.
verdicts.reason: The underlying role is real and confirmed by primary annual reports, but the claim as written gets its dates wrong and cites a source that does not contain it. The FY2015-16 RDEL annual report gives appointment as Independent Director w.e.f. 18 Jan 2016 (five-year term, postal ballot). It is not "additional director 2015-03 / independent director 2016-03". The FY2017-18 annual report gives resignation w.e.f. 30 Jan 2018, so 'to' should not be null and the "end date not verified / Dec 2023 reconstitution" note is wrong. The cited BSE FY2022-23 filing never names Major. With the corrections and the primary sources below, the edge goes up to documented.

Replace the srcs BSE FY2022-23 filing (d1455b75...) with "RDEL Annual Report FY2015-16, Directors' Report and Corporate Governance Report — https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/annualreport/533107/5331070316.pdf" and "RNEL Annual Report FY2017-18, Directors' Report — https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/annualreport/533107/5331070318.pdf"; keep Wikipedia as secondary. Rewrite d: drop "search summaries give additional director March 2015..." and "annual report ... not opened / end date not verified"; state "appointed with Rahul Sarin, S. A. Hasnain, R. Karani, R. Chitale at the Reliance takeover board of 18 Jan 2016; resigned 30 Jan 2018; ~6 yr 7 mo after retirement, outside the one-year window". per:fali-major: identity.din null -> "03026199"; sub/office -> "independent director, Reliance Defence and Engineering Ltd 2016-01-18 to 2018-01-30"; fix the d line accordingly. Remove the open-question entry at line ~4257 (annual-report confirmation) as resolved. The narrative text "from 2015-03/2016-03 ... primary annual report not opened" should read "2016-01-18 to 2018-01-30 (RDEL AR FY2015-16; RNEL AR FY2017-18)".

Major) match the record. This is the same person named in the CBI AgustaWestland FIR and chargesheet (edge c073). verdicts.baseRate: Does not apply. This is a factual office-holding edge, not a discriminating property. Every service chief has a tenure edge like this, and holding the office implies nothing.

No primary record, such as a PIB release or gazette notification, is in hand, so 'reported' is the right tier. verdicts.dateTest: Claim: George Fernandes held the office of Defence Minister from 1998-03-19 to 2001-03-16. The Tribune of 19 March 2001 (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2001/20010319/main3.htm) says "Mr Fernandes quit as Defence Minister on March 15" and that Jaswant Singh was given additional charge by Rashtrapati Bhavan communique "today", i.e. 18 March 2001. The Wikipedia date of 16 March may be the formal notification date, but no source in hand shows that. There is also an internal glitch in the source: the row's duration template reads {{ayd|1998|12|5|2001|3|16}}, which starts the count on 5 Dec 1998 and contradicts the displayed 19 March 1998. Any event dated 15 to 18 March 2001 cannot be pinned to Fernandes or to Jaswant Singh from this record alone.

The CAG portal listing, seen only through search snippets, describes it as a compliance audit "for year ended March 2011", tabled 9 Aug 2011. The audit came after the matter became public in Oct 2010 and the CBI FIR in Jan 2011, and before the HC and SC rulings, so it sits in the right order. The tabling date of 9 Aug 2011 comes from search snippets only and has not been checked against a primary record.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The entity is the Adarsh Co-operative Housing Society, Colaba, Mumbai. The CAG title is "Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on Adarsh Co-operative Housing Society, Mumbai", Union Government (Defence Services). It is not Adarsh Credit Co-operative Society, a different entity with a similar name. The report number 11 is confirmed independently by the archived saiindia URL path (.../2011_12/Defence_Services/Report_11/). The year label differs between sources: the path uses the 2011_12 series, which matches CAG's numbering by financial year in that era (e.g. 2G was "Report No. 19 of 2010-11"), while the portal snippet says "Report No. 11 of 2011". The PDF cover was not read, so it is not known which form it prints.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable as a test of discrimination. This is a claim that a record exists, not an inference from a property shared with others. Symmetry control: the same lens applies to the NDA-era Rafale audit (CAG Report No. 3 of 2019), which already sits in the same file with the cag→case edge. This UPA-era audit therefore has a matching NDA-era counterpart, and the pair is balanced.
verdicts.denialFound: None found for the existence or number of the report; no one disputes that the audit exists. verdicts.innocentReading: This is a neutral record that a statutory auditor examined the case. The CAG quote ("a group of select officials, placed in key posts, could subvert rules...") is the auditor's finding, not a court finding of guilt. An audit observation is not adjudication. The 'enforce' predicate overstates it a little, since CAG has no power to sanction; 'investigation/audit' is the accurate meaning.
verdicts.reason: The claim holds at the 'reported' tier. Two independent pointers agree on Report No. 11 about Adarsh, Defence Services: (1) the CAG portal listing, seen through search snippets (cag.gov.in/en/audit-report/details/16039 and saiindia.gov.in/defence/new-delhi-i/en/audit-report/details/16039); (2) the Wikipedia citation to the CAG's own PDF, archived in 2012, whose path is .../2011_12/Defence_Services/Report_11/Adarsh_Defence.pdf. I could not open the primary record. cag.gov.in returned 503, saiindia.gov.in reset the connection, and web.archive.org reset the connection and is blocked for WebFetch. So it cannot be 'documented'. The edge's only cited sources are Wikipedia, and one of them is a bare redirect to the other. That makes the source chain thinner than it should be, but it is not wrong.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: CAG reported to Parliament on 21 Jul 2017 that 61 of 152 Army ammunition types held stock for under 10 days. The stock data is as of September 2016. The Outlook source is dated 25 Jul 2017, and Jaitley's Rajya Sabha reply ("significant progress has been made" since the audit date) is the same day. These dates are consistent. One caveat: the record's "from: 2017-07" is the tabling date, not the date of the condition. The shortfall describes stock in Sep 2016, and the minister says it changed afterwards, so the claim must not be read as describing stock in Jul 2017 or later.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is the CAG (constitutional auditor). The subject is MoD/Army ammunition management, which matches s=cag and t=min:ministry-of-defence. The report can be identified from search results and press: Report No. 15 of 2017, a compliance audit of the Union Government (Defence Services), Army and Ordnance Factories, tabled 21 Jul 2017. The CAG listing page (cag.gov.in/content/report-no15-2017-...) and the overview PDF returned 503 or a connection reset, so I could not read the paragraph number in the primary document. The tag "report number unverified" can be narrowed to "paragraph number unverified."
verdicts.baseRate: This shortfall is chronic, not specific to one government. CAG Report No. 19 of 2015, tabled 8-9 May 2015 and covering 2008-09 to 2012-13 (the UPA-II period), found holdings under 10 days for more than 50% of ammunition types and only about 10% held at the full 40-day War Wastage Reserve (Tribune, May 2015). Applying the same lens to the UPA-II control gives the same reading, and slightly worse. A critical ammunition finding appears in essentially every CAG ammunition audit, so it says nothing about which government was in office. The claim stays fair because it makes no attribution to any government.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. In Rajya Sabha on 25 Jul 2017, Defence Minister Arun Jaitley said the forces are "reasonably and sufficiently equipped" to defend the country and that "Subsequently thereafter, significant progress has been made" (Outlook, https://www.outlookindia.com/national/after-cags-report-on-shortage-of-ammunition-in-army-jaitley-says-forces-sufficie-news-299775). The record already carries this. Later reporting (HT, 16 Nov 2017) says the government set a June 2018 target to close the shortage.
verdicts.innocentReading: The Ordnance Factory Board has under-supplied for a long time and has had quality rejections since at least 2013, and import procurement for War Wastage Reserve stock is slow. The audit was a routine CAG compliance finding on stock as of Sep 2016. After Uri, emergency procurement powers were used, and the minister says stock improved after the audit date. The finding shows the oversight system working (CAG audit, tabled, questioned in Parliament, minister answered). It is not evidence of concealment.
verdicts.reason: The source says what the claim says. Outlook: "61 out of 152 types of ammunition available were meant for less than 10 days of fighting a war" and "The army is supposed to hold stocks of ammunition for 40 days of an intense war." The Quint (21 Jul 2017) independently confirms: "Out of 152 types of ammunition crucial to fight a war, 61 types would last 10 days of war," based on September 2016 data. The figures, the auditor and the ministry all match, and the denial is recorded. The claim does not combine true facts into an insinuation, and it does not name a person below public rank or give operational detail beyond what CAG published. Two independent outlets would technically meet the documented tier. I keep it at reported because the primary CAG text (report and paragraph) could not be opened here (cag.gov.in returned 503). Upgrade to documented once the paragraph in Report No. 15 of 2017 is read.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change "report number unverified" to "CAG Report No. 15 of 2017 (Compliance Audit, Army and Ordnance Factories), tabled 21 Jul 2017; paragraph number not verified." 2) Add to d: "stock position as of September 2016," and keep from=2017-07 only as the tabling date, or add a note on the condition date. 3) Add a second source: The Quint, 21 Jul 2017, https://www.thequint.com/india/2017/07/21/cag-slams-ofb-for-critical-lack-in-supply-of-ammunition-to-army. Do not use its "20-day reserves" phrasing; the War Wastage Reserve norm is 40 days. 4) Add the CAG primary link https://cag.gov.in/content/report-no15-2017-compliance-audit-union-government-army-and-ordnance-factories-reports with upgradeIf: "paragraph text read on cag.gov.in confirms 61/152 below 10(I) days." 5) Add the symmetry control: CAG Report No. 19 of 2015 (data from the UPA-II period, 2008-13) found more than 50% of ammunition types below 10 days (Tribune, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/army-s-ammo-won-t-last-10-days-if-there-s-war-cag-78596). This frames the finding as chronic, not specific to one government. 6) Optionally note the OFB supply-quality angle that the same report raised (ammunition supplied since March 2013).

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Ministry of Defence (Government of India) signed a contract with AB Bofors for 410 155mm howitzers on 24 Mar 1986, during the Rajiv Gandhi government (Oct 1984 to Dec 1989), so the dates overlap. A primary record backs the date. The Delhi HC judgment of 31 May 2005 (Srichand P. Hinduja v State, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/230231/) refers to "the Bofors contract dated 24.3.1986" and to "counter trade obligations of Bofors, which obligations are created by the contract of 24.3.1986 itself." The record already notes the date falls outside the 2000–2026 minister window and is kept only for the Bofors–Rafale control. That is correct.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. The counterparty is AB Bofors (Sweden) and the buyer is the Government of India / MoD, which is the entity the HC judgment and the press timelines name. The gun is the FH-77B 155mm field howitzer. The source gives the quantity as 410. Zee News's own intro says "400" but its timeline says "410 units", and 410 is the figure most sources use.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable. This is a plain contract-award edge, not a discriminating property. As a symmetry check, the Rafale control should carry the same fields (date, quantity, value in the original currency, and a primary source). This edge currently cites only Wikipedia and gives the value in a converted currency, so the two cases are not recorded symmetrically.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable to a contract-award fact. Nobody disputes that the contract existed or when it was signed. The bribery allegations are separate edges (c054/c055). The Hindujas were discharged by the Delhi HC on 31 May 2005; the judgment is at https://indiankanoon.org/doc/230231/.
verdicts.innocentReading: There is no wrongdoing in this edge. It records a sovereign procurement contract. The problem is accuracy: the US$285 m figure appears to be a widely repeated error, or perhaps a partial figure, that started in a Yahoo News piece Wikipedia cites.
verdicts.reason: The date, parties and quantity hold up, and the date is confirmed by a primary court record. The load-bearing amount does not. The cited Wikipedia timeline does say "A $285 million contract ... was signed for supply of 410 155 mm Howitzer field guns." It cites a dead Yahoo News piece, and the same article's lead calls the deal a US$1.4 billion package and a Rs 15 billion contract. The standard reported value is Rs 1,437.72 crore. Zee News timeline: "Government of India and Bofors enter into contract for supply of 410 units of 155mm Howitzer guns valuing Rs 1437.72 crores." The Tribune also carries the Rs 1,437 crore figure. At the 1986 exchange rate of roughly Rs 12–12.6 per US$, that is about US$1.1–1.2 bn, about four times US$285 m. The source contradicts itself and the figure clashes with the standard rupee value, so the stated amount cannot stand. Wikipedia is also a tertiary source, not "a credible outlet with named sourcing" under the contract.
verdicts.corrections: lab/text: replace "US$285 m" with "Rs 1,437.72 crore (as reported)" and drop the dollar figure, or add the note "US$285 m figure in Wikipedia/Yahoo is inconsistent with Rs 1,437.72 crore at 1986 rates; not used". d: delete "Rupee value not verified" and state the rupee value with its sources. srcs: add the Delhi HC 31 May 2005 judgment (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/230231/) for the contract date ("contract dated 24.3.1986"). Add the Zee News timeline (https://zeenews.india.com/india/three-decades-of-bofors-case-a-timeline-2050864.html) and The Tribune (https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/31-yrs-after-bofors-india-gets-new-gun-409381/) for the quantity and Rs value. Keep Wikipedia only as a pointer, or drop it. tier: keep "reported". It could go to documented for date and parties via the HC record, but the value rests on press timelines and not on a contract document or a CAG report. Make the Rafale control edge use the same fields.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: AB Bofors (alleged) paid about Rs 64 crore in commissions to intermediaries around the 24 Mar 1986 contract, alleged from 16 Apr 1987. The 1986 contract was signed under the Rajiv Gandhi (Congress) government. Swedish Radio first made the kickback allegation on 16 Apr 1987, so from=1987-04-16 is a fair start date for the allegation. Two caveats. (1) According to Wikipedia, the 16 Apr broadcast did not give the amount; the ~Rs 60-64 crore figure came later (a May 1987 broadcast and the Swedish National Audit Bureau report of June 1987). (2) The answer and ruling sit later in time and are recorded in the file: the Hinduja counsel's answer and the Delhi HC quashing (31 May 2005, c056/c058), the SC dismissal (2 Nov 2018, c060) and the final dismissal (6 Aug 2026, c061). The dates are consistent and there is no chronology error.
verdicts.identityTest: The source node is force:ab-bofors (AB Bofors, Sweden). The 2005 judgment names the company as 'M/s Krtongen Kemi Och Forvaltning AB (for short "the Bofors Company")', which is the renamed Bofors entity. The record should note this name so the identity can be checked against the judgment. The target is force:case-bofors, a case-record node. The intermediaries are named in the judgment's quoted CBI note ('payment made to A.E. Services and M/s Svenska Inc.') and in the Hinduja-side facts (McIntyre Corporation). The claim names no person below public rank, so the identity test passes.
verdicts.baseRate: This is a single-case claim, so a base rate is not really meaningful. The SPEC symmetry control is Bofors beside Rafale. Rafale's alleged edge (c063) carries contras from the vendor (Dassault, c065), the MoD (c064) and Reliance (c066). Bofors' alleged edge (c055) carries a contra only from the Hinduja group (c056) plus court rulings. It has none from AB Bofors, the edge's own source node, even though the vendor did answer publicly. The asymmetry runs against Bofors and should be fixed. It does not refute the claim.
verdicts.denialFound: (1) In the file: Hinduja counsel, as recorded in Delhi HC, Srichand P. Hinduja v State through CBI, 31 May 2005 (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/230231/): 'Fortunately, they have been vindicated and charges of corruption have been quashed by the High Court... instead of launching a persecution based on a political agenda.' The quote is accurate. (2) Not in the file: AB Bofors' own response, which is the vendor's denial. Bofors said the payments to three non-Indian companies were 'winding-up charges' for terminated agency agreements, and its President told the Joint Parliamentary Committee that 'no commission was paid to any Indian agent' (summarised at https://www.csmonitor.com/1987/1012/iscand.html and https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/india/boffors-gun-deal.htm). (3) The court ruling: in the same 2005 judgment, the HC discharged the Bofors company and quashed all proceedings against the Hinduja brothers. It also recorded that the investigation cost 'nearly rupees 250 crores' and that the 'bubble... burst'.
verdicts.innocentReading: Bofors' account is that the payments were contractual 'winding-up charges' owed to former agents (A.E. Services, Svenska, Pitco/Moresco) when their agency agreements were ended. On that account they were not bribes. Before May 1985, paying agents was legitimate: the 2005 judgment records that 'up to April, 1985, having agents was legitimate as the Government itself used to pay them commissions'. No court ever convicted anyone. The proceedings were quashed or discharged, not tried. So the existence of payments to intermediaries is well supported, but their character as kickbacks remains an unadjudicated allegation. 'Alleged' is the right tier, and the label must not slide into 'kickback' as a finding.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives at 'alleged'. I opened all three sources. National Herald (2 Nov 2018) says it directly: 'dismissed CBI's appeal against the Delhi High Court verdict discharging all the accused including Hinduja brothers in ₹64 crore Bofors pay-off case.' Wikipedia says 'The Swedish company paid ₹640 million in kickbacks', citing India Today 2009, which equals Rs 64 crore. The Delhi HC 2005 judgment (Indian Kanoon 230231) does not mention Rs 64 crore. It does name the intermediaries through the CBI note ('payment made to A.E. Services and M/s Svenska Inc.' was 'in respect of the gun contract'), it contains the Hinduja counsel's answer quoted in c056, and it contains the quashing. The tier is correct: a named party (the CBI, through its chargesheet) asserted the payments, there was no conviction, and a contra is present in the same file. Three defects remain, all fixable, none refuting. (a) The d field credits the Rs 64 crore figure to 'Swedish Radio (16 Apr 1987) and the CBI chargesheet', but neither is among the cited sources, and the 16 Apr broadcast did not give the amount. (b) The only party contra comes from the Hinduja group, not from AB Bofors, the source node. Bofors' 'winding-up charges / no commission to any Indian agent' answer is missing, which breaks symmetry with Rafale, where Dassault's contra is recorded. (c) The edge carries a:64 from ab-bofors to case-bofors, a case node. Under the contract's rule that money flows s→t, that reads as Rs 64 crore paid into a case record.
verdicts.corrections:
1. In d, replace 'Alleged by Swedish Radio (16 Apr 1987) and by the CBI chargesheet' with: 'Kickback allegation first broadcast by Swedish Radio, 16 Apr 1987; the ~Rs 64 crore figure is the amount carried in press accounts of the CBI case (National Herald, 2 Nov 2018: "₹64 crore Bofors pay-off case"; India Today 2009 via Wikipedia: ₹640 million).' If the attribution to the CBI chargesheet is kept, add the chargesheet or a report quoting it as a source.
2. Replace the Wikipedia source with its underlying citation: India Today, 'Key players in Bofors scandal', 28 Apr 2009, archived at archive.today/20120716110017. Optionally add the Swedish National Audit Bureau report of June 1987 as the primary record that payments to agents existed.
3. Add a contra edge from force:ab-bofors to claim:money-people:c055, tier reported: 'Bofors stated the payments to three non-Indian companies were winding-up charges on terminated agency agreements and that no commission was paid to any Indian agent (testimony before the JPC, 1987–88).' This mirrors c065 (Dassault) for the Rafale control.
4. Either drop a:64 from this edge, or move the amount into d as 'alleged amount, not a flow into the case record'. Under the s→t money convention, an edge into a mechanism node should not carry an amount.
5. In the d field of force:ab-bofors, add the name under which the company appears in the 2005 judgment: 'Krtongen Kemi Och Forvaltning AB (the Bofors Company)'.
6. In the claim text, '(answered by Hinduja counsel; Delhi HC quashing)' should read '(answered by Hinduja counsel and by Bofors — winding-up charges; Delhi HC quashed/discharged 2005, not an acquittal after trial)'.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: the Supreme Court (bench headed by CJI Ranjan Gogoi) dismissed the CBI's SLP against the Delhi HC order of 31 May 2005, on 2 Nov 2018. Gogoi was CJI from 3 Oct 2018 to 17 Nov 2019, so the dates overlap. National Herald and The Tribune both give 2 Nov 2018. The CBI filed the SLP in early Feb 2018. From 31 May 2005 that is about 4,630 days. Take off the 90-day limitation period and you get about 4,540 days, which is consistent with the 4,522 days the Court gives.
verdicts.identityTest: The order is the one the source names. It is the CBI's SLP against the 2005 Delhi HC judgment that quashed charges against the Hinduja brothers and discharged the Bofors company (Srichand P. Hinduja v State through CBI, already in the record via Indian Kanoon doc 230231). It is a different matter from the advocate Ajay Agarwal appeal, which stayed pending and is claim c061. The actor is 'sc' (Supreme Court), which is correct.
verdicts.baseRate: This is a single court event, so a base rate does not apply. Symmetry against the SPEC control (Bofors beside Rafale) holds: the record states the SC dismissals in both cases the same way, as a court ruling with no implied wrongdoing. The claim also attributes no motive to the government that filed late (the delay ran across UPA-I, UPA-II and NDA) or to the one that filed in 2018 (NDA).
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable: this is a judicial ruling, not an accusation. No CBI statement disputing the order was found. The press coverage does not reproduce the CBI's grounds for the delay, so there is no CBI response to record (not asked).
verdicts.innocentReading: This was a dismissal on limitation, a procedural ruling. The Court did not decide the merits of the 2005 quashing and let the CBI argue its points in Agarwal's pending appeal. The record should not be read as the SC finding the accused innocent.
verdicts.reason: The source confirms the claim in every detail. National Herald (2 Nov 2018) quotes the bench headed by CJI Ranjan Gogoi: "We are not convinced with the grounds furnished by the petitioner in explaining the inordinate delay of 4522 days in filing this SLP (appeal)." It also says Ajay Agarwal's appeal against the same HC verdict was still pending. The Tribune separately confirms the date, the bench, that the dismissal was on delay, and the pending Agarwal appeal, but it does not give the 4,522 figure. So that number rests on one outlet, and 'reported' is the right tier. It would become 'documented' if the SC order (SLP (Crl) Diary no. of 2018) or a second outlet giving the 4,522 figure were added.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Add The Tribune (https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/supreme-court-dismisses-cbi-s-appeal-in-bofors-case-677727/) as a corroborating source for the date, bench, delay ground and pending Agarwal appeal. 2. In `d`, state that the dismissal was on limitation (delay not condoned), not on the merits, and that the CBI was allowed to argue in the Agarwal appeal. 3. Add an upgradeIf: upgrade to 'documented' once the SC record of proceedings dated 2 Nov 2018 is retrieved. 4. verdicts.dateTest: Restated: the Supreme Court (bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran) dismissed advocate Ajay K Agrawal's appeal against the Delhi High Court order of 31 May 2005 on Thursday, 6 Aug 2026. The bench is a sitting SC bench, so there is no tenure question. The DNA report is datelined 7 Aug 2026 and says the hearing was "Thursday". 6 Aug 2026 is a Thursday and 7 Aug is a Friday (checked with Python datetime), so taking the weekday as the date is correct. A separate search summary of contemporaneous coverage states it directly: "On Thursday (August 6), the Supreme Court dismissed the last surviving appeal". Republic's URL carries 2026-08-07, which is consistent. The claim is not stale either: the earlier CBI SLP dismissal (2 Nov 2018) is recorded separately as c060, and this is the later, distinct appeal. The date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: The entities match the source. The court is the Supreme Court of India. The appellant is advocate Ajay K Agrawal (DNA: "Advocate Ajay K. Agrawal"). The order challenged is the Delhi HC judgment of 31 May 2005 that quashed proceedings against Srichand, Gopichand and Prakash Hinduja and AB Bofors. That is the same order recorded in this file as the 2005 R S Sodhi J ruling, and the case node force:case-bofors is the right target. One minor naming fix: the judge is "K Vinod Chandran" (Republic and the search summary use that form), not "Vinod K Chandran". The quote "No question of adjournment. It is a 2018 matter." appears verbatim in DNA.
verdicts.baseRate: Not applicable in the discriminating sense. This is a single dated judicial event, not a property claimed to separate one entity from its peers, and it implies no wrongdoing by anyone. Symmetry control (Bofors beside Rafale): the same lens records Rafale's SC rulings, the 14 Dec 2018 dismissal and the 14 Nov 2019 dismissal of review petitions, as enforce/judicial-closure edges in the same way. So the claim does not favour either the UPA-era or the NDA-era case.
verdicts.denialFound: No denial is needed: the claim is a court dismissal and accuses no one. None found, and nobody was asked. Republic's coverage quotes no Hinduja, CBI, Congress or BJP response. The appellant's only recorded position is his request for four weeks to delete the names of deceased respondents, which the bench refused.
verdicts.innocentReading: The claim is itself the exculpatory record. The SC turned down a third-party advocate's appeal against a 2005 quashing that had been pending since 2018, after refusing an adjournment. That is routine docket closure of a stale petition in which the prosecuting agency's own appeal had already failed in 2018 on limitation (a 4,522-day delay). Nothing in it implies a merits finding of innocence or guilt beyond the 2005 quashing it leaves standing. The label should not be read as an acquittal after trial: some outlets, including Republic, call the 2005 order an "acquittal", but it was a quashing/discharge.
verdicts.reason: The DNA URL was opened through WebFetch; a direct curl attempt returned 403. The page supports every element of the claim: SC bench Pardiwala/Chandran, appellant advocate Ajay K Agrawal, the challenge to the 31 May 2005 Delhi HC order quashing proceedings against the Hinduja brothers and AB Bofors, dismissal after refusing an adjournment ("No question of adjournment. It is a 2018 matter."), and a hearing on "Thursday". The publication date is 7 Aug 2026. The weekday arithmetic is correct (6 Aug 2026 is a Thursday), and a search summary of contemporaneous coverage gives "Thursday (August 6)". Republic World separately confirms the bench, the appellant and the subject. No contrary reporting was found. The claim holds at its stated tier. It could be raised to documented by citing the second independent outlet (Republic World), or the SC order itself once it is located on the court's website.

Add a second source: ["Republic World — Supreme Court Closes Bofors Chapter, Rejects Final Plea Against Hinduja Brothers' Acquittal (7 Aug 2026)", "https://www.republicworld.com/india/supreme-court-closes-bofors-chapter-rejects-final-plea-against-hinduja-brothers-acquittal-2026-08-07-134188"]. verdicts.dateTest: Restated: Ministry of Defence (GoI) signed the IGA with France, plus the supply protocols and offset contracts with Dassault and MBDA, for 36 Rafale on 23 Sep 2016. Manohar Parrikar was Raksha Mantri from Nov 2014 to Mar 2017, so the dates overlap. The SC judgment of 14 Dec 2018 says: "The contract along with Aircraft Package Supply Protocol; Weapons Package Supply Protocol; Technical Arrangements and Offset contracts was signed in respect of 36 Rafale Jets on 23 rd September, 2016." It also says: "Two of the said contracts were signed with Dassault and M/s MBDA Missile Systems Limited on 23rd September, 2016, the same day on which the IGA was signed between the Government of India and the Government of France." The judgment also confirms the AoN of 29 Jun 2007, the joint statement of 10 Apr 2015, the RFP withdrawal begun in Mar 2015 and completed in Jun 2015, and CCS approval. The date passes. Parrikar's name does not appear in either cited source. The fact is true but needs its own source.
verdicts.identityTest: The parties are correct, with one caveat. The IGA itself is government to government (GoI and French Republic), not MoD and Dassault. The award edge MoD→Dassault is right for the Aircraft Package Supply Protocol and the Dassault offset contract. MBDA is a separate offset counterparty for the weapons package, and the edge leaves it out. The text "36 Rafale IGA ... signed" on an edge to Dassault blurs the line between the IGA and the industrial contracts.
verdicts.baseRate: The SC records that IGAs, FMS and similar routes make up "nearly 40%" of Rs 7.45 lakh crore procured under DPP since 2002. So the IGA route is common but does not cover most procurement. Keeping the price out of public view is normal for IGA/FMS buys. The government gave Parliament only the basic aircraft price and showed the full pricing to CAG; CAG Report 3 of 2019 tabled it in redacted or relative form. Control: the Bofors contract value (about Rs 1,437 crore, 1986) was public. Price opacity is a real difference from Bofors, but it is a feature of the procurement route, not evidence of wrongdoing. The claim makes no accusation, so the symmetry test is not strained.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable as a denial, because this is a neutral award fact. Dassault's own statement of 10 Oct 2018 (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2018/10/10/1619657/0/en/Rafale-contract-for-India-clarifications-by-Dassault-Aviation.html) gives no value at all. It says only: "Dassault Aviation has committed to offsets in India worth 50% of the value of the purchase." The government's position, recorded in the SC judgment, is that pricing is withheld under the IGA's confidentiality terms and for national-security reasons, and was shared with CAG.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is an ordinary record that a contract was signed. The value is one widely reported figure (about EUR 7.87 bn, roughly Rs 59,000 crore). Under the IGA's confidentiality clause the official price was given only to CAG and to the Court in sealed cover. That is standard for government-to-government arms purchases and implies nothing improper.
verdicts.reason: The signing date, the parties and the contract structure are documented in a primary court record (SC, 14 Dec 2018), so that part survives. The value attribution does not. The claim says "Rs 59,000 crore per Dassault", but Dassault's 10 Oct 2018 statement, read from the primary release, contains no rupee or euro figure. It says only "offsets in India worth 50% of the value of the purchase". "(Rs 59,000 crore)" is ThePrint's own gloss. BusinessToday's report of the same statement gives EUR 3.9 bn as the offset value instead. As written, the amount is pinned to a party that never stated it, which is a source-chain failure. "Price redacted in the CAG report" is also unsourced: the SC passage cited is the much-criticised paragraph written before CAG Report 3 of 2019 was tabled in Feb 2019. Parrikar's role is also absent from the cited sources. Once corrected, the signing fact is tier "documented". The value can only carry "reported", attributed to the media.
verdicts.corrections: text: replace "(value Rs 59,000 crore per Dassault; price redacted officially)" with "(value widely reported as about EUR 7.87 bn / Rs 59,000 crore; official price not published, disclosed to CAG and to SC in sealed cover)". d: delete "Dassault's statement of 10 Oct 2018 calls it a 'Rs 59,000 crore' contract". Replace with: "Dassault's 10 Oct 2018 statement gives offsets as '50% of the value of the purchase' with no figure; Rs 59,000 crore is ThePrint's gloss." a: keep 59000 only with a flag that the value is media-reported, or set it to null. tier: documented for the signing and parties (SC judgment); the value sub-field is reported. srcs: add the Dassault primary release (globenewswire 10 Oct 2018 or dassault-aviation.com PR_Dassault-Aviation_Rafale-India_DRAL.pdf). Add CAG Report No. 3 of 2019 (Capital Acquisition in IAF) for the redaction statement. Add a PIB/MoD release or a credible report for the Parrikar–Le Drian signing. Note MBDA as the second offset counterparty, and note that the IGA is GoI–Government of France. ThePrint returned 403 to direct fetch; its wording was checked through a fetch summary and search snippets.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as written: petitioners (WP(Crl) 225, 297 and 298 of 2018) and the Congress allege that MoD's 23 Sep 2016 IGA for 36 Rafales (Parrikar as Defence Minister) was priced worse than the 126-MMRCA negotiation, and that the Government of India picked Reliance as Dassault's offset partner. The contract date of 23 Sep 2016 falls inside the NDA window, so the dates line up. One defect: the record has `from` = 2018-09-21, the Mediapart/Hollande date. That date only fits the offset-partner limb. The price limb is older. Wikipedia records Randeep Surjewala (Nov 2017) asking whether the per-aircraft cost had gone from Rs 526.1 crore to Rs 1,570 crore. The record's own contra c066, Reliance Defence's denial of 12 Aug 2018, also comes before the claim's `from` date. The SC judgment places the petitions after the Hollande report: 'This seems to have triggered of the writ petitions under consideration.' It also records that WP 298/2018 (Sinha, Shourie, Bhushan) followed a CBI complaint of 4 Oct 2018 and was filed before the 31 Oct 2018 hearing. The exact date '24 Oct 2018' does not appear in any of the three cited sources.
verdicts.identityTest: The entities hold up. s=min:ministry-of-defence is the contracting party to the IGA (SC para 16 onward). t=force:dassault-aviation is the OEM. The SC names 'Reliance Defence' as the offset partner the petitioners objected to ('how a novice company i.e. Reliance Defence came to replace the HAL as the Offset partner'). Dassault's 10 Oct 2018 statement names the 'Reliance Group' and the JV Dassault Reliance Aerospace Ltd. So mapping the benefit to energy:reliance-adag (the Anil Ambani group) is consistent with the sources. The record correctly treats the benefit as alleged, with amountCr null.
verdicts.baseRate: Under DPP 2013 offset guidelines clause 4.3 ('The OEM/vendor/Tier-I sub-vendor will be free to select the Indian offset partner'), the OEM picks the Indian offset partner in every offset contract. 'Vendor picked a private IOP' therefore does not single this deal out. What does single it out is the named allegation from a former head of the counterparty state that the buyer government proposed the partner, which is why the claim stays alleged rather than analytic. On price, the SPEC symmetry control (Bofors beside Rafale) is present in the file (force:case-bofors, c06x). Like Bofors, Rafale has an alleged limb, an audit record and a court ruling, so the same lens is applied to both. No ≥80% non-discrimination problem arises, because the claim asserts an allegation and not a pattern.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it is already in the file as contra edges. MoD, 22 Sep 2018 (The Quint, https://www.thequint.com/news/india/rafale-deal-indian-govt-chose-ambani-reliance-french-president-hollande): 'Government of India has no role in the selection of Indian Offset partner which is a commercial decision of the Original Equipment Manufacturer.' Dassault, 10 Oct 2018 (ThePrint): 'freely chosen' Reliance Group. Reliance Defence, 12 Aug 2018 (Business Today): it denied receiving any contract from MoD. Anil Ambani wrote to Rahul Gandhi that the government had no role (per The Quint). On price: SC, 14 Dec 2018 (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/95183857/): 'no occasion to really doubt the process' and 'no substantial material on record to show that this is a case of commercial favouritism'. CAG Report 3 of 2019 Vol II para 2.2 found the contract 2.86% below the Audit Aligned Price. The file has that as the cag→force:case-rafale edge, but not as a contra on c063. Hollande's own later hedge (Wikipedia: he 'said that he was unaware' whether Dassault was pressured and that the French government did not choose Reliance) is also left out of c063's `d`.
verdicts.innocentReading: Dassault had an MoU with Reliance going back to 2012 (the SC notes Reliance–Dassault contacts 'starting from the year 2012'). The offset guidelines leave the choice of Indian offset partner to the OEM. The 36-aircraft fly-away IGA dropped the 108 aircraft to be licence-built at HAL, so HAL's role ended for structural reasons. The price difference follows from changes in scope (India Specific Enhancements, weapons package, escalation and exchange-rate movement over 2007–2016). On a like-for-like basis, CAG found the 2016 contract 2.86% below the aligned 2007 bid. Hollande's quote may reflect what the French side understood about Indian preferences, not a direction from MoD, and he later said he did not know whether pressure had been applied.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives as `alleged`. Each limb is asserted by named parties, and the cited primary record bears this out. The SC judgment records the petitioners' challenge to 'the alteration of pricing' and to Reliance Defence replacing HAL as offset partner. It also records the Hollande report as the trigger: 'the Reliance Group was the name suggested by the Government of India. This seems to have triggered of the writ petitions'. The Quint confirms the Mediapart quote ('The Indian government proposed this service group… We did not have a choice'), the reaffirmation by Hollande's office on 22 Sep 2018, and the MoD denial. Contras from MoD, Dassault and Reliance sit in the same file, which meets the CONTRACT rule for alleged claims. Upgrading to documented is not possible, because the SC dismissed the petitions and CAG found the price lower. Killing the claim is not justified either: the allegation is real, made by named parties, and the subject of a court record. The defects are in the fields, not the claim: a wrong `from` date for the price limb, an unsourced petition date, and an incomplete contra set.
verdicts.corrections: 1) `from`: change 2018-09-21 to the earliest dated price allegation, Congress/Surjewala in Nov 2017 per Wikipedia (or split the claim into a price limb from 2017-11 and an offset-partner limb from 2018-09-21). As it stands, contra c066 (12 Aug 2018) comes before the claim it answers. 2) `d`: '24 Oct 2018 petition' is not in any cited source. Either cite a dated news report or write 'WP(Crl) 298/2018, filed before 31 Oct 2018 after a CBI complaint of 4 Oct 2018' (SC text). 3) Add a contra edge cag→claim:money-people:c063 for the price limb: CAG Report 3 of 2019 Vol II para 2.2, 2.86% below the Audit Aligned Price, with the caveat already in the file that the base aircraft price shows no difference. Also add the SC 14 Dec 2018 finding as answering both limbs. The label '(answered by MoD, Dassault, Reliance Defence)' covers only the offset-partner limb. 4) `d`: after 'Hollande's office reaffirmed it on 22 Sep 2018', add Hollande's later hedge that he was unaware whether Dassault was pressured and that the French government did not choose Reliance (Wikipedia). 5) Optional: the SC also records petitioner Sanjay Singh, MP (WP 297/2018), as alleging 'alteration of pricing'. Cite this as the primary-record anchor for the price limb instead of leaving it to 'the Congress' without a source.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Dassault Aviation formed DRAL with the Reliance group, created 10 Feb 2017. ThePrint (11 Oct 2018) quotes Dassault's statement of 10 Oct 2018: "This joint venture, Dassault Reliance Aerospace Ltd (DRAL), was created February 10, 2017". MCA-derived registries give CIN U35999MH2017PLC291083 with incorporation on 10 Feb 2017. The joint statement in Wikipedia dated 3 Oct 2016 is an announcement before incorporation, so it does not conflict. The date holds. But `to: null` with no % hides a dated change in shareholding. Dassault held 49% from incorporation until the RAL-to-Dassault transfer of 2% (Rs 175.96 cr), due to complete by 1 Nov 2025. After that it holds 51% and DRAL becomes a Dassault subsidiary (Business Today / Business Standard, 5 Sep 2025, citing the Reliance Infra exchange filing).
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is the one the sources name. Dassault Reliance Aerospace Limited, CIN U35999MH2017PLC291083, registered in Maharashtra (Nagpur facility). Source s is Dassault Aviation SA. The Indian co-owner is Reliance Aerostructure Ltd, a Reliance Infrastructure subsidiary, not "Reliance Group" in general and not Reliance Industries. The file has no edge for the Reliance side.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating, and not meant to be. Foreign OEMs routinely form Indian JVs with private partners to discharge offset obligations (Tata-Lockheed, Tata-Airbus, Adani-Elbit, Mahindra-Airbus/Thales, Kalyani-Rafael). Taken alone, a 49% foreign stake in an offset JV is the normal structure under the then-49% automatic-route FDI cap. The edge is a plain ownership fact and carries no inference.
verdicts.denialFound: Nobody disputes the fact itself. On the related question of choosing a partner, Dassault (10 Oct 2018, ThePrint) said it "has freely chosen to make a partnership with India's Reliance Group". Reliance Defence (12 Aug 2018, Business Today) called the allegations "absolutely unfounded" and said the Ministry had no role. Both are already in the file as separate claims.
verdicts.innocentReading: Under its offset obligation (50% of the contract value), Dassault set up a minority-held JV with an Indian private firm. That was the standard FDI-compliant structure at the time. In 2025 it moved to majority control so it could give warranties and service guarantees for Falcon parts built in Nagpur. The ownership fact alone implies no favour.
verdicts.reason: Both sources say what the claim says, and both the date and the entity check out. The fact stands. The edge breaks the contract in two ways, though. First, the `own` predicate requires a % in `d`. Second, the stated reason for leaving it out ("split is not verified from a primary record") is wrong. Reliance Infra's Sep 2025 exchange filing, as reported by Business Today and Business Standard, gives Dassault 49% with RAL holding 51% until the 2% transfer (completion by 1 Nov 2025), and Dassault 51% after it. The Wikipedia line "51:49" does not say who holds which side, and readers could take Dassault as the majority holder from 2017, which would be wrong. The incorporation date is backed by Dassault's own statement plus MCA registry data. With the exchange filing added, the tier can go up to documented.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Split the edge by date. Edge A: dassault-aviation own dral, from 2017-02-10 to 2025-11-01 (completion date per filing; confirm actual), d: "49% (RAL 51%) per Reliance Infrastructure exchange filing, Sep 2025". Edge B: from 2025-11-01, to null, d: "51% after purchase of 2% from Reliance Aerostructure Ltd for Rs 175.96 cr; DRAL becomes a Dassault subsidiary". 2) Remove "the split is not verified from a primary record and no percentage is asserted here". Replace "Wikipedia gives ... 51:49 split" with "joint statement of 3 Oct 2016 announced the JV (Wikipedia)". 3) Add CIN U35999MH2017PLC291083 to node force:dral. 4) Add sources: https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/dassault-aviation-to-take-majority-control-of-dassault-reliance-aerospace-with-51-stake-check-details-492808-2025-09-05 ; https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/dassault-aviation-to-raise-stake-in-dassault-reliance-aerospace-to-51-125090500894_1.html ; https://www.zaubacorp.com/company/DASSAULT-RELIANCE-AEROSPACE-LIMITED/U35999MH2017PLC291083 (MCA mirror; mca.gov.in is blocked). Where possible, use the Reliance Infra BSE/NSE filing itself as the primary record. 5) Add the matching edge for the Reliance side: Reliance Aerostructure Ltd (Reliance Infrastructure) own dral, 51% from 2017-02-10, 49% from Nov 2025. 6) Tier: documented once the exchange filing or a second outlet is attached; it stays reported if only ThePrint is kept.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as a sentence: Ministry of Defence awarded AgustaWestland a contract for 12 AW101 VVIP helicopters on 8 Feb 2010, and terminated it on 1 Jan 2014. The awarder is an institution with no tenure window, so the date test passes trivially. The note in `d` says the signing fell inside A K Antony's tenure as Defence Minister (26 Oct 2006 to 26 May 2014). That is correct: Feb 2010 and Jan 2014 both fall inside it. The record has a date error: `to` is null even though both the label and `d` say the contract was cancelled in Jan 2014.
verdicts.identityTest: Passes, with one refinement. The legal counterparty was AgustaWestland International Ltd (AWIL, UK), a Finmeccanica (now Leonardo) subsidiary. Business Standard, quoting the MoD's 1 Jan 2014 statement: the government "terminated the agreement signed with AgustaWestland International Ltd on 8 February 2010 for the supply of 12 VVIP/VIP helicopters on grounds of breach of the Pre-contract Integrity Pact". The entity label "AgustaWestland (Finmeccanica group, UK/Italy)" names the right corporate group, but it should say AWIL. Indian identifiers (CIN etc.) are null, which is correct for a foreign company.
verdicts.baseRate: Does not apply in a discriminating sense. The edge records a contract award, a property that every foreign vendor with an MoD contract shares, and it makes no allegation. It points no wrongdoing at anyone, so there is no conjunction to test. The SPEC control (AgustaWestland beside Tatra/BEML, Bofors beside Rafale) should be run on the case node `force:case-agustawestland`, not on this edge.
verdicts.denialFound: Nobody disputes the award or the termination. The disputed facts, all on the bribery side and not in this edge, are these. AgustaWestland/Finmeccanica denied wrongdoing. On 8 Jan 2018 the Milan Court of Appeals acquitted former Finmeccanica CEO Giuseppe Orsi and former AgustaWestland CEO Bruno Spagnolini of corruption (Reuters, cited on the Wikipedia page). The Busto Arsizio court acquitted ex-IAF chief S P Tyagi in Oct 2014. AgustaWestland is reported to have kept EUR 106 million for the 3 helicopters it delivered (NDTV, 29 Apr 2016). None of this contradicts the claim.
verdicts.innocentReading: The edge is a neutral procurement fact: the MoD bought 12 VVIP helicopters from AWIL for the IAF Communication Squadron in Feb 2010 and terminated the contract on 1 Jan 2014 for breach of the integrity pact. On its own it implies no corruption by any person.
verdicts.reason: I checked the single cited source, the Wikipedia article (raw text). It says: "The Indian Ministry of Defence (MoD) signed a contract to purchase 12 AgustaWestland AW101 helicopters in February 2010" and "India cancelled the Rs 3,600 crore deal with AgustaWestland in January 2014... on grounds of breach of the Pre-contract Integrity Pact". The MoD's own termination statement of 1 Jan 2014, as quoted by Business Standard, gives the exact signing date (8 Feb 2010) and names AWIL. The contract value is EUR 556 million (about Rs 3,600 crore). The actor, object, count and dates all hold, and the edge claims no wrongdoing. The one problem is the sourcing. Wikipedia is a tertiary source, not "one credible outlet with named sourcing", so "reported" rests on the citations behind it. If Business Standard (or Economic Times) and the PIB/MoD release of 1 Jan 2014 are added to `srcs`, the edge qualifies as `documented` (primary record plus two independent outlets). I could not retrieve the PIB release URL directly, so I am keeping it at `reported` until it is added.
verdicts.corrections:
1. Set `to` to "2014-01-01" (the contract was terminated on 1 Jan 2014). It is currently null.
2. Make `from` precise: "2010-02-08".
3. In `lab`/`d`, name the counterparty as AgustaWestland International Ltd (AWIL), a Finmeccanica (now Leonardo) subsidiary.
4. Replace "contract value not verified" with: EUR 556.262 million (about Rs 3,600 crore). About 45% (about Rs 1,620 crore) was paid and 3 helicopters were delivered.
5. Add to `srcs`: Business Standard "Govt scraps AgustaWestland chopper deal" (https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/govt-scraps-agustawestland-chopper-deal-114010100555_1.html) and the MoD/PIB release of 1 Jan 2014. Once the PIB release is attached, upgrade to `documented`.
6. Make sure the Antony-tenure note in `d` stays a neutral statement of when the contract was signed and does not imply who signed it. The signatory was the MoD acquisition wing, not the minister personally.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: AgustaWestland allegedly paid bribes to intermediaries and Indian officials to win the AW101 VVIP contract and get the specifications changed. Wikipedia says the payments were made "in 2006 and 2007", and the contract was signed Feb 2010 under Defence Minister Antony (in office 2006-10-26 to 2014-05-26). The former Air Chief served 2004-12-31 to 2007-03-31, so the 2006-07 payment window overlaps his tenure. The specification change is the disputed point: his side says it came from the 2003 ASQR or PMO/NSA Brajesh Mishra advice before his tenure, while the CBI dates it to his tenure. The other dates check out: the allegation became public 12 Feb 2013 (Orsi arrested, Reuters cited), the CBI preliminary enquiry was 25 Feb 2013, the FIR 13 Mar 2013 and the chargesheet Sep 2017. Every date the record states holds.
verdicts.identityTest: The parties and their roles hold: AgustaWestland and its parent Finmeccanica (Orsi was CEO), the former Air Chief S. P. Tyagi, who is named in the FIR and chargesheet, and the middlemen Michel and Haschke. The target node fails. The edge runs force:agustawestland -> min:ministry-of-defence with pred "direct", and "direct" is in MONEY_PREDS ("payment recorded", money flowing s->t). So the graph shows AgustaWestland paying the Ministry of Defence. No source says that. The alleged recipients are middlemen (Michel, Haschke, Gerosa), the IDS Infotech/Aeromatrix channels, Tyagi relatives, and unnamed officials and politicians. The Ministry was the buyer. It froze the contract (Feb 2013), cancelled it for breach of the integrity pact (Jan 2014) and encashed AgustaWestland's bank guarantee. Its own minister said on 25 Mar 2013 that "bribes have been taken". The ministry is the injured party, not the payee.
verdicts.baseRate: Base rate does not apply to the bribery itself. This is a case record, not a pattern inferred from comparison. Symmetry holds: the file runs AgustaWestland (UPA) beside Tatra/BEML, and Bofors beside Rafale, with identical fields, as the SPEC requires. The record says 0 of 7 cases ended in a final conviction. Symmetry note the record could add: the NSA whose advice Tyagi cites (Brajesh Mishra) served under the NDA government, while the contract was signed under UPA-II.
verdicts.denialFound: The record holds a contra, money-people:c072. The Milan retrial court acquitted Orsi and Spagnolini on 8 Jan 2018 for "insufficient proof that any bribery took place", and Cassation upheld that in 2019. Wikipedia (Tyagi article) quotes it. Found but not in the record: (1) The former Air Chief's own denial. He says the specification change, especially the lower service ceiling, came from PMO/Brajesh Mishra advice: https://www.ajaishukla.com/2013/02/brajesh-mishra-loosened-norms-that-let.html. Wikipedia also says the Busto Arsizio court (Oct 2014) found no corruption by him. (2) Michel's interview denial that he ever met any "Gandhi" (cited in the Wikipedia scandal article). (3) The Brescia appeals court acquitted Haschke on 30 Jun 2025: https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/italy-court-acquits-consultant-india-helicopter-case-2025-07-01/. Weighing against these: Antony's 25 Mar 2013 statement that "corruption has taken place... bribes have been taken", and the 2014 cancellation for breach of the integrity pact.
verdicts.innocentReading: The specification change may have been a legitimate decision to widen the vendor field. The 6,000 m ceiling allowed only Eurocopter EC-225 to qualify, and the 2003 ASQR and PMO/SPG input brought it down to 4,500 m. The payments to IDS Infotech and Aeromatrix may have been for real engineering subcontracts. That is the defence's reading, and the Italian retrial and Cassation accepted it for lack of proof that bribery took place. Indian courts have not framed charges (as of Dec 2025), so no court has found any payment to be a bribe.
verdicts.reason: The wording and the sources hold up. Wikipedia confirms the arrest of the Finmeccanica chief on 12 Feb 2013, the CBI FIR of 13 Mar 2013 naming the former Air Chief, his relatives and four companies, the Sep 2017 chargesheet against him "and nine others", and the claim that the specifications were changed on the NSA's orders before his tenure. "Alleged" is the correct tier: these are agency allegations not yet tried, and the contra c072 is in the file. The edge as encoded is still wrong. "direct" is a money predicate (s->t "payment recorded"), so the graph shows AgustaWestland paying the Ministry of Defence. No source alleges that. The Ministry was the buyer, cancelled the contract and encashed the guarantee. Its own minister said bribes had been taken. The edge should be re-targeted, not killed. The contra set is also thin: only the Italian acquittals are recorded, without the accused's own denial and the Haschke acquittal.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change t from min:ministry-of-defence to force:case-agustawestland. This keeps it a statement about the case without inventing a payee. If you keep a money predicate, name the alleged recipients only at public rank, i.e. per:sp-tyagi, and do not name his relatives. Do not use pred "direct" with the Ministry as payee. Use pred "analytic" or a case-level alleged edge, or put the CBI allegation on a force:cbi -> per:sp-tyagi enforce edge (c073 already exists). 2) In d, add that Wikipedia dates the alleged payments to 2006-2007, inside the former Chief's tenure (to 2007-03-31), while the contract came in 2010. 3) Reword the specification sentence. The specification history is contested. The ceiling was cut from 6,000 m to 4,500 m in the 2003 ASQR/PMO-NSA (Brajesh Mishra) era, which is his side's account. The CBI places the change in 2005, during his tenure. The Tyagi Wikipedia article itself calls the bribery testimony "unverified". 4) Add contras: the former Chief's denial (ajaishukla.com, Feb 2013), the Busto Arsizio Oct 2014 finding of no corruption by him (Wikipedia, citing India Today 24 Jun 2015), and the Haschke acquittal of 30 Jun 2025 (Reuters). 5) Add the counter-record that the Ministry itself (Antony, 25 Mar 2013) said bribes were taken and cancelled the contract in Jan 2014 for breach of the integrity pact. With that added, "answered by the Italian acquittals" no longer reads as the whole answer. 6) Keep from=2013-02-12 as the first-allegation date. Optionally note that the Italian investigation began in late 2011.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated: "the Milan Court of Appeal (3rd section, the retrial bench) acquitted Giuseppe Orsi and Bruno Spagnolini of international corruption on 8 Jan 2018; Italy's Corte di Cassazione made the acquittal final on 22 May 2019." The sequence holds. Busto Arsizio trial court, Oct 2014: cleared of corruption, convicted of false invoicing. Milan appeal, Apr 2016: convicted. Cassation, 16 Dec 2016: annulled the conviction and sent the case back to Milan for retrial. Milan retrial, 8 Jan 2018: acquitted. Cassation, 22 May 2019: acquittal final. The 2019 ruling comes after the 2018 retrial and after c071's "from" date of 2013-02-12, so there is no chronology conflict. One caveat in the d field: Wikipedia gives 8 Apr 2016 for the appeal conviction, but some wire reports date it 7 Apr 2016. Cite it as "Apr 2016" unless a primary source settles the day. The edge's from date of 2018-01-08 is correct.
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is the Italian judiciary (Milan Court of Appeal and Corte di Cassazione), which matches the source. The defendants are Giuseppe Orsi (former CEO of Finmeccanica/Leonardo, and earlier of AgustaWestland) and Bruno Spagnolini (former CEO of AgustaWestland). The d field calls Orsi "the former CEO", which is ambiguous; it should name both men and their companies. Scope matters for the 'contra' edge to c071. The Italian acquittal covers only the two Italian executives on the international-corruption charge. It does not cover the Indian accused (S. P. Tyagi, the Tyagi cousins, Michel, Khaitan), whose CBI/ED cases in India are still pending. Haschke was acquitted separately by the Brescia appeals court on 30 Jun 2025, per Reuters as cited on Wikipedia. So the edge contradicts the allegation in Italian courts but does not settle it in India.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating, and it does not need to be: this is a record of a court outcome, not a pattern inference. The symmetry control in SPEC is Bofors beside Rafale, and Bofors had a parallel outcome: the Delhi HC quashed the charges against the Hindujas in 2005 and the case was later closed. Recording a foreign or domestic acquittal as a 'contra' edge should be applied the same way to every case in force:case-*. Applied that way, the claim is consistent.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable in the usual sense: the claim is itself the exculpatory record for the accused. No statement from Italian prosecutors contesting the 2019 finality was found. Wikipedia says the Milan General Prosecutor's appeal went ahead without the Attorney General's support. The Indian government and CBI kept prosecuting in India after the acquittal. Not asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is the innocent reading of c071. Italian courts, after a full retrial, found the prosecution's evidence of bribery insufficient, and the highest court made that final. It is a judicial finding of insufficient proof against the two Italian executives, not a finding that no payments to intermediaries occurred and not a ruling on the Indian accused.
verdicts.reason: The source says what the claim says. Wikipedia's "2013 Indian helicopter bribery scandal" page: "on 8 January 2018, the Milan Third Court of Appeals finally cleared the defendants and dismissed all charges, on grounds of insufficient evidence ... The verdict was upheld by the Supreme Court of Cassazione on 22 May 2019." The underlying reports are independent. Defense News, 22 May 2019 (Tom Kington): "A former CEO of Italy's Leonardo and a former fellow manager were given a final and definitive acquittal by Italy's highest court on Wednesday in a bribery case dating back to the sale of helicopters to India in 2010." Reuters (9 Jan 2018) and The Wire/Scroll/Quint also report the 2018 acquittal. Dates, actors and outcome all match. The cited S. P. Tyagi Wikipedia URL is a redirect to "Shashindra Pal Tyagi". That page confirms the Jan 2018 acquittal of Orsi and Spagnolini but says nothing about Cassation in 2019. The claim survives. The tier is right for the sources as cited, which are Wikipedia only. With Reuters 2018 and Defense News 2019 cited directly as two independent credible outlets, it qualifies for documented.
verdicts.corrections: 1) srcs: replace or add the primary outlets. Defense News 22 May 2019, https://www.defensenews.com/industry/2019/05/22/former-leonardo-ceo-gets-final-acquittal-in-helicopter-kickback-case/ ; Reuters 9 Jan 2018 (archived), https://web.archive.org/web/20200906183548/https://in.reuters.com/article/leonardo-india-corruption-trial/italian-court-clears-former-leonardo-bosses-in-india-corruption-case-idINKBN1EX159 ; The Wire, https://thewire.in/211852/italy-court-acquits-former-agustawestland-finmeccanica-top-managers-in-corruption-case/ . With these, upgrade the tier to documented. 2) Change the Tyagi URL to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashindra_Pal_Tyagi (redirect target), or drop it, since it does not support the 2019 Cassation part. 3) lab/d: name the defendants: "acquitted Giuseppe Orsi (ex-CEO Finmeccanica/Leonardo) and Bruno Spagnolini (ex-CEO AgustaWestland)". Replace "the former CEO sentenced to four years on 8 Apr 2016" with "Apr 2016 Milan appeal conviction (Orsi 4 yrs per Wikipedia; Spagnolini also sentenced)". 4) Add a scope note to d: "Italian acquittal does not bind the Indian CBI/ED proceedings against Indian accused, which remain pending; Haschke separately acquitted by Brescia appeals court 30 Jun 2025." 5) Fill the claim text's "upheld by Cassation 2019" with the exact date, 22 May 2019.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated: CBI registered an FIR on 13 Mar 2013, arrested S. P. Tyagi on 9 Dec 2016 and chargesheeted him on 1 Sep 2017. Tyagi was Chief of the Air Staff from 31 Dec 2004 to 31 Mar 2007. The enforcement steps come after his tenure, which is expected because the claim records what CBI did, not something done in office. The alleged conduct (changing specifications to favour AgustaWestland) is said to have happened during his tenure, and the contract was signed in Feb 2010. Nothing in the chronology contradicts the claim. Each date matches its source. The 2013 scandal article on Wikipedia says: "registered an FIR on 13 March 2013" and "On 9 December 2016, the CBI arrested former Indian Air Force Chief S. P. Tyagi ... In September 2017, the CBI filed a formal chargesheet against S. P. Tyagi and nine others." Deccan Chronicle/PTI gives the exact day: "Former Indian Air Force (IAF) Chief SP Tyagi was on Friday [1 Sep 2017] chargesheeted by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in a Delhi Court along with nine others."
verdicts.identityTest: This is the right person. Shashindra Pal Tyagi was the 20th Chief of the Air Staff (31 Dec 2004 to 31 Mar 2007, succeeded by F. H. Major), and both Wikipedia pages and the news reports identify him that way. The source URL https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._P._Tyagi redirects to Shashindra_Pal_Tyagi, and the content is consistent. Small problem inside the sources: the scandal article says the FIR named "his three brothers: Juli, Docsa and Sandeep", but the Tyagi page and the news reports call Sanjeev 'Julie' Tyagi a cousin. The edge itself does not depend on this.
verdicts.baseRate: This is an enforcement-stage record, not an inference drawn from a shared property, so a base-rate test does not discriminate here. Context: Deccan Chronicle/PTI reports that Tyagi is the first IAF chief to be chargesheeted by CBI, so this does not apply to most service chiefs. Symmetry also holds. The probe was ordered by A. K. Antony (UPA defence minister) on 13 Feb 2013 and the FIR was registered under UPA-II. The arrest and chargesheet came under the NDA. The specification change is attributed to Brajesh Mishra, NSA under NDA-I. Neither political side is singled out.
verdicts.denialFound: Reported: "He has denied the charge." (Weekend Leader/IANS, https://www.theweekendleader.com/Headlines/8693/former-iaf-chief-tyagi-gets-bail-in-agustawestland-case.html). On the chargesheet, Deccan Chronicle/PTI wrote: "Efforts to seek reaction from Tyagi did not fructify as he neither took a call, nor responded to messages" (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/010917/agustawestland-case-cbi-files-chargesheet-against-ex-iaf-chief-sp-tyagi.html). So he was asked and did not reply. Wikipedia also records his side's argument that the specifications were changed before his tenure on the NSA's orders. Separately, the Italian courts acquitted the AgustaWestland executives in 2018 and Cassation upheld that in 2019; c072 already records this.
verdicts.innocentReading: A chargesheet is CBI's own position: the agency believes there is a prima facie case. It is not a judicial finding. The innocent reading is that CBI chargesheeted a retired chief on evidence that may not hold up at trial. The main foreign case collapsed in Italy for insufficient proof, and the specification change is documented as a decision taken by several agencies, including the PMO and SPG. The claim already says "no finding of guilt", and that is the correct framing.
verdicts.reason: Every element checks out. The cited Wikipedia scandal article states the FIR date (13 Mar 2013), the arrest (9 Dec 2016) and the chargesheet against Tyagi and nine others (Sep 2017). Deccan Chronicle/PTI independently confirms the chargesheet date of 1 Sep 2017 and "along with nine others". The subject is a former service chief, which is a public rank. The claim states the stage and says there is no finding of guilt. It is not a conjunction of separate facts implying wrongdoing: it is a straight chronology of enforcement steps. The tier stays "reported" for now. The only cited sources are Wikipedia, which is a tertiary source and carries a BLP-sources tag on the Tyagi page. Independent coverage (PTI/Deccan Chronicle, Tribune, Scroll, HT) or a CBI press release would support "documented" once it is added to srcs.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Make the chargesheet date exact: "chargesheet 1 Sep 2017". 2) In d, replace "trial status and bail of the former Chief not verified" with: "granted bail by the Patiala House court on 26 Dec 2016 (bond Rs 2 lakh, not to leave Delhi-NCR) — Scroll https://scroll.in/latest/825144/agustawestland-scam-court-grants-bail-to-former-air-force-chief-sp-tyagi". Trial status remains unverified. 3) Add to srcs: Deccan Chronicle/PTI 1 Sep 2017 (URL above) for the chargesheet; Tribune https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/nation/cbi-arrests-ex-iaf-chief-tyagi-2-others-334871 for the arrest. Once these are added, the tier can be raised to documented, because there would then be two independent outlets. 4) Add the response to d: "He has denied the charge (IANS, Dec 2016); did not respond to PTI on the chargesheet." 5) Fix the relative wording: use "relatives" or "cousin (Sanjeev 'Julie' Tyagi)", not "brothers", where c071 or the FIR description says so. 6) Shorten the claim text to "CBI FIR 13 Mar 2013; arrest 9 Dec 2016; chargesheet 1 Sep 2017" so it matches lab.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim is: the courts (SC, Delhi HC, Special CBI court at Rouse Avenue) ruled in the case against Christian Michel James, who was extradited in Dec 2018, on four dates, and every date falls inside the case window. 1) Extradition 2018-12-04: Gulf News (18 Feb 2025) says he was "arrested on December 4, 2018, following his apprehension in Dubai". Wikipedia says "On 5 December 2018, Christian Michel... was extradited to India from Dubai". He landed in Delhi late on 4 Dec, so the one-day difference is an artefact of timing and does not refute the claim. 2) SC bail 2025-02-18: Gulf News dated 18 Feb 2025 quotes the bench: "We are inclined to grant bail on conditions as may be determined by the trial Court." 3) Delhi HC bail 2025-03-04 (ED/PMLA case, Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma): confirmed by ANI (aninews.in ...20250304185321) and Business Standard (125030400950). Search summaries also say "the high court on March 4 had directed him to furnish a personal bond and surety of Rs 5 lakh each". 4) Charges not framed as of 2025-12-23: LawBeat (dated 24 Dec 2025) quotes Special CBI Judge Sanjay Jindal: "Despite expiry of more than seven years after the arrest of the accused Christian Michel James, the proceedings are at initial stage and charges are yet to be decided." The sequence is consistent. 'from' 2018-12-04 is acceptable.
verdicts.identityTest: The 'alleged middleman, a British national' is Christian Michel James in every source (Gulf News, LawBeat, Wikipedia, ANI, Business Standard). The case is the 12 AW101 VVIP helicopter contract (Rs 3,600 cr). There is a split between the CBI case (SC bail; the Rouse Avenue CBI court order of 23 Dec 2025) and the ED case (HC bail, 4 Mar 2025), and the record's 'd' field draws it correctly. Edge-node problem: s = force:delhi-district-courts, but two of the four rulings are by the Supreme Court and the Delhi High Court, not district courts. Under the contract, 'enforce' (agency→subject: cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction) also fits poorly for bail grants, which are judicial relief rather than enforcement. These are field-level mismatches, not identity errors about the person or the case. He is a named accused in a nationally reported prosecution and the public subject of SC/HC orders, so he is not a 'person below the public rank'.
verdicts.baseRate: This is a procedural fact, not a discriminating property. Long pre-charge custody and delays in framing charges are common in Indian CBI/ED cases. The SC itself said the trial "may not be completed in the next 25 years at this pace", and multi-year undertrial status is the norm, not the exception. The claim implies nothing beyond the case stage, so a base rate cannot refute it. Symmetry: SPEC requires AgustaWestland beside Tatra/BEML and Bofors beside Rafale with identical fields ('latest stage'). This edge fills the 'latest stage' field for the UPA-era case. The control holds only if the Tatra/Bofors/Rafale records carry equivalent latest-stage edges. That is the file-level symmetryCheck's job, not a defect in this edge.
verdicts.denialFound: Michel has denied wrongdoing throughout. In his bail application he called the CBI allegations "absolutely false and baseless" (reported, e.g. Deccan Herald https://www.deccanherald.com/india/middleman-michel-claims-he-never-2064871; The Wire https://m.thewire.in/article/law/let-me-remain-in-tihar-augustawestland-accused-christian-michel-refuses-bail). Italy's Court of Cassation (2019) upheld the acquittals in the Italian proceedings. This edge records only procedural events (extradition, bail, stage), not guilt, so the denial belongs on the c071 'alleged' edge's contra, not here. Gulf News carries no statement from Michel or his lawyer about the SC bail.
verdicts.innocentReading: The edge says only that an accused was extradited, got bail from the SC and the HC after more than six years of custody, and that charges were not yet framed after seven years. That reflects slow investigation and multi-agency (CBI/ED) proceedings, not a finding of guilt or innocence. Nothing in it implies wrongdoing by any government, and it is as consistent with prosecutorial delay as with a strong case.
verdicts.reason: The claim is not refuted. All four dated facts check out against the sources. The Gulf News quote confirms the SC bail of 18 Feb 2025. ANI and Business Standard (dated 4 Mar 2025) confirm the Delhi HC bail in the ED case on 4 Mar 2025, which the record wrongly described as resting on a 'search summary'. LawBeat quotes the Special CBI Judge's line that "charges are yet to be decided". Gulf News places the extradition arrest on 4 Dec 2018. The only variance is Wikipedia's 5 Dec 2018, explained by the late-night arrival. The edge is a conjunction of procedural facts and draws no further inference. 'Reported' is the right tier and is conservative. Each date except the 23 Dec stage has two or more independent outlets, but the charges-not-framed element rests on one outlet's report of the order, not the order itself.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Add the primary-outlet sources for the HC bail: ANI https://aninews.in/news/national/general-news/agustawestland-pmla-case-delhi-hc-grants-bail-to-christian-michel-in-ed-matter20250304185321/ and Business Standard https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/agustawestland-delhi-hc-grants-bail-to-christian-michel-in-ed-case-125030400950_1.html. Remove '(search summary of Business Standard)' from 'd'. 2) In 'd', note that Wikipedia gives 5 Dec 2018 and Gulf News gives the arrest as 4 Dec 2018, after a late-night arrival. 3) Note that the LawBeat article is dated 24 Dec 2025, reporting the order of 23 Dec 2025. Name the judge (Special CBI Judge Sanjay Jindal) and the quote ("proceedings are at initial stage and charges are yet to be decided"). 4) Edge source node: force:delhi-district-courts does not cover the SC (18 Feb 2025) or the Delhi HC (4 Mar 2025). Either change s to a generic courts/judiciary node or split the claim into three edges, one per court. Consider whether 'enforce' is the right predicate for bail rulings. 5) Optional: add a pointer to the later procedural history (the Delhi HC modified the bail conditions on 22 May 2025, and the SC dismissed his challenge to the local-address condition on 29 May 2025) so 'to: null' is not read as continuous custody or release without qualification.

verdicts.dateTest: Written out, the claim is: MoD/Army procured Tatra trucks through BEML, which bought them via an intermediary at inflated prices, from 1986 onward. The allegation became public and was acted on in 2012. Oneindia says the CBI registered the case on 30 Mar 2012 naming Rishi and unnamed MoD, Army and BEML officials. Tribune, 12 Jun 2012: "The Ministry of Defence (MoD) suspended Chairman-cum-Managing-Director ... VRS Natarajan this morning" (11 Jun). A K Antony was Defence Minister from 2006 to 2014, so the FIR date falls inside his tenure. Natarajan had been CMD "for more than 10 years", so the alleged conduct also falls inside his tenure. The problem is the edge's from=2012-06-11. That is the suspension date, not the date of any award. Oneindia says "Since 1986, the Indian Army has bought over 7,000 Tatra trucks", so an award edge dated 2012 misdates the procurement. The date of the suspension belongs on a separate enforce edge (MoD→BEML CMD, or CBI→force:case-tatra), not on the award edge.
verdicts.identityTest: This passes. co:beml is Bharat Earth Movers Ltd, Bangalore, the DPSU both sources name. Tribune says it is "the government-run defence equipment manufacturer Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML)". The intermediary is named in the sources as NRI Ravi (Ravinder) Rishi / Vectra Group (Tatra Sipox UK).
