He is not on this edge, which is correct because the refusal rule bars naming a vendor as beneficiary without a primary record. Direction MoD→BEML for the award is right: the Army was the buyer through MoD and BEML was the supplier.
verdicts.baseRate: This is not a base-rate claim. It is a single case record. The SPEC pairs it with AgustaWestland (UPA-era to UPA-era) using identical fields. Both cases involve an alleged middleman in a UPA-II-period procurement, and both were run by the CBI. The symmetry holds as long as the AgustaWestland record also carries its contra and court stage with the same detail. Nothing here suggests a property that 80% or more of DPSUs share. Buying spares and finished vehicles through a foreign marketing entity is common, though, so the "intermediary" element only discriminates if Tatra Sipox UK was not an OEM entity. That point is disputed (see the innocent reading).
verdicts.denialFound: Natarajan, Tribune 12 Jun 2012 (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2012/20120612/main1.htm): "Natarajan today said he respected the government's decision and maintained he would come out clean". The same article says Natarajan called the General's assessment of the trucks incorrect and demanded an apology. A search result summary (Ajai Shukla, https://www.ajaishukla.com/2012/03/bribe-row-puts-spotlight-on-bemls-tatra.html, and Deccan Herald https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india/tatra-scam-beml-had-technology-2350706) says BEML management and MoD officials denied engaging an agent. They said Tatra Sipox (UK) Ltd was a wholly owned subsidiary and marketing arm of the OEM Tatra Sipox a.s. Rishi and Natarajan both said no rules were violated. I did not open these two pages in full, so this text comes from the search summary and not a verbatim quote. The record says "BEML's own response was not retrieved", which is wrong: it exists and should be added as a contra.
verdicts.innocentReading: BEML had bought Tatra vehicles and kits for the Army under a long-running arrangement since 1986. It treated Tatra Sipox UK as the OEM's authorised marketing arm, so in its view this was not a prohibited middleman. On this reading the price gap reflects BEML's value-add, margins and kit assembly rather than a kickback. The CBI's own 2014 finding of insufficient evidence for a chargesheet is consistent with this reading. Against it, the reported documents show Tatra Sipox UK (incorporated 1994) predating Tatra Sipox a.s. (1998). That cuts against the "subsidiary" defence. It is why the matter remains an allegation and has not been dismissed.
verdicts.reason: The core claim holds at the alleged tier. The Tribune page I opened confirms the CBI case on the Defence Minister's request, the 11 Jun 2012 suspension of the BEML CMD, and the allegations of a middleman instead of direct purchase from the OEM and "around 60 per cent more". Named parties made the allegation: Gen V K Singh, ex-BEML AGM S N Ashoka, shareholder K S Periyaswamy, and the CBI FIR itself. A contra exists (c076). But three fields misstate the sources. (1) a=750 sits on an award edge, which implies a ₹750 crore contract value. Oneindia's 750 is an unattributed alleged amount siphoned "in bribes and commissions" ("It was alleged that BEML officials, and the defence ministry siphoned off at least Rs 750 crore"). It is not an award value. (2) from=2012-06-11 is the suspension date, not when anything was awarded; procurement ran from 1986. (3) "answered by CBI's own 2014 closure report" overstates the record. The closure report was filed on 26 Aug 2014, but reporting indicates the special court had not accepted it as of 2019, and the Lt Gen Tejinder Singh bribe-offer charges were framed and upheld by the Delhi HC in 2022. These are fixable field errors, not a refutation of the alleged edge.
verdicts.corrections: (1) Set a=null on c075. Move the 750 figure into d as: "Oneindia (27 Aug 2014), unattributed: 'It was alleged that BEML officials, and the defence ministry siphoned off at least Rs 750 crore in bribes and commissions' — alleged diversion, not contract value". (2) Set from to the procurement start (1986, per Oneindia "Since 1986, the Indian Army has bought over 7,000 Tatra trucks") or null. Put the 2012-03-30 CBI FIR and the 2012-06-11 suspension on enforce edges. (3) Name the allegers in d: Gen V K Singh (bribe-offer claim), S N Ashoka (2009 memo), K S Periyaswamy (shareholder). (4) Change the label from "answered by CBI's own 2014 closure report" to "CBI filed a closure report 26 Aug 2014 citing insufficient evidence; court acceptance not established (reported pending as of 2019)". (5) Add a contra edge from co:beml / BEML management: Tatra Sipox (UK) Ltd described as the OEM's wholly owned marketing subsidiary, and no rules violated (Natarajan, Rishi). Source: Ajai Shukla, Mar 2012 (https://www.ajaishukla.com/2012/03/bribe-row-puts-spotlight-on-bemls-tatra.html) and Deccan Herald. Replace "BEML's own response was not retrieved". (6) On c076, downgrade tier from documented to reported, since it rests on one Oneindia explainer and the closure report itself was not opened. (7) Remove the Oneindia phrase "Rs 750 crore siphoned off" from any headline-level label; it is the outlet's framing, not a finding.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim is: CBI (prosecuting agency), through the Special Judge CBI at Rouse Avenue, had charges framed under s.12 PC Act on 2019-08-02 against a retired Lt Gen, on the complaint of Gen V K Singh, Army Chief from 31 Mar 2010 to 31 May 2012. The alleged offer was made on 2010-09-22, inside his tenure, so the date test passes for the complaint. The HC date is wrong. The record gives 2022-07-22 for the Delhi HC refusal, but that is the date the PTI/Devdiscourse/ThePrint stories were published. The judgment itself (Indian Kanoon doc 157216120, CRL.REV.P. 832/2019, 2022/DHC/002687) reads "Reserved on: 06.07.2022 / Date of Decision: 20.07.2022", with signing date 21.07.2022. The Tribune piece in the record says the HC upheld the charges "in June 2022", which is also wrong, so that source should not be relied on for this date.
verdicts.identityTest: This passes. Every source names the same accused (Lt Gen (retd) Tejinder Singh), the same complainant (Gen V K Singh, then COAS), the same amount (Rs 14 crore), the same meeting date (22 Sep 2010), the same subject (1676 HMVs including Tatra) and the same judge (Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav). The record correctly flags this as a "separate case" from the BEML/Tatra procurement FIR of 2012, which the CBI closed in 2014. Hanging it on force:case-tatra is acceptable only because the lab says "Separate case". The accused is below the public rank, and the lab correctly leaves him unnamed and out of the nodes. V K Singh is a service chief, which is a public rank, so naming him is allowed.
verdicts.baseRate: This is a single case-stage fact, not a property compared across entities, so the base rate is not discriminating either way. On symmetry, the SPEC control runs AgustaWestland beside Tatra, and both concern UPA-II-era procurement. The edge is a court-stage record, not a partisan inference, so running the same lens on a rival produces no asymmetry.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and the record does not carry it. In 2012 Tejinder Singh publicly denied the allegation as "absolutely false and concocted" and filed a criminal defamation complaint against Gen V K Singh and four officers (Deccan Herald / Tribune 2012 coverage, e.g. https://www.deccanherald.com/content/238536/army-chief-names-tejinder-cbi.html and https://www.tribuneindia.com/2012/20120426/main3.htm). In his statement to the CBI he admitted the meeting but said he went to seek support for the NTRO chief's post. In 2013 the CBI was reported to be closing the preliminary enquiry for lack of evidence (Hindustan Times 1 Jul 2013 via PressReader). In the HC his counsel argued that no s.12 offence was made out. The record does carry A K Antony's 2022 testimony that the Chief gave no note or recording, which supports the defence.
verdicts.innocentReading: Framing a charge needs only a prima facie case, and the HC's refusal to interfere at that stage is not a finding of guilt. The case rests on the complainant's word about a private meeting. The accused admits meeting him and gives another purpose for it, and the then Defence Minister testified that he received no documentary or audio evidence. No trial outcome was found. The accused is presumed innocent.
verdicts.reason: The substance survives. Charges were framed on 2 Aug 2019 on Gen V K Singh's complaint of a Rs 14 crore offer for 1676 HMVs, and the Delhi HC (Kaurav J) held the order "does not call for any interference". Both secondary sources say this, and the primary judgment confirms it. The claim cannot pass as written, though. The HC decision was given on 20.07.2022, not 2022-07-22 (the press date). The accused's public denial and his defamation complaint are missing from the record. Once the judgment URL is added as a source, this is a primary court record, so `documented` is the right tier for the stage facts (charge framed, revision dismissed). The bribe offer itself stays an allegation under trial.
verdicts.corrections: 1) In lab/text, change "Delhi HC refused to interfere 22 Jul 2022" to "20 Jul 2022 (decided; reported 22 Jul 2022)". 2) Add the source ["Delhi HC, Lt Gen (Retd) Tejinder Singh v CBI, CRL.REV.P. 832/2019, decided 20.07.2022, 2022/DHC/002687", "https://indiankanoon.org/doc/157216120/"]. 3) Set from to "2019-08-02", the date of the Special Judge CBI (Rouse Avenue) order framing the s.12 PC Act charge. 4) Raise the tier to documented for the procedural facts, and make the wording explicit: "bribe offer alleged by the complainant; charge framed; trial pending; outcome not found". 5) Add the denial to d: in 2012 the accused called the allegation "absolutely false and concocted", filed criminal defamation against Gen V K Singh, and told the CBI he met the Chief to seek support for the NTRO post. Also note that the CBI was reported in 2013 to be closing the PE for lack of evidence. Cite the Deccan Herald / Tribune 2012 URLs. 6) In the Tribune source note, flag that it gives the HC ruling as "June 2022", which the judgment contradicts. 7) Keep the accused unnamed in lab and keep him out of the nodes, as the refusal on persons below public rank requires.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: the Government of Maharashtra (Revenue and Forests Department, Collector Mumbai; MMRDA as planning authority) allotted state land and granted building permissions to Adarsh CHS between 2003 and 2010. The cited HC judgment gives the dates: "On 18.1.2003, Revenue and Forests Department of Government of Maharashtra issued Letter of Intent", "On 4.10.2004, possession of Adarsh plot was handed over by the Collector, Mumbai", and plinth permission on 6.9.2005. The allegations came later: CBI FIR Jan 2011, MoEF demolition order 14.1.2011, CAG report 2011, the Army's WP 452/2012, the Commission's report Apr 2013. Each accuser was in office or existed when it made its allegation, so the actors and dates line up. But the edge's "from": "2011-01-14" is the MoEF order date. It is not the date of the award. An `award` edge should be dated to the LOI (2003-01-18) or the handover of possession (2004-10-04). The allegation dates belong in `d`.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. In WP 452/2012 the Society is "4. Adarsh Co-operative Housing Society Ltd, having its address at CTS No.652, Block VI, Colaba Division" (respondent no. 4). The State of Maharashtra is respondent no. 1, through its Urban Development Department. As a co-operative society it has no CIN or DIN, so `ty: trust` / `fam: recipient` is correct. One caveat: the clearances (building permissions) came from MMRDA and the Municipal Corporation (respondents 2 and 3), not from the State alone. The `award` s→t correctly carries only the land allotment.
verdicts.baseRate: The property "State allotted government land to a co-operative housing society at concessional terms" is very common in Mumbai and does not single Adarsh out. The Society said as much in its public defence ("there are so many like us": Samata, Nyay Sagar, and others; Indian Express 2011, cited on Wikipedia). The features that do single it out are rarer and are on record: (a) no security NOC from the Defence Establishment, which the HC held "mandatory" (para 85) and absent (paras 86-88); (b) 25 of 102 members found ineligible and 22 benami transactions (Commission, per Wikipedia); (c) a CAG audit finding. Symmetry: SPEC case controls pair Bofors with Rafale and AgustaWestland with Tatra; Adarsh has no assigned partisan pair. The allotting governments were Congress-NCP (1999-2014). That same government appointed the Commission (Jan 2011) and its cabinet first rejected the report and then partially accepted it. The BJP-led government reopened the case in 2014. Party belongs as text in `d` only. The nearest like-for-like control is Sukna (Army land NOC, 2009), already in the file.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. The contra edge money-people:c079 is present and documented from the HC judgment. The Society's affidavit of 31.7.2014 contends "the petition suffers from delay and laches", and its counsel submitted that the building was "constructed, completed and was granted Occupation Certificate" (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/121443544/). In its reply of 13.7.2005 the Society said "the plot falls in Block VI of Colaba Division where Defence Department owns no land". On title, the State Government told the Commission the land was state land (DNA, https://www.dnaindia.com/mumbai/report-adarsh-scam-land-belongs-to-us-maharashtra-govt-tells-probe-panel-1542537). The Society also made a public "so many like us" defence (Indian Express, cited on Wikipedia).
verdicts.innocentReading: The land was state land, not Army land. The Army's own Defence Estates Officer and HQ MG&G Area confirmed in 2000 that it "belongs to the Government of Maharashtra and falls outside the Defence Boundary" (HC para 86). On 30.9.2004 HQ MG&G Area also wrote that there were "no security implications" in the transfer. The Commission's interim report likewise held the land was the State's, contrary to the Ministry of Defence's claim, and found it was never reserved for Kargil widows. MMRDA's counsel argued that between 2003 and 2010 the Defence Establishment "did not raise any security concern". On this reading the Army's later claim is about security and the missing NOC, not about title. The allotment was an ordinary discretionary state allotment. The illegality turns on eligibility of members, FSI and the missing NOC, which the HC decided (demolition ordered; stayed by the SC on 22 Jul 2016; appeal pending). The CBI trial and SC appeal are unfinished, so "breach of rules" has not been finally adjudicated. That keeps the claim at alleged.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives because its core is on record. The CAG said officials "could subvert rules and regulations in order to grab prime government land" (Wikipedia, quoting CAG Report No. 11 of 2011-12, Defence Services). The CBI has investigated since Jan 2011. The HC judgment records the MoEF demolition order "dated 14.1.2011" and holds that the defence NOC was mandatory and never obtained. The contra c079 is in the file, so `alleged` meets the contract. However, the phrase "on land the Army claimed" is not supported by the cited HC judgment, which records the opposite. The Army's own DEO and HQ MG&G Area confirmed in 2000 that the land "belongs to the Government of Maharashtra and fell outside the Defence Boundary". The 2003 LOI records only that the land was "in possession of the Defence Department". The Ministry of Defence's title claim was rejected by the Commission's interim report. Also, the HC judgment does not mention the CAG or the CBI. Those parts rest on Wikipedia alone, so sourceCheck is "partially". The edge is not refuted, but the framing and dating need correcting.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Label: change "on land the Army claimed" to "on state land in Defence possession beside the Colaba Military Station". Add to `d`: "The Ministry of Defence claimed title; the Commission's interim report held the land belonged to the State; in 2000 the Army's DEO and HQ MG&G Area had confirmed state ownership (HC para 86)." 2) Attribution in `d`: the Army's WP 452/2012 alleges that building permissions were given without a security NOC from the Defence Establishment, and seeks demolition. It does not allege that the allotment itself breached rules. Attribute the allotment allegation to the CAG, the CBI and the Commission, which found 25 of 102 members ineligible and 22 benami transactions. 3) CAG citation: the Wikipedia source URL path is ".../2011_12/Defence_Services/Report_11/Adarsh_Defence.pdf", so cite "Report No. 11 of 2011-12 (Union Government, Defence Services)", not "Report No. 11 of 2011". 4) Change "the Maharashtra Cabinet rejected its findings in Dec 2013" to "rejected, then partially accepted after review (Dec 2013-Jan 2014; Wikipedia)". 5) `from`: an award edge should carry the award date. Use 2003-01-18 (LOI) or 2004-10-04 (possession handed over), both from the HC judgment. Move 2011-01-14 into `d` as the MoEF order date. 6) Source note: the HC judgment supports the MoEF order date, the NOC finding and the Society's answer. It does not mention the CAG or the CBI, so tag those parts as reported via Wikipedia, or open the CAG PDF on the archive (web.archive.org is blocked here; try a cag.gov.in mirror). 7) Optionally add the State's ownership affidavit (DNA) as a second contra on the title point.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Supreme Court (bench of J. Chelameswar and A. M. Sapre per Business Standard) directs Centre to take possession of the Adarsh building and no demolition, 22 Jul 2016. This follows the Bombay HC judgment of 29 Apr 2016 (c080), which stayed demolition for 12 weeks so the Society could appeal. 29 Apr plus 12 weeks is about 22 Jul, so the date fits the sequence. Deccan Chronicle is dated "22 July 2016 1:10 PM IST" and says "on Friday"; 22 Jul 2016 was a Friday. Ranjit Kumar was Solicitor General from 2014 to 2017, so his tenure covers the date. Passes.
verdicts.identityTest: The subject is the 31-storey Adarsh housing society building in Colaba, which is the same entity as force:adarsh-society, respondent 4 in WP 452/2012. The actor is the Supreme Court of India. The Centre's representative is named as SG Ranjit Kumar. No CIN or DIN applies (cooperative society). Passes.
verdicts.baseRate: Not discriminating, and the claim does not need it. An SC interim stay or status-quo order on a High Court demolition order pending appeal is the routine outcome when the losing party appeals, and most such appeals get one. The claim records a procedural event and imputes no wrongdoing, so no symmetry control (UPA/NDA) is engaged. The order was made under the NDA government on a matter decided under the UPA, and the Centre (NDA) itself undertook to secure the building, which cuts against any partisan reading.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable in the usual sense, because the claim is a court action and not an allegation against a party. The Society's position appears in c079: delay, Occupation Certificate, and its intention to appeal. The SC order is effectively the result of that appeal. No statement from the Society on the 22 Jul order was found. Not asked by us.
verdicts.innocentReading: This is an ordinary interim order pending the appeal. The SC kept the subject matter intact (no demolition, Centre in possession through the military estate officer, supervised by the HC registrar) until it could hear the appeal. It is not a final ruling on the merits. It neither vindicates nor condemns the Society.
verdicts.reason: The Deccan Chronicle source says what the claim says. Quote: "The top court asked the Centre to take over possession and to ensure that no demolition takes place while securing the controversial Adarsh society building... 'We will secure the building and there will be no demolition,' said Solicitor General Ranjit Kumar to the court. The next hearing of the case has been fixed for August 5." Business Standard of 23 Jul 2016 independently reports the same thing ("Take possession of Adarsh apartments: SC to Centre", https://www.pressreader.com/india/business-standard/20160723/281522225443621). The claim survives. Tier stays 'reported' rather than 'documented' for two reasons: the SC order itself was not opened, and DC is "with agency inputs", so the two outlets may both draw on PTI and may not be independent. There is one problem with how it is framed. DC's URL slug ("sc-quashes-hc-order") and its lead sentence ("ruled against the Bombay High Court order") overstate what happened. This was an interim order, not a quashing, and the record should not inherit that wording.
verdicts.corrections: (1) In c081 'd', change "Judicial ruling on money-people:c078" to "Interim order (appeal pending) on money-people:c078". Add the bench (J. Chelameswar, A. M. Sapre) and the detail that the military estate officer takes charge under supervision of the HC registrar, to be completed by 5 Aug 2016. (2) Add Business Standard 23 Jul 2016 (https://www.pressreader.com/india/business-standard/20160723/281522225443621) as a second source. Leave the tier at 'reported' unless the SC record of proceedings (SLP/Civil Appeal against WP 452/2012) is retrieved from sci.gov.in, in which case upgrade to 'documented'. (3) Do not reuse DC's slug wording "quashes HC order" anywhere. The force:case-adarsh 'sub' ("SC stayed it 22 Jul 2016") is correct. The narrative's strongestCounter ("Supreme Court halted demolition ... and the Centre took possession") is acceptable but should say "interim order". (4) Keep the existing note "final Supreme Court outcome was not found".

verdicts.dateTest: Restated: the Army's Court of Inquiry and then a General Court Martial (GCM) alleged that 33 Corps improperly issued a no-objection certificate (NOC) at Sukna, with disciplinary action set in motion in January 2010. Deccan Chronicle (6 Sep 2014) gives the year of the NOC: "The case pertains to the grant of a no-objection certificate by the Army's Siliguri-based 33 Corps for construction on non-Army land adjoining Army land at Sukna in West Bengal in 2009." Some outlets (Assam Tribune, India TV) put the land matter in 2008, so the year is contested at the margin. The Supreme Court judgment, as quoted by Legal Services India, puts Avadhesh Prakash's show-cause notice at 11.01.2010, his retirement at 31.01.2010 and the switch to disciplinary proceedings "two days prior to his retirement". That fits from:"2010-01". The same text also says "Court of Inquiry on 07.01.2009" while the scam "broke out in the end of the year 2010", which contradicts itself and probably contains a typo. A K Antony was Defence Minister from 26 Oct 2006 to 26 May 2014, so the MoD action (Antony recommended court martial on 27 Jan 2010, per Tribune and Deccan Herald reporting found by search) falls inside his term. The rulings come later: AFT on 5 Sep 2014 (Rath) and SC on 24 Jan 2019 (Prakash). The dates pass.
verdicts.identityTest: Partial. Neither cited source names the edge's actor, min:ministry-of-defence. Deccan Chronicle names only 33 Corps, the Army court martial and Gen V K Singh as a respondent. The SC text says "The Chief of Army Staff initially directed Administrative Action" and then disciplinary proceedings were started. It does not say who forced that change. The edge's own note says the MoD link rests on "Deccan Herald/Tribune summaries; pages not opened". A web search did turn up those outlets (tribuneindia.com/2010/20100128/main2.htm; deccanherald.com/content/49530/army-chief-orders-court-martial.html), and they report that Antony recommended a court martial on 27 Jan 2010 after Army chief Deepak Kapoor had recommended only administrative action. So the MoD link is reportable, but the srcs listed do not support it. The allegation itself came from the Army: a Court of Inquiry ordered by Eastern Army Commander Lt Gen V K Singh. The two officers are named correctly (Rath in the AFT 2014 ruling, Avadhesh Prakash in the SC 2019 ruling).
verdicts.baseRate: This lens does not really apply. The SPEC's case set has seven cases, and four of them (AgustaWestland, Tatra, Sukna, Adarsh) began under the UPA. The file already runs the same fields on the NDA-era cases (Rafale, Pegasus), and none of the seven ended in a final conviction. Sukna is not picked out by any property more than 80% of comparable cases share. The UPA/NDA symmetry is written into the file. Note that in this case the UPA-era MoD pushed for prosecution rather than shielding the officers, which cuts against a partisan reading.
verdicts.denialFound: The record already carries answers from the accused officers' side. AFT, 5 Sep 2014 (Deccan Chronicle): "The petitioner, Lt. Gen. Rath (retd.) is acquitted of all charges. He is entitled to restoration of all benefits with 12 percent interest". The tribunal also blamed the respondents for "undue harassment and loss of reputation" (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/140906/nation-current-affairs/article/lt-general-p-k-rathretd-cleared-sukna-scam). SC, 24 Jan 2019: the GCM was improperly constituted (one Lt Gen and four Maj Gens) and "the entire proceedings held by the said GCM stood vitiated" (https://www.legalservicesindia.com/law/print/1159). Rath also spoke publicly (deccanherald.com 'rath-says-he-has-been'). No separate response from the MoD on the rulings was found. We did not ask for one.
verdicts.innocentReading: Several readings fit without the NOC being shown to be corrupt. The NOC may have been an ordinary corps-level decision about non-Army land. It came under suspicion after a private trust falsely claimed a Mayo College affiliation. A command-level Court of Inquiry and a minister keen to look tough after Adarsh then escalated it into prosecutions. One prosecution failed on the merits (Rath was acquitted by the AFT). The other failed on procedure (Prakash, because the GCM sat below his rank). On this reading the "improper NOC" may have been poor judgment or a deception practised on the officers, not corruption.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives because the core allegation is in the record: the Army's Court of Inquiry and GCM charged officers over the 33 Corps NOC at Sukna, which both cited sources confirm. The alleged tier carries its contra (c084 for the AFT, c085 for the SC), as the contract requires. It has three defects to fix. (1) The cited srcs do not support the actor, min:ministry-of-defence. The MoD's 27 Jan 2010 recommendation is only reportable from Tribune/Deccan Herald pages that the file admits it did not open. (2) "Answered by SC 2019" overstates what the SC did. It set the GCM aside only on how the court was constituted, and it did not rule on the merits. The SC text also shows that the AFT in its 2017 order (dated 20.12.2017) had upheld Prakash's guilt on 'unbecoming conduct' under Section 45 of the Army Act, and the file leaves that out. (3) The 'influenced and vitiated' quote attributed to the AFT in node d and in c084 does not appear on the Deccan Chronicle page. That page says "undue harassment and loss of reputation".
verdicts.corrections: c083.srcs: add the Tribune (28 Jan 2010, https://www.tribuneindia.com/2010/20100128/main2.htm) and Deccan Herald (https://www.deccanherald.com/content/49530/army-chief-orders-court-martial.html) pages after opening them, or else change s to the Army (Eastern Command Court of Inquiry) and drop the MoD link. c083.d: replace 'Defence Minister recommended court martial Jan 2010 (pages not opened)' with sourced wording: 'Army chief Deepak Kapoor recommended administrative action; Defence Minister A K Antony recommended court martial of Lt Gen Avadhesh Prakash on 27 Jan 2010'. Add 'Court of Inquiry ordered by Eastern Army Commander'. Note that the year is 2009 per Deccan Chronicle and 2008 in other reporting. Claim text: change 'answered by AFT 2014 and SC 2019' to 'Rath acquitted on merits by AFT 2014; Prakash's dismissal set aside by SC 2019 on GCM composition (procedural), after AFT in Dec 2017 had upheld guilt on unbecoming conduct'. force:case-sukna d 'Counter-record' and c084.d: remove the quote 'influenced and vitiated', which is not on the Deccan Chronicle page, and quote 'undue harassment and loss of reputation' instead. The word 'vitiated' belongs to the SC 2019 ruling on Prakash. Do not put the Lt Gens' names in node or claim text (they are below public rank); keeping them in source titles is acceptable.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: Supreme Court (bench of A K Sikri, S Abdul Nazeer and M R Shah) set aside the GCM dismissal of Ex Lt Gen Avadhesh Prakash on 24 Jan 2019. The cited source and the primary order on Indian Kanoon (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/156623410/, "Avadhesh Prakash vs Union Of India on 24 January, 2019", Supreme Court Daily Orders) both give 24 Jan 2019, Criminal Appeal No. 140 of 2019 with Civil Appeal No. 9739/2018. The order sets out the chain: Prakash was Military Secretary from 01.05.2008, his name came up in the Court of Inquiry on 07.01.2009, disciplinary proceedings were started two days before he retired on 31.01.2010, the GCM dismissed him, and the AFT ruled on 20.12.2017. The SC ruling comes after all of these. The dates pass. One snag: the order itself says the scam "broke out in the end of the year 2010", which sits badly with a 2009 Court of Inquiry. That is a slip inside the judgment and does not affect the 24 Jan 2019 date.
verdicts.identityTest: Pass. Both sources name the officer as Ex Lt Gen Avadhesh Prakash, commissioned 20.12.1970, promoted Lt Gen in Oct 2007 and Military Secretary from 01.05.2008. The order ties the proceedings to the "so-called 'Sukna Land Scam' case", so the target force:case-sukna is correct. This is a different officer from Lt Gen P K Rath, whom the AFT cleared in Sep 2014 (c084), and the order names Rath's GCM separately. The claim's "a former Lt Gen" is accurate. A Lt Gen is above the public-rank threshold, so naming him is allowed.
verdicts.baseRate: Mostly not applicable, because this is a single dated court order rather than a pattern claim. As a check on the case set, 0 of the 7 named case records ended in a final conviction. So "court set the outcome aside" is common across the seven, and on its own it says nothing about guilt or innocence either way.
verdicts.denialFound: The respondent was Union of India (MoD/Army). Its position, as recorded in the order, was that Rule 40(2) of the Army Rules was complied with because the appellant had already retired, and the AFT had accepted this. The SC rejected it: "Merely because the appellant had retired in the meantime cannot be a ground to discard and give a go by to the provisions of Rule 40(2)". I found no later MoD statement or review petition. Not asked by us.
verdicts.innocentReading: The set-aside was procedural, not an exoneration on the merits. The SC held the GCM invalidly constituted (one Lt Gen and four Maj Gens tried a Lt Gen, against Rule 40). It declined to send the case back for a fresh GCM because only one charge, s.45 'unbecoming conduct', still stood after the AFT ruling, that charge was "not of a very serious nature", the officer had retired, and other officers had received only "severe reprimand". The claim text says "set aside", which is accurate and does not overstate. But the Legal Services India column's gloss that the bench "found no credible evidence" and that he "stands acquitted" is the columnist's wording, not the court's, and must not be carried into the record.
verdicts.reason: The claim survives. The cited Legal Services India article quotes the order, and the primary SC order on Indian Kanoon confirms it word for word: "the GCM was not validly constituted... entire proceedings held by the said GCM stand vitiated... The punishment of dismissal imposed upon the appellant also stands set aside. The appellant shall be entitled to all the benefits; pensionary or otherwise... within a period of three months." The date, bench, officer and outcome all match. Now that the primary court order is open, the tier should go up from reported to documented.
verdicts.corrections: (1) tier: reported -> documented. Add the primary source ["Supreme Court, Ex Lt Gen Avadhesh Prakash v Union of India, Crl.A. 140/2019 with C.A. 9739/2018, 24 Jan 2019 (Indian Kanoon)", "https://indiankanoon.org/doc/156623410/"] ahead of the Legal Services India column, which is an advocate's commentary. (2) In d, add the scope of the ruling: "Set aside on the composition of the GCM (Rule 40, Army Rules); the Court did not remit for a fresh GCM, noting that only one charge (s.45 unbecoming conduct) survived the AFT's 20 Dec 2017 order and was 'not of a very serious nature'; it is not a finding on the merits of the Sukna allegation." (3) Optionally, name the officer (Ex Lt Gen Avadhesh Prakash, Military Secretary from 1 May 2008), since he is at public rank and named in the order. (4) In the related refutation entry and the case-sukna node, keep "set aside" and avoid "acquitted / no credible evidence" for this officer. (5) In c083 and the case node, flag the internal date tension: the CoI is dated 07.01.2009, but the order says the scam "broke out in the end of the year 2010".

verdicts.dateTest: The claim is that petitioners in WP(Crl) 314/2021 and connected petitions alleged, from July 2021, that Pegasus (NSO Group) was used against Indian phones. The SC order of 27 Oct 2021 says: "On 18th July 2021, a consortium of nearly 17 journalistic organizations from around the world, including one Indian organization, released the results..." and the petitions were filed after that. So from=2021-07 is correct. The window falls inside the NDA term (Home: Amit Shah, MeitY: Vaishnaw from 7 Jul 2021). The underlying 2019 WhatsApp-vector targeting also falls under NDA-II. The dates are consistent.
verdicts.identityTest: NSO Group is the entity the order names: "a 'spyware suite' called Pegasus that was being produced by an Israeli Technology firm, viz., the NSO Group". The leaked numbers were "allegedly under surveillance by clients of the NSO Group through the Pegasus software". The order does not name an Indian buyer, and neither does the file ("No Indian purchase record is in this file"). The edge s=force:nso-group is therefore the producer, not the alleged user. That is accurate as long as the edge is not read as NSO having surveilled anyone itself. The predicate 'sector' is a misfit. It is meant for an entity-to-industry edge, and here it links a vendor to a court case record. The claim text passed to me ("answered by Union's position and limited affidavit") differs from the file label ("petitions of 2021"). The answer does exist as contra c087, so this is cosmetic.
verdicts.baseRate: Pegasus targeting was not unique to India. Citizen Lab (2018) found suspected infections in about 45 countries, as the order recounts. The WhatsApp v NSO exhibits in N.D. Cal. (2025) list 1,223 victims in 51 countries, with Mexico 456, India 100, Bahrain 82, Morocco 60 and Pakistan 58. So "Pegasus was used against citizens of country X" does not single out India or the BJP. It is a property of NSO's government client base. Symmetry: the case-record fields (subject, government at the time, first allegation, investigating body, stage, counter-record) are the same as for Bofors and Rafale. Under the same lens, a UPA-era surveillance allegation would be read the same way. Pegasus has no UPA-era counterpart because NSO's India exposure dates from 2017–19.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes. (1) The Union's position as recorded in the SC order: the Solicitor General "reiterated the statement dated 18th July 2021 made by the Hon'ble Minister of Railways, Communications and Electronics and Information Technology ... regarding the statutory mechanism ... which ensures that unauthorized surveillance does not take place". A 'limited affidavit' of 16 Aug 2021 cited national security (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/39021018/). This is in the file as contra c087. (2) Not in the file: on 9 Aug 2021, MoS Defence Ajay Bhatt said in a Rajya Sabha written reply that "the Ministry of Defence has not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies" (https://www.theweek.in/news/india/2021/08/09/no-transaction-with-nso-group-defence-ministry-tells-parliament.html ; https://scroll.in/latest/1002445/pegasus-row-defence-ministry-has-not-had-any-transaction-with-nso-group-says-centre). This denial covers only MoD, not MHA or the agencies. The Union never confirmed or denied use by the agencies authorised to intercept.
verdicts.innocentReading: Pegasus may have been used on phones in India by a foreign government client of NSO rather than an Indian agency. The leaked list of 50,000 numbers is a list of possible targets, not of confirmed infections. The SC Technical Committee (25 Aug 2022, per the CJI's oral summary) found malware in 5 of 29 phones but could not attribute it to Pegasus. Lawful interception under the Telegraph Act/IT Act s.69 is a separate route the Union points to. None of these readings rules out Indian state use. The question is unresolved, so 'alleged' is the right tier for the use-by-whom proposition.
verdicts.reason: The source holds. The 27 Oct 2021 SC order (Indian Kanoon 39021018) says what the claim says: 18 Jul 2021, nearly 17 organisations, a list of some 50,000 numbers allegedly surveilled by NSO's clients, nearly 300 Indian ("senior journalists, doctors, political persons, and even some Court staff"), and the Citizen Lab 'spyware suite' report. The allegation is unadjudicated: the committee could not establish Pegasus on the 29 phones, the report is sealed, and on 29 Apr 2025 the Court declined to publish it. The required contra (c087) is in the same file, so 'alleged' carries its answer as the contract requires. The claim is not refuted. The wording is loose, though. The same order records that the then MeitY Minister acknowledged in Parliament on 20 Nov 2019 that "the devices of certain Indians were also affected" by Pegasus via WhatsApp. The US WhatsApp v NSO exhibits also count 100 India victims. So the bare proposition "Pegasus was used against phones of Indian citizens" is documented. What remains alleged is that Indian state agencies used it against the roughly 300 people on the 2021 list. The label should say this so the tier attaches to the right proposition.
verdicts.corrections: 1) lab: rewrite to name the alleged proposition, e.g. "Alleged (petitions of 2021): Indian state agencies used NSO Group's Pegasus against ~300 Indian numbers on the leaked list". Do not use the unqualified "Pegasus used against phones of Indian citizens", which is under-tiered. 2) pred: 'sector' is wrong for vendor→case. Use the case-record convention: 'law'/'mechanism' linkage or an 'analytic' link, or move the allegation edge so it runs from the petitioners/case node. Keep NSO as producer only. 3) d: "about 17 news organisations" should read "nearly 17 journalistic organisations ... including one Indian organisation", as printed. Add that at filing "nearly 10 Indians' devices were allegedly forensically analysed". 4) Add a documented sibling edge or a line in d: on 20 Nov 2019 the then MeitY Minister acknowledged in Parliament that Indian WhatsApp users' devices were affected by Pegasus (recounted in the same SC order, para 4). 5) Add the MoD denial as a second contra: Ajay Bhatt, Rajya Sabha written reply, 9 Aug 2021, "Ministry of Defence has not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies". Note that MHA, not MoD, authorises interception. 6) upgradeIf: an official admission of procurement or use by an Indian agency, or publication of the Technical Committee report attributing infections. Note the WhatsApp v NSO (N.D. Cal., 2025) exhibit counting 100 India victims of the 2019 campaign as reported context (TechCrunch 9 Apr 2025; The Wire). It does not name the client. 7) The 18 Jul 2021 date for the Minister's statement in c087 follows the order, but Parliament convened on 19 Jul 2021. Flag "as recorded in the order".

verdicts.dateTest: The claim reads: the SC Technical Committee (constituted 27 Oct 2021, overseen by Justice R V Raveendran) reported, through CJI N V Ramana's bench (Ramana, Surya Kant, Hima Kohli), that malware was found in 5 of 29 phones, that Pegasus was not established, and that the Government had not cooperated. This was read out on 25 Aug 2022. The reports were filed in sealed cover in early August 2022 and opened at the 25 Aug 2022 hearing. Ramana was CJI until 26 Aug 2022, so the date falls inside his tenure and the committee's mandate. The dates agree and the from-date of 2022-08-25 is correct.
verdicts.identityTest: The committee is the one named in the 27 Oct 2021 order: Chaudhary, Prabaharan and Gumaste, overseen by Raveendran. The Tribune names the bench as "Justice NV Ramana... Justice Surya Kant and Justice Hima Kohli". A CIN or DIN does not apply to a court body. The entity matches.
verdicts.baseRate: Does not apply. This is a single court-record event, not a comparative or discriminating property. No inference from a pattern is made. There is no symmetry control that fits (the SPEC lists case-pegasus as a case record, not as one side of a paired comparison).
verdicts.denialFound: At the hearing, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta replied to the CJI's remark on non-cooperation: "I am not aware of that" (LiveLaw and Alt News, https://www.altnews.in/amit-malviyas-claim-that-the-sc-did-not-allege-non-cooperation-by-the-govt-during-pegasus-probe-is-misleading/). BJP IT cell head Amit Malviya publicly said the SC "hasn't alleged non cooperation by central Govt". Alt News rated this misleading, but confirmed the written order of 25 Aug 2022 is procedural only and says nothing on cooperation. The non-cooperation finding exists only as the CJI's oral reading of the sealed report. The government did not issue a substantive rebuttal of the 5-of-29 finding. It has held throughout that national-security details cannot be disclosed.
verdicts.innocentReading: Finding generic malware on 5 of 29 phones does not show state surveillance. The committee reportedly said it could not attribute the malware to Pegasus, and it may reflect poor cyber hygiene. The government's "non-cooperation" matches the stand it took openly in court: it refused to say on affidavit, on national-security grounds, whether it used Pegasus. It is not necessarily evidence of concealment. The claim as worded ("Pegasus not established") already avoids both over-readings: "Pegasus was used" and "Pegasus was disproven".
verdicts.reason:
The claim survives. The Tribune (25 Aug 2022) carries the key sentences: "In five phones some malware was found but the technical committee says it can't be said to be Pegasus" and "the Bench... quoted the panel as having said that the Government did not help it". ThePrint, Deccan Herald, Outlook and LiveLaw independently corroborate both points. Two caveats keep it at reported rather than documented:
- The second cited source (the MediaNama article on the committee's report, Aug 2022) predates the hearing and does not support the claim. It does not mention the five phones, Pegasus attribution or non-cooperation, so only one cited source supports it.
- The written SC order of 25 Aug 2022 is procedural only. The findings exist solely as the bench's oral reading of a sealed report, so no primary record contains them.
verdicts.corrections:
1. srcs: replace the MediaNama URL (pre-hearing; does not say 5/29, does not say Pegasus not established, does not mention non-cooperation) with https://theprint.in/india/29-mobile-phones-examined-malware-found-in-five-but-no-conclusive-proof-of-pegasus-panel-tells-sc/1100313/ and/or the LiveLaw report https://www.livelaw.in/top-stories/breaking-pegasus-probe-committee-report-to-remain-sealed-in-supreme-court-207519.
2. Add a denial/contra field: SG Tushar Mehta, "I am not aware of that"; Amit Malviya's claim that the SC did not allege non-cooperation, and Alt News's finding that his claim is misleading (https://www.altnews.in/amit-malviyas-claim-that-the-sc-did-not-allege-non-cooperation-by-the-govt-during-pegasus-probe-is-misleading/).
3. In d, state that the written order of 25 Aug 2022 records only that the reports were filed in sealed cover, and that the findings are the CJI's oral reading.
4. Keep the tier at reported even with two outlets, because no written record contains the findings.
5. Do not echo the Tribune headline ("No Pegasus spyware found"). Keep "Pegasus not established / could not be said to be Pegasus".

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Supreme Court bench (Surya Kant J, N Kotiswar Singh J) said the Technical Committee report would not be disclosed, at the hearing on 29 Apr 2025. Kant J was a puisne judge of the SC in Apr 2025 and had sat on the 27 Oct 2021 bench that set up the committee; he became CJI in Nov 2025. Kotiswar Singh J has been on the SC since Jul 2023. Both were in office on that date. LawBeat, SC Observer ('Day 8', 29 Apr 2025), Verdictum and Business Standard/PTI all date the hearing 29 Apr 2025. The next date of 30 Jul 2025 is confirmed by LawBeat and SC Observer. The date test passes.
verdicts.identityTest: Actor 'sc' is the Supreme Court of India, in WP(Crl) 314/2021 Manohar Lal Sharma v Union of India and connected matters. That is the same case as c086/c088/c089 and SC Observer's case page. The report is the Raveendran-supervised Technical Committee report, filed in a sealed cover in Aug 2022. The identity test passes.
verdicts.baseRate: Courts keep national-security material in sealed cover very often in Indian SC practice, so the property does not single anything out. Examples: Rafale pricing was given to the Court in a sealed cover in 2018. The Chandrachud bench criticised sealed covers in the 2023 OROP case but did not end the practice. The claim says nothing beyond what happened in this one case, and it makes no comparative or wrongdoing inference. The symmetry control in the SPEC (Bofors beside Rafale; UPA beside NDA) gives the same reading: the Rafale pricing was also sealed or redacted under an NDA government, and the court accepted it. No asymmetry is implied.
verdicts.denialFound: This is a court statement, not an accusation, so no denial applies. The government's position is on record. Per SC Observer (https://www.scobserver.in/reports/pegasus-spyware-probe-day-8-petitioners-demand-revelation-of-sealed-cover-report/), SG Tushar Mehta 'expressed strong reservations against disclosing the contents of the report, arguing that the sovereignty of the nation was at stake' and said 'terrorists cannot have a privacy right'. Petitioners (Kapil Sibal, Shyam Divan) asked for disclosure: 'It is an open Court system here.'
verdicts.innocentReading: The bench was not hiding wrongdoing. It applied the ordinary rule that material bearing on national security stays sealed. It offered a route for affected individuals: a yes/no answer on whether their device was infected, and release of the parts that concern them. The committee had already reported in Aug 2022 that Pegasus was not established on the 29 phones it examined. The remark 'To have spyware, there is nothing wrong. The question is against whom it is being used' is general legal commentary. It does not find that the government bought or used Pegasus.
verdicts.reason: The source holds. LawBeat quotes Kant J: 'Any court touching the security of the nation — we are not going to disclose a single word. Yes, when individuals are affected, that part we can release.' It also quotes: 'To have spyware, there is nothing wrong. The question is against whom it is being used.' The next date of 30 Jul 2025 matches. Business Standard/PTI ('Supreme Court says technical report on Pegasus will not be made public'), Verdictum and SC Observer report the same remarks independently. What fails is the framing, not the fact. These were oral observations at a hearing. None of the four outlets reports a written order recording non-disclosure, yet the record's 'd' calls it a 'Judicial ruling'. The flat label 'will not be made public' also drops the court's offer to release or confirm the parts that concern individuals. With one outlet in the record and only oral remarks, 'reported' is the right tier. Adding SC Observer and PTI/Business Standard as sources would meet the two-outlet test for 'documented' on the narrow fact that the remarks were made. It would not support calling them a ruling.
verdicts.corrections: d: replace 'Judicial ruling on money-people:c086' with 'Oral observations at hearing in WP(Crl) 314/2021 (no written order on non-disclosure located)'. lab: 'Supreme Court bench (Surya Kant, Kotiswar Singh JJ), 29 Apr 2025: national-security portions of committee report will not be disclosed; parts concerning affected individuals may be shared'. d: add that SG Tushar Mehta opposed disclosure on sovereignty grounds, and that the court proposed letting affected individuals ask for a yes/no answer. srcs: add SC Observer Day 8 report (https://www.scobserver.in/reports/pegasus-spyware-probe-day-8-petitioners-demand-revelation-of-sealed-cover-report/) and Business Standard/PTI (https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/supreme-court-says-technical-report-on-pegasus-will-not-be-made-public-125042900434_1.html). pred: 'enforce' is defined for cancellation, suspension, freeze, investigation, sanction or debarment, and a non-disclosure remark fits poorly. Consider recording it as a case-stage event and noting this in 'd'. Status: SC Observer shows the case pending as of Jul 2025. Check for any order from 30 Jul 2025 or later before publishing, and set 'supersededBy' if one exists.

verdicts.dateTest: Written as a claim: "the platform sets the Bofors case record (contract 24 Mar 1986, Congress) beside the Rafale case record (IGA 23 Sep 2016, BJP) using identical fields." Most Bofors dates check out. Swedish Radio 16 Apr 1987, CBI FIR 22 Jan 1990, chargesheet 22 Oct 1999 and the Delhi HC orders of 4 Feb 2004 and 31 May 2005 all match the file's sources (c055, c057, c058). The SC dismissal of 2 Nov 2018 matches National Herald. For the 2026 dismissal, DNA's date line reads 7 Aug 2026; c061 fixes it as 6 Aug from the weekday, and either date supports "2026". Rafale: SC 14 Dec 2018, review 14 Nov 2019 and CAG Report 3 of 2019 (2.86%) all match. The date test FAILS on the Rafale "first allegation" field. The claim says "first allegation Sep 2018", but the file's own source, Wikipedia's "Rafale deal controversy" page, records Congress (Manish Tewari) questioning the price on 24 Sep 2016, the day after signing. Randeep Surjewala and Rahul Gandhi made the Reliance/HAL allegation in Nov 2017, and Shourie, Sinha and Bhushan raised it on 8-9 Aug 2018. The file also cites Reliance's own 12 Aug 2018 rebuttal (Business Today), and a rebuttal cannot come before the allegation it answers. This field carries the symmetry: the gap from decision to allegation reads as about 13 months for Bofors and 24 months for Rafale, when the real Rafale figure is 1 day (price) or about 14 months (offset partner).
verdicts.identityTest: Both entities are correctly identified as case records. force:case-bofors is the US$285m, 410-howitzer contract of 24 Mar 1986, RC 1(A)/90. force:case-rafale is the 36-aircraft IGA of 23 Sep 2016, with WP(Crl) 225/2018 and Review Petition (Crl) 46/2019. No person below public rank is named, and there are no CIN or DIN issues. A minor point: "decision 2016" for Rafale is the signing date. The decision to buy 36 aircraft was announced in the joint statement of 10 Apr 2015, so for both cases the field should be labelled contract-signature date.
verdicts.baseRate: The claim is a symmetry control, not a property claim, so it does not raise a discriminating-property issue. In the file's seven-case set, 0 of 7 have a final conviction, so "convictions: 0" separates nothing. Likewise, almost every Indian defence-procurement controversy draws a government denial of wrongdoing, so a "common feature" built on government denial is close to 100% and tells the reader nothing about either case.
verdicts.denialFound: Bofors: on 20 Apr 1987 Rajiv Gandhi told the Lok Sabha that no kickbacks were paid and no middlemen were involved, and a PTI-circulated statement called the report "false, baseless and mischievous" (https://www.business-standard.com/article/current-affairs/rs-1-437-cr-india-sweden-bofors-guns-deal-timeline-of-the-31-year-old-case-117102100190_1.html ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bofors_scandal). This denial is not in the file. The only Bofors answer recorded there is the Hinduja counsel's 2005 submission (c056). Rafale: MoD said the government had no role in choosing the offset partner (The News Minute, 22 Sep 2018; The Quint), Dassault said the choice was its own (ThePrint), and Reliance said its contract came from Dassault (Business Today, 12 Aug 2018). Against the Nov 2021 Mediapart allegation of commissions to a middleman, the government and Dassault maintained that there was no corruption (https://theprint.in/defence/french-journal-mediapart-claims-cbi-ed-were-aware-of-kickbacks-in-rafale-deal/763068/).
verdicts.innocentReading: The comparison is a deliberate SPEC control ("Bofors beside Rafale; identical fields") and asserts no wrongdoing. The two records differ because the cases differ in kind and era. Bofors was a commercial contract with a criminal FIR and chargesheet. Rafale was a government-to-government agreement reviewed on writ petitions, with a CAG audit, and after 2018 any CBI probe needs s.17A prior approval. The claim's own innocentReading field states this adequately.
verdicts.reason: The claim is refuted as written, on two points. First, a load-bearing "identical field" is wrong: the claim's own cited source (Wikipedia, Rafale deal controversy) shows the first Rafale allegation came in Sep 2016 (price) or Nov 2017 (Reliance/HAL), not Sep 2018, and the file's own Business Today rebuttal of 12 Aug 2018 comes before the claimed date. Second, the "Common feature" sentence stretches two different things into one. In Bofors the government denied that any intermediaries or kickbacks existed (Rajiv Gandhi, Lok Sabha, 20 Apr 1987, which the file does not source). In Rafale the government denied having any role in choosing the offset partner. The sentence also leaves out Rafale's own intermediary allegation (Mediapart, Nov 2021, Sushen Gupta, EUR 7.5m, CBI/ED said to hold the material since Oct 2018) and so understates the parallel. A further asymmetry: Bofors's CAG field is "not retrieved" while Rafale's CAG field carries a favourable finding, even though a CAG report on the gun deal exists (tabled 1989). As a control, the tier stays analytic once the fields are fixed.
verdicts.corrections: 1. c091.d and force:case-rafale.d: change Rafale's "first allegation Sep 2018" to "first public allegation 24 Sep 2016 (Congress, price); Reliance/HAL allegation Nov 2017 (Rahul Gandhi, Surjewala); Hollande remark via Mediapart 21 Sep 2018". Source: Wikipedia, Rafale deal controversy, reported. 2. Rewrite the "Common feature" sentence as: "Common feature: an allegation about an intermediary (Bofors 1987; Rafale, Mediapart Nov 2021) or an offset partner (Rafale 2017-18), each denied by the government of the day. Bofors: Rajiv Gandhi told the Lok Sabha on 20 Apr 1987 that no middlemen were involved. Rafale: MoD said it had no role in choosing the offset partner." Add a source for the Bofors denial (Business Standard timeline or Lok Sabha debates of 20 Apr 1987). 3. Add to the Rafale record: Mediapart's Nov 2021 allegation of EUR 7.5m in commissions to Sushen Gupta and its report that CBI/ED held the material from Oct 2018, tier alleged, with the government/Dassault denial as contra. 4. Bofors CAG field: record that the CAG report on the gun deal (1989) exists and was not opened, so the field is not left looking empty beside Rafale's favourable CAG finding. 5. Label the decision field "contract signed" for both cases, and note the Rafale 36-aircraft announcement of 10 Apr 2015. 6. Bofors 2026 SC dismissal: keep 6 Aug 2026 with c061's caveat (DNA's date line reads 7 Aug). 7. Add srcs to c091 (the two Wikipedia pages, the SC judgments, the Delhi HC 2005 judgment, the CAG Report 3 of 2019 PDF), since the comparison currently carries no sources of its own.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, rewritten: "the file sets AgustaWestland (decided 2010, UPA) and Tatra/BEML (UPA era) side by side on identical fields, as of Dec 2025." The AgustaWestland dates hold. The contract was signed in Feb 2010 with A K Antony as Defence Minister. The CBI FIR was filed 13 Mar 2013, the contract was cancelled in 2014, and the former Air Chief was arrested 9 Dec 2016. LawBeat confirms the 23 Dec 2025 order and quotes the special judge: "Despite expiry of more than seven years after the arrest of the accused Christian Michel James, the proceedings are at initial stage and charges are yet to be decided". The Tatra dates fail. Calling it "Tatra (BEML, UPA era)" contradicts the file's own source. Oneindia (26 Aug 2014) says: "Since 1986, the Indian Army has bought over 7,000 Tatra trucks." Pioneer (2019) says the alleged scam concerned purchases made before 2006 under the procurement manual of that time. The supply window therefore runs from 1986 (Congress) through 1998–2004 (NDA) into UPA. Only the bribe-offer meeting (22 Sep 2010) and the FIR (2012) fall in UPA years. The Tatra entity record also has no "decision-date and government at the time" field, which the AgustaWestland record does have.
verdicts.identityTest: The entities match their sources. The AgustaWestland record is the 12 AW101 contract, the former Air Chief is S P Tyagi, and the middleman is Christian Michel. Tribune (12 Jun 2012) supports the Tatra record: "The CBI registered a case after Defence Minister AK Antony asked it to look into the Tatra case. NRI Ravi Rishi has been booked", and it confirms that BEML CMD V R S Natarajan was suspended. Devdiscourse, ThePrint and the Tribune (28 Sep 2022) support the separate bribe-offer case against the retired Lt Gen (charges framed 2019; the Delhi HC dismissed his challenge 20–22 Jul 2022). One problem: the record puts two separate Tatra proceedings into one "case" column, the BEML/Vectra FIR with its closure report and the PC Act bribe-offer trial. The AgustaWestland column is a single case with several chargesheets, so the fields are not like for like.
verdicts.baseRate: Close to 100% of large Indian defence-procurement corruption cases have no conviction years after the FIR. That holds for Bofors (Hindujas discharged 2005), Barak, the HDW submarine case, the Scorpene leak case, AgustaWestland and Tatra. So "convictions 0" does not tell these cases apart, and it says nothing about this pair in particular. The other shared features also have a base rate near 100% for UPA-era scandals: a DM-ordered CBI probe, an intermediary, and a retired officer in the record. The comparison describes the cases; it does not point to anything.
verdicts.denialFound: Responses exist in the record. For AgustaWestland, the Milan retrial acquitted the executives on 8 Jan 2018 and Cassation upheld this in 2019; the Indian accused were not convicted, and Michel obtained bail from the SC on 18 Feb 2025 (Gulf News). For Tatra, the CBI filed its own closure report on 26 Aug 2014 (Oneindia). Antony said in cross-examination on 28 Sep 2022 that the Chief had not complained to the Ministry or handed over documents (Tribune). The retired Lt Gen contested the framing of charges. BEML's own response was not retrieved, and the file does not say whether BEML was asked. Contrary record omitted from c092: Daily Pioneer (2019, https://www.dailypioneer.com/2019/india/court-slams-cbi-and-def-ministry.html) reports that Special Judge Pulastya Pramachala had not accepted the closure report, called the CBI's failure to produce the pre-2006 procurement manual "shocking", and ordered the CBI Joint Director to report.
verdicts.innocentReading: The SPEC requires this pairing as a control (SPEC.md line 20; CONTRACT-force.md line 90). Its point is to show that two UPA-era defence corruption cases moved at the same slow pace with no conviction. That is a fact about the Indian courts, not about either government or vendor. The innocentReading already stored is adequate.
verdicts.reason: This should stay an analytic edge, but the text as written fails on three counts, so I am marking it refuted. (1) "Tatra (BEML, UPA era)" is wrong by the file's own source. Oneindia records purchases since 1986, and the alleged irregularities predate 2006, so the window covers Congress, NDA and UPA governments. The Tatra record also has no decision-date/government field, so the "identical fields" claim in the label is false. (2) It says "Both began with the then Defence Minister ordering a CBI probe". That contradicts the two entity records' own "first public allegation" fields: the Italian arrest of the Finmeccanica chief on 12 Feb 2013, and the Army Chief's 2012 disclosure. The DM's order came after each, as a response. (3) For the BEML case it gives the "CBI closure report 2014" as the latest stage. It leaves out that the special court had still not accepted that report in 2019 and criticised the CBI. Claim c076 in the same file already flags this. Leaving it out makes the Tatra column look more settled than the AgustaWestland column, which breaks the symmetry this control is there to test. Also, "convictions 0" for Tatra is not established: the file itself says "trial outcome not found".
verdicts.corrections: d: replace "Tatra (BEML, UPA era)" with "Tatra (BEML; Tatra trucks bought through BEML since 1986, spanning Congress, NDA and UPA governments; bribe-offer meeting 22 Sep 2010 and FIR 2012 under UPA-II)". Replace "CBI closure report 2014" with "CBI closure report 26 Aug 2014, which the special court had not accepted as of 2019 (Pioneer 2019)", and add https://www.dailypioneer.com/2019/india/court-slams-cbi-and-def-ministry.html to srcs. Replace "Both began with the then Defence Minister ordering a CBI probe" with "In both, the then Defence Minister referred the matter to the CBI after the first public allegation (the Italian arrest of Feb 2013; the Army Chief's 2012 disclosure)". Change Tatra "convictions 0" to "no conviction found in opened sources". Add a sentence that the Tatra column merges two proceedings (the BEML/Vectra FIR and the PC Act bribe-offer trial). Entity force:case-tatra: add the missing field "decision-date and government at the time: multiple contracts from 1986 onward; no single decision date" so its fields match force:case-agustawestland. lab: drop "identical fields" until the Tatra record has the decision-date field. Optionally add to the innocentReading that a near-100% no-conviction base rate across defence cases makes "convictions 0" non-discriminating.

verdicts.dateTest: The claim in standard form: the platform assigns 7 named cases to the government in office "at the decision date" (UPA 2004-14: 4, NDA 2014-: 2, pre-both: Bofors) and finds 0 final convictions as of Oct 2026. The convictions half checks out. Bofors: Delhi HC quashed the proceedings on 31 May 2005 (c058). Rafale: the SC dismissed the petitions in 2018 and the review in 2019. AgustaWestland: Italian acquittal on retrial on 8 Jan 2018, upheld by Cassation in 2019, and the Indian trial has no verdict. Tatra: CBI closure report on 26 Aug 2014, and the separate bribe-offer trial had charges framed in 2019, the HC refused to interfere in 2022, and no verdict was found. Adarsh: the Bombay HC quashed the sanction to prosecute on 22 Dec 2017, the SC stayed demolition, and Wikipedia says no final verdict as of 2024. Sukna: the AFT acquitted Lt Gen P K Rath on 5 Sep 2014 (Deccan Chronicle: 'acquitted ... of all charges that he had been found guilty of by an Army Court Martial'), and on 24 Jan 2019 the SC set aside Lt Gen Avadhesh Prakash's GCM dismissal (indiankanoon doc 156623410). Pegasus: the committee report is sealed. The decision-date half fails. Tatra is placed under UPA by its FIR date (2012), not by its decision date. The intermediary arrangement at the heart of the allegation is BEML's contract with Tatra Sipox UK, dated 1997 (United Front government) and renewed in 2003 under NDA-I, with Tatra supply going back to 1986 (Deccan Herald / IPA reporting). Adarsh is placed by its CAG date (2011). Its allotment and clearance decisions ran through the 2000s, were made largely by the Maharashtra Congress-NCP state government, and partly fell under NDA-I at the centre. The d field quietly switches to 'Decision or first allegation'. That mixed basis moves cases into the UPA column, so the label's own date key fails for at least Tatra.
verdicts.identityTest: The case entities are the correct ones. The Sukna court-martial outcomes cover both officers: Rath (AFT 2014) and Avadhesh Prakash (SC 2019, Sikri/Nazeer/Shah bench). The record correctly does not name them, since they are below the public rank. The edge endpoints s=force:case-sukna and t=force:case-pegasus are arbitrary. The claim compares seven cases, not Sukna and Pegasus, so the edge misrepresents what is being compared. Pegasus, Sukna and Adarsh are not defence-procurement cases, and the label's 'same fields' framing groups unlike case types together.
verdicts.baseRate: All 7 of 7 cases (100%) have no final conviction. That is well above the 80% threshold, so the property does not separate UPA from NDA. Fields that do separate the two columns: an FIR or criminal investigation was opened in 4 of 4 UPA-column cases and 0 of 2 NDA-column cases. The SC declined to order a probe into Rafale, and there is no FIR on Pegasus. In the UPA-column cases, investigation was ordered by UPA itself and continued under NDA. This is still a hand-picked set, not a sample. The claim says so itself.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable to the analytic comparison itself, and no denial is invented here. Relevant party positions found or in the record: both Sukna officers were vindicated by the AFT (2014) and the SC (2019). The Adarsh Society's answer to the Bombay HC is in c079. The Government of India denied any transaction with NSO; this is not opened here, so it is not cited by URL. The parties were not asked about this comparison.
verdicts.innocentReading: The seven cases are the famous ones, and which cases become famous depends on who is in opposition at the time. Older cases have had longer to reach a stage. Indian corruption prosecutions of senior officials rarely end in conviction under any government. Court-martial verdicts were set aside on procedure (GCM composition) and on findings that the proceedings were 'influenced and vitiated', not as a judgment on the government. Having no FIR (Rafale, Pegasus) and having an FIR without a conviction are different outcomes, but neither proves anyone guilty or innocent.
verdicts.reason: The '0 of 7 final convictions' count and the per-case stages are supported by the record and by independent reporting, including the Sukna AFT and SC rulings. The claim fails on its own grouping key, 'by government at the decision date'. Tatra's decision, the 1997 Tatra Sipox contract renewed in 2003 under NDA-I, falls outside UPA. Adarsh is keyed to its CAG report date rather than to the decisions, which were largely made by the state government. The d field switches to 'decision or first allegation', which shifts the columns toward UPA. The headline figure is also 100% shared, so it cannot tell the governments apart. The tier stays analytic once the corrections are applied.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Change lab/text from 'by government at the decision date' to 'by government at first allegation/FIR', or re-key every case by decision date: Tatra = 1986 first supply / 1997 Tatra Sipox contract / 2003 renewal (NDA-I), so it is not UPA; Adarsh = allotment and clearance decisions in the 2000s, mostly by the Maharashtra state government, overlapping NDA-I at the centre; AgustaWestland = 2010; Sukna = 2009; Rafale = 2016; Pegasus = 2017 alleged purchase / 2021 first allegation. 2) Add a column that actually separates the two sides: 'FIR/criminal investigation opened: UPA-column 4/4, NDA-column 0/2'. Note that the UPA-era probes were ordered by UPA's own Defence Minister or Army and were continued under NDA. 3) Rafale stage: add the French PNF judicial investigation opened in 2021 (status to verify); 'petitions dismissed' covers India only. 4) Replace the edge endpoints (case-sukna → case-pegasus) with a set-level node, or attach the claim to the symmetryCheck block, because the comparison is not between Sukna and Pegasus. 5) State that Sukna, Adarsh and Pegasus are not procurement cases. 6) Cite the Sukna outcomes as c084 (AFT 5 Sep 2014) and c085 (SC 24 Jan 2019, indiankanoon.org/doc/156623410), and do not name the officers in this claim.

verdicts.dateTest: Mahindra: the sources hold. The Mahindra press release says "The Ministry of Defence (MoD) has awarded a major contract to Mahindra Defence Systems Limited (MDS) worth Rs.1349.95 Cr" and is dated 27 Aug 2021. The MyNeta bond-level page shows all Mahindra & Mahindra bonds bought on 27/Jan/2023 and encashed by the BJP on 30 Jan and 7 Feb 2023. So the order came 17 months before the bonds, and a bond cannot have caused it. The later period (awards after Jan 2023) was not searched, so this test is only half done. Megha (MEIL): the file says there is no MoD award to MEIL. That is wrong at group level. On 15 Jun 2023 the MoD signed a contract worth about Rs 500 cr, Buy (Indian) category, with ICOMM Tele Ltd, a MEIL group company, for 1,035 radio-relay containers (reported by Statesman, BW Businessworld, MEIL's own release and Global Trade Alert; the PIB release was not opened). MEIL's BJP bond purchases fall both before it (2023-04-11) and after it (2023-10-11/12). But MEIL bought bonds in almost every sale window from Apr 2019 to Oct 2023, for nine parties. A steady pattern like that does not single out the ICOMM order. Cyient: no order was dated, so nothing could be tested.
verdicts.identityTest: The bond buyers do not match the contract winners. Mahindra & Mahindra Ltd (the parent) bought the bonds, but Mahindra Defence Systems Ltd (a subsidiary) won the order. MEIL bought the bonds, but ICOMM Tele Ltd (a group company) won the MoD order. Cyient Ltd bought the bonds; its defence line is a segment plus Cyient DLM, which listed separately, and the share of defence in the donor's business is not established. "Defence and security vendors" therefore describes one documented MoD vendor at subsidiary level (Mahindra), one group-level MoD vendor (MEIL via ICOMM) and one firm with a defence segment (Cyient). The headline generalises from that to a whole class.
verdicts.baseRate: The headline figures recompute correctly. Rs 619 cr out of Rs 1,001 cr is 61.8% to the BJP. Rs 5,594.20 cr out of Rs 12,145.88 cr is 46.1% (confirmed on the MyNeta party-wise page: BJP Rs 55,94,20,11,000). My parse of the MEIL page gave 467/773 bonds to the BJP (60.4%); the page shows about 4 in 5 rows, and this is consistent with 584/966. The three-donor sample is not discriminating. 29.1% of all 1,280 donors gave only to the BJP, and 73.7% of donors of Rs 10 cr or more gave to it at least once. Two out of three defence-linked donors giving only to the BJP is not distinguishable from that base. Symmetry: MEIL gave Rs 382 cr to eight other parties (BRS, DMK, YSRCP, TDP, Congress, JD(U), JD(S), Janasena), mostly parties running states, in the same windows and denominations. The same "bonds for orders" reading would apply equally to those parties for state contracts. No award series was built for bond buyers and non-buyers alike (L&T, Tata Advanced Systems, Bharat Forge, the DPSUs), so the DPSU/private-vendor control in the SPEC was not run.
verdicts.denialFound: None found from Mahindra & Mahindra, MEIL/ICOMM or Cyient about these bonds; they were not asked, and the file records no request. The strongest counter on record is missing from the narrative. On 2 Aug 2024 the Supreme Court (Common Cause and CPIL v Union of India) dismissed petitions seeking a court-monitored SIT probe into alleged electoral-bond quid pro quo. The bench said the allegations were assumptions at that stage, and that an SIT should not be ordered when ordinary criminal-procedure remedies had not been used (LiveLaw: https://www.livelaw.in/top-stories/supreme-court-dismisses-pleas-for-sit-investigation-into-electoral-bonds-quid-pro-quo-says-ordinary-remedies-not-invoked-265451 ; Business Today: https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/electoral-bonds-supreme-court-rejects-plea-for-sit-investigation-into-quid-pro-quo-use-of-bonds-by-political-parties-439891-2024-08-02). I found no named party alleging specifically that defence vendors bought bonds to win defence orders. The public allegations about MEIL concern infrastructure contracts, not MoD orders.
verdicts.innocentReading: Large conglomerates bought bonds every quarter for whichever parties held power at the Centre and in the states where they operate. MEIL's spread across nine parties and nearly every sale window fits political hedging or general access-buying, not payment for particular defence orders. The Mahindra order came out of an open tender with sea trials, according to Mahindra's own release, and was signed 17 months before the bond. Cyient's Rs 10 cr in Nov 2023 is matched to no order. The party in power at the Centre gets the largest share of every donor class, defence-linked or not.
verdicts.reason: The narrative joins individually documented facts (A bought bonds; A's subsidiary or group company got an MoD order) into a proposition that none of the sources states ("to win orders"). The one date test that was run, Mahindra, points the wrong way: the order came 17 months before the bond. The defence-linked donor share of BJP bonds is not distinguishable from the all-donor base. The headline also overstates "defence and security vendors" from a sample of three. As a proposition it is refuted; it survives only as an analytic record that carries its innocent reading and does not imply wrongdoing. The record also has a factual omission (ICOMM's MoD contract of 15 Jun 2023, which matters to both the strongest case and the date test) and it understates the Supreme Court's position in two ways: (1) the Feb 2024 judgment held there is a "legitimate possibility that financial contribution to a political party would lead to quid pro quo arrangements" and noted the Solicitor General "did not deny" that corporate donations are made for favours; (2) the Aug 2024 order refused an SIT, calling the quid pro quo claims assumptions. Its status should be "unsupported by the records in hand", not "contested", unless a named party making the defence-specific allegation is found.
verdicts.corrections: 1. Change status "contested" to "unsupported (no record links a bond to an order)", or name the party who makes the defence-specific allegation. As it stands, no alleger is cited, so the alleged tier is not available. 2. Add to strongestCase: "MEIL group company ICOMM Tele Ltd signed a ~Rs 500 cr MoD contract (Buy-Indian, 1,035 radio-relay containers) on 15 Jun 2023; MEIL bought BJP bonds on 2023-04-11 and 2023-10-11/12." Source: the PIB release of 15 Jun 2023 (find and open it), with https://meil.in/icomm-bags-rs-500-crore-order-defence-ministry and https://www.businessworld.in/article/Defence-Ministry-Signs-Rs-500-Cr-Contract-For-Communication-System/16-06-2023-480711/ as backup. Also correct claim c009–c017 field d: "no MoD award to MEIL is in this file" should read "a MEIL group company (ICOMM) holds a 15 Jun 2023 MoD contract; the bond buyer is MEIL itself". 3. Add to strongestCounter: "the Supreme Court on 2 Aug 2024 dismissed pleas (Common Cause, CPIL) for an SIT into alleged bond quid pro quo, calling the allegations assumptions at that stage" (LiveLaw URL above). 4. Replace "the Supreme Court ... did not find a quid pro quo" with "the Supreme Court (15 Feb 2024) held there is a 'legitimate possibility' that contributions lead to quid pro quo but adjudicated no specific donor-order link". 5. Reword "Megha Rs 966 cr (Rs 584 cr to the BJP), Mahindra & Mahindra Rs 25 cr and Cyient Rs 10 cr, all to the BJP" as "...; Mahindra (Rs 25 cr) and Cyient (Rs 10 cr) gave only to the BJP", so it does not read as though all of MEIL's bonds went to the BJP. 6. State the parent/subsidiary/group mismatch (M&M vs MDSL; MEIL vs ICOMM) in the narrative itself. 7. Record denialFound as "not asked" for M&M, MEIL and Cyient. 8. Re-examine the Force Motors void: check whether Force Motors holds Army orders (Gurkha) before excluding it from the defence-linked set, since it bought Rs 6.35 cr, all to the BJP.

verdicts.dateTest: The two cases in the record do not overlap the cooling-off window. (1) Avinash Chander was DG DRDO / Secretary DDR&D from 2013 until his contract was ended on 31 Jan 2015. The government ended it early: Wikipedia says DoPT "advised his contract to end due to poor performance". He was appointed to the Astra Microwave board on 29-01-2018 (AR 2020-21, raw text: "1. Dr. Avinash Chander 05288690 29-01-2018"). The gap is about 3 years, against a one-year rule. Under that civil rule, which is not the armed-forces rule, a Group A officer needs permission for commercial employment within one year. He became Chairman later: MarketScreener gives 31 Mar 2019. The narrative's "chairs the board ... since 2018-01-29" mixes up the date he joined as a director with the date he became chairman. (2) F. H. Major was Chief of the Air Staff from 31 Mar 2007 to 31 May 2009. Wikipedia says "Independent Director at Reliance Defence and Engineering Limited since 2016". The Mar 2015 additional-director date comes only from search summaries. Either way the role began about 5y9m to 6y9m after he retired, well outside the window. The BSE filing of 27 Nov 2024 lists the board reconstituted on 08 Dec 2023 and does not name Major, so the narrative's present tense ("sits on") is unverified and probably wrong.
verdicts.identityTest: Chander: DIN 05288690 matches the Astra AR 2020-21 director table, and the skills matrix confirms the person: "He is the retired Secretary, Defence R&D and Director General, DRDO." Identity holds. Major: identified only by office and dates on Wikipedia. No DIN is given. The company was then Pipavav Defence / Reliance Defence & Engineering, not "Reliance Naval and Engineering", and no primary filing naming him was opened. The cited BSE PDF does not mention him. Wikipedia's own citation is an archived reliancedefence.co board page, which I could not reach (the archive.org connection was reset). Identity is plausible but not established from a primary record.
verdicts.baseRate: None was computed. The record's own base-rate row is 0/2 ("documented roles located ... not a sample"). There is no denominator: no list of retired chiefs, Vice Chiefs or DG DRDOs from 2000 to 2026, and no count of how many joined vendor boards, inside or outside the window. The DPSU control in the SPEC (private vendor beside the competing DPSU) was not run. The record's scope says "Leaves out ... DPSU board scans". The only board control is Bharat Forge's board page, which shows none. Two hand-picked cases cannot discriminate in either direction, so neither the narrative nor its rebuttal rests on a rate. Symmetry: both appointments came under the NDA.
