Major's predecessor era (UPA) was not scanned, and neither was the 2012 Standing Committee's UPA-era concern about middlemen, so the UPA-II/NDA control is also missing.
verdicts.denialFound: None found. I did not ask. Neither Chander, Major, Astra Microwave nor Reliance was asked, and no outlet has put an allegation to them. A search found no reporting that alleges impropriety in either appointment (Fali Major search: Wikipedia, Bharat Rakshak, a Business Standard report on the R-Infra takeover of Pipavav; no controversy about the board seat). With no allegation there is nothing to deny, and that absence is the record.
verdicts.innocentReading: Listed defence-electronics and shipbuilding firms are expected by SEBI LODR to fill independent-director seats with people who have relevant expertise, and the pool of people with senior missile, radar or air-acquisition experience is almost entirely retired officers and DRDO scientists. Astra's skills matrix lists Chander's DRDO background as the reason for his seat. Both appointments came years after retirement, outside the cooling-off rule. Chander had been removed early by the same government, which does not fit a "reward" from government. The real issue the narrative points at is lobbying and middlemen. The documented source for that is the 2012 Standing Committee statement quoted by PTI, which is generic and names no one.
verdicts.reason: The claim's causal core ("as a reward or for access") has no source. None of the four sources says any retired officer or scientist got a board seat as a reward or for access. The PTI/Shillong Times piece quotes the Standing Committee: "some of the retired defence officers work with the private sector and act as a middlemen for defence procurement". That is a generic concern, names no one, and does not support the reward-or-access mechanism. Antony also said "Retired officers of the army or bureaucrats work for Indian companies, foreign companies". The two named cases both fall outside the cooling-off window, there is no base rate, and the DPSU and UPA-II controls were not run. On top of that, the strongestCase overstates its evidence. It labels the Air Chief's board seat "Documented", but the record's own claim c029 rates it "reported" (Wikipedia only, with the annual report not opened). It uses the present tense ("sits") for a board that was reconstituted in Dec 2023. And it dates Chander's chairmanship from his appointment as a director. The entry should stay as an analytic narrative, with its status lowered and its wording fixed. It does not belong at any evidentiary tier above analytic. Killing it is not needed: it is a real circulating concern with a documented parliamentary origin. But because no one has alleged anything against Chander or Major, the narrative should not lead with them as its illustration.
verdicts.corrections: 1) status: lower "speculative" to "unsupported", or keep "speculative" with the explicit note "no source alleges reward or access in any named case". 2) strongestCase: lead with the documented generic evidence: the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Defence report tabled 30 Apr 2012, quoted by PTI 3 May 2012: "some of the retired defence officers work with the private sector and act as a middlemen for defence procurement", plus its recommendation of 5 years for Brigadier and above (Antony in the Rajya Sabha, 2 May 2012). 3) Change "a former DG DRDO chairs the board ... (Astra Microwave, since 2018-01-29)" to "a former DG DRDO (contract ended early 31 Jan 2015) has been an independent director of Astra Microwave since 29 Jan 2018 (DIN 05288690, AR 2020-21) and its Chairman from 31 Mar 2019 (reported, MarketScreener; primary filing to be opened)". 4) Change "Documented: ... a former Air Chief sits on a listed shipbuilder's board (Reliance Naval and Engineering, from 2015/2016)" to "Reported (Wikipedia only): F. H. Major was an independent director of Reliance Defence & Engineering (formerly Pipavav Defence) 'since 2016'; end date unverified; that board was reconstituted 08 Dec 2023 and the BSE filing of 27 Nov 2024 does not list him". Drop "Documented" and "sits". 5) strongestCounter: add "Chander's DRDO contract was ended early by the government, which cuts against a 'reward' reading", and "neither the UPA-II/NDA control nor the DPSU-board control was run". 6) Remove the Reliance BSE 27 Nov 2024 filing as support for Major's role (in c029), because it does not name him. Either open the FY2015-16/2016-17 Reliance Defence annual report for DIN and appointment date, or keep c029 at "reported". 7) whatWouldChangeThis: specify the denominator as every retired service chief, Vice Chief and DG DRDO from 2000 to 2026, against the board lists of listed defence vendors and DPSUs, split by UPA-II/NDA era.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated as: CBI / successive Union governments failed to prosecute alleged commissions on the 24 Mar 1986 Bofors contract, 1990 to 2026. The dates check out against the record. FIR 22.1.1990 and chargesheet 22.10.1999 are quoted in the Delhi HC judgment of 31 May 2005 (indiankanoon 230231). Kapoor J's judgment is dated 4.2.2004, and Sodhi J says it "quashed all charges under the Prevention of Corruption Act and bribery". Sodhi J's order is 31.5.2005. The CMM allowed withdrawal under s.321 against Quattrocchi on 04.03.2011; the application was filed 03.10.2009. The SC dismissed the CBI SLP on 2 Nov 2018 (National Herald: "over 4,500 days' delay"). The exact figure of 4,522 days does not appear in the cited National Herald piece, but Republic and Business Standard (Aug 2026) print it. The SC dismissed Ajay Agarwal's appeal on 6 Aug 2026 (Business Standard, The Federal, Republic). The window covers both governments, so the timing is symmetric. The 1999 chargesheet came under NDA. The failure to appeal in 2004–05, the release of the London accounts in 2005–06, the withdrawal of the Red Corner Notice and the s.321 withdrawal (2009–11) came under UPA. The late SLP of 2018 came under NDA. The narrative's "system" framing is fair across parties.
verdicts.identityTest: Entities match the court records: RC-1(A)/90, AB Bofors, the Hinduja brothers (Crl. Rev. 271/272 of 2004), and CBI v Ottavio Quattrocchi before CMM Vinod Yadav. The contract value is wrong. The narrative says "US$285 m contract", a figure taken from Wikipedia's timeline, which cites a Yahoo news piece. The primary record in the file's own source (CMM order, 4 Mar 2011) says: "a total cost of SEK 8,410,660,984 [equivalent approximately to Rs. 1437.72 crores (as per the exchange rate on March 21, 1986...)". At 1986 rates that is roughly US$1.1–1.2 bn, not $285 m. The Hinduja brothers are named as court parties. They are private individuals, though they are directors of a business group, so keep them only as the court record names them.
verdicts.baseRate: Ending without a conviction does not discriminate. None of the seven defence cases in this file reached a final conviction, and Indian defence-procurement corruption cases rarely end in one. The features that do set Bofors apart are rare and documented. (1) The CBI did not appeal within limitation for 4,522 days, and per 2026 reporting its own explanation was that officers favoured an SLP but approval "had not been received from the competent authority". (2) The Union, through the Additional Solicitor General, asked the UK in Dec 2005 to release Quattrocchi's frozen London accounts. (3) The Red Corner Notice was withdrawn; the CMM order para 85 records the ASG's argument for this. (4) The prosecution withdrew under s.321. No other case in the file has this cluster. So "contested" is the right status, not "unsupported".
verdicts.denialFound: Responses on record. Rajiv Gandhi told Parliament in 1987 that neither he nor his family received any consideration; this is widely reported, but no URL was opened here. The Delhi HC on 4.2.2004 exonerated "the late Shri Rajiv Gandhi and Shri S.K. Bhatnagar" (quoted in https://indiankanoon.org/doc/230231/). The Hinduja side argued the CBI ran "a persecution based on a political agenda" (same judgment, para 12). On the cover-up limb, the CMM order records the ASG's argument that "the Red Corner Notice was withdrawn against 'Q', after the approval of Attorney General of India, as it was impinging very heavily upon the exchequer" (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/114666204/, para 85). Per 2026 reporting, the CBI said SLP approval was not received from the competent authority (Business Standard, 7 Aug 2026). The narrative does not record any of these responses on the cover-up limb; it should.
verdicts.innocentReading: The case may have failed on evidence rather than through suppression. The Swiss documents proved payments to AE Services, Svenska and McIntyre, but not that they were tied to the contract. Key accused died (Chadha and Bhatnagar in 2001, Ardbo, Quattrocchi in 2013). Malaysian (2002) and Argentine (2007) courts refused extradition. After 14 years and about Rs 250 crore, prosecutors and law officers may have judged that further pursuit cost more than it could recover; the s.321 withdrawal was approved as proper by the CMM. On this reading, the non-appeal and withdrawal are ordinary prosecutorial triage.
verdicts.corrections:
1. strongestCase: replace "a US$285 m contract" with "the SEK 8,410,660,984 (about Rs 1,437.72 crore) contract of 24 Mar 1986 (CMM order, 4 Mar 2011)". Make the same fix in the edge description on force:ab-bofors, which says "Rupee value not verified"; it is verified in the CMM order.

2. strongestCase: add the documented cover-up elements:
   - Dec 2005: the ASG asked the UK to release Quattrocchi's frozen London accounts.
   - The Red Corner Notice was withdrawn with the AG's approval (CMM order, para 85).
   - The CBI's 2000 note to the Swiss authorities said the McIntyre payments were not connected to the contract (Delhi HC 2005, para 39).
   - The CBI explained the 4,522-day delay as SLP approval not received from the competent authority.
   - Jan 2011: the ITAT held that Rs 41 crore was paid to Chadha and Quattrocchi (Tribune, 4–5 Jan 2011, reported tier).

3. strongestCounter: replace "no court found a payment proved" with "payments to AE Services, Svenska and McIntyre are established, but no criminal court found them to be bribes linked to the contract or to a public servant, and no one was convicted". Add the evidentiary-failure innocent reading: accused died, and the Malaysian (2002) and Argentine (2007) extraditions failed.

4. Cite the "4,522 days" figure to Business Standard or Republic (Aug 2026), since National Herald says only "over 4,500 days". Alternatively, write "over 4,500 days".

5. Replace the DNA source, which returns 403 here, with Business Standard (https://www.business-standard.com/india-news/sc-closes-bofors-case-rejects-final-plea-against-2005-hinduja-acquittal-126080700519_1.html) or The Federal (https://thefederal.com/category/news/supreme-court-dismisses-final-bofors-case-appeal-brings-legal-battle-to-an-end-252770). Both confirm the 6 Aug 2026 dismissal by Pardiwala and Vinod Chandran JJ.

6. Add the responses to the record (the ASG's cost rationale and the CBI's approval explanation), so that the cover-up limb carries the other side's answer.

7. Set the tier to analytic (the platform's own weighing; status stays contested) and attach an innocentReading field.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: "MoD (Defence Minister Manohar Parrikar, in office 2014-11-09 to 2017-03-13) signed the 36-Rafale IGA and offset contracts on 2016-09-23, and Dassault formed DRAL with Reliance on 2017-02-10." The signature falls inside Parrikar's tenure and the NDA window. The joint statement (10 Apr 2015), RFP withdrawal (Jun 2015), Hollande remark (Mediapart, 21 Sep 2018), MoD denial (22 Sep 2018), Dassault statement (10 Oct 2018), SC dismissal (14 Dec 2018), CAG tabling (13 Feb 2019) and SC review (14 Nov 2019) are all in the right order. The SC 2018 judgment, para 25, says "the report of the CAG has been examined by the Public Accounts Committee". That statement came before the CAG report was tabled on 13 Feb 2019. The 2019 review judgment records that the Government asked for this to be corrected ("order for correction"). The narrative's description of the mismatch holds. No chronology fault.
verdicts.identityTest: The entities match the sources. "Reliance Defence Ltd" is named in the MoD release and the BT/Reliance statement. Dassault Reliance Aerospace Ltd (DRAL) is named by Dassault. The two judgments are WP(Crl) 225/2018 (Manohar Lal Sharma, 14 Dec 2018) and RP(Crl) 46/2019 in WP(Crl) 298/2018 (Yashwant Sinha, 14 Nov 2019). The audit is CAG Report No. 3 of 2019 (Performance Audit), Vol II. One discrepancy: BT has Reliance's CEO saying "Dassault holds a 49 per cent stake" in DRAL. The narrative makes no claim about the stake split, so nothing in it is wrong.
verdicts.baseRate: Allegations of overpricing or favoritism follow almost every large Indian defence import: Bofors, HDW, Barak, Scorpene, AgustaWestland, Tatra, Rafale. That makes "an allegation exists" non-discriminating (≥80% of big-ticket imports). In 2016–18 private Indian offset partners chosen by the OEM were the norm under DPP 2013/2016 offset guidelines, so "OEM chose a private group" is not discriminating either. What would discriminate is how this partner was chosen: a group with no aerospace track record, a JV formed after the IGA, and the Hollande remark. The narrative's strongestCase rests on these. The symmetry control holds. File claim c091 runs Bofors beside Rafale with identical fields. The Mediapart 2021 material (alleged €7.5m to Sushen Gupta, 2007–2012) points at the UPA period, so the same lens also lands on the rival government.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it is recorded with sources. MoD, 22 Sep 2018 (TNM): "The Government has stated earlier and again reiterates that it had no role in the selection of Reliance Defence as the Offset partner" (https://www.thenewsminute.com/news/rafale-row-centre-reacts-says-it-played-no-role-selection-reliance-88802). Dassault, 10 Oct 2018 (ThePrint): "Dassault Aviation has freely chosen to make a partnership with India's Reliance Group" (https://theprint.in/defence/picking-reliance-as-partner-was-our-choice-dassault-says-again-after-new-rafale-row/132659/). Reliance Defence CEO, 12 Aug 2018 (BT): Dassault "chose Reliance Defence Ltd to meet its 'offset'"; Dassault's offset share was "about 25 per cent" (https://www.businesstoday.in/...109401-2018-08-12). One omission: on 22 Sep 2018 Hollande told AFP he did not know whether India had pressured Dassault and "only Dassault can comment on this" (https://scroll.in/article/895491/no-french-ex-president-hollande-did-not-deny-his-rafale-remarks-to-afp-heres-what-he-said).
verdicts.innocentReading: The 126-MMRCA talks stalled for more than three years over HAL's responsibility for 108 licence-built aircraft. Government then switched to a 36-aircraft fly-away IGA for speed. Under the offset guidelines the OEM picks its Indian partners, and Dassault picked a large Indian group to build a Nagpur facility. CAG aligned the 2007 bid to the 2016 scope and found the 2016 contract 2.86% cheaper. The price was redacted under Article 10 of the IGA and the 2008 Indo-French classified-information agreement, not to hide anything. The Supreme Court found "no occasion to really doubt the process".
verdicts.reason: Every cited source says what the narrative says. SC 2018, para 4: Hollande's remark "seems to have triggered" the petitions. SC 2018: "there is no occasion to really doubt the process". The PAC sentence is in para 25, and the 2019 review judgment shows it was corrected. CAG Vol II, p.129: MoD's 15 Jan 2019 letter sought redaction; "Ministry was intimated about CAG's reluctance/refusal to carry out the redaction of price information… Ministry has strongly reiterated their stand". CAG: "signed in 2016 for 'U' million € which was 2.86 per cent lower than Audit's aligned price". Dassault: DRAL "created February 10, 2017". The record is framed as a contested narrative, gives both sides with the accused parties' recorded answers, and runs the Bofors control. It does not assert the allegation as fact, so it is not refuted. The thesis itself (overpriced plus a crony offset) rests on assertions by named parties: petitioners, the Congress, and Hollande's remark, which he qualified the next day. No court or auditor has found it, so it belongs at "alleged" with contra, not higher. The weakness is balance, not falsity. The strongestCase gives no evidence at all for the "overpriced" half. It also leaves out the most-cited offset-crony material that came after 2018.
verdicts.corrections:
1. strongestCase, add the overpricing evidence (each item needs its source). (a) CAG Vol II itself: the vendor's bank-guarantee savings ("AAB3" million €) "should have been passed on to Ministry", and France refused an escrow account. Same CAG PDF, approx. p.140–142. (b) Petitioners' objections, as recorded in the SC 14 Nov 2019 review judgment: parallel PMO negotiation "strenuously objected to by the Indian Negotiating Team", and the dissent within the INT. (c) The Hindu's Feb 2019 reports on per-aircraft cost escalation and waived anti-corruption clauses, tiered as reported, one outlet.
2. strongestCase/whatWouldChangeThis: add that Mediapart reported in Nov 2021 an alleged ≥€7.5m paid by Dassault to Sushen Gupta in 2007–2012, and that CBI/ED did not open a case. Note that this period is UPA-era, for symmetry. Add that the French PNF opened a judicial inquiry on 14 Jun 2021 (corruption, influence peddling, favoritism) and that its status as of 2026 is unknown. Sources: ThePrint https://theprint.in/defence/india-rafale-deal-under-scanner-in-france-judge-appointed-to-probe-alleged-corruption-reports/689233/ and The Week https://www.theweek.in/news/india/2021/11/08/cbi-was-aware-of-kickbacks-in-rafale-deal-alleges-french-journal.html.
3. strongestCounter: add Hollande's 22 Sep 2018 AFP statement that he did not know whether India pressured Dassault ("only Dassault can comment on this"). Also add Reliance's claim that Dassault's share of the offsets was about 25%, against the opposition's 'Rs 30,000 crore' figure.
4. srcs: add a source for the Hollande remark itself, e.g. The Quint link already used on c063, or Scroll.
5. The narrative's claim text should state the tier it rests on: allegations by petitioners and the Congress, not found by the SC or CAG. Keep status "contested".

verdicts.dateTest: The claim, put in the actor/act/thing/date form: AgustaWestland (AgustaWestland International Ltd / AgustaWestland SpA, Finmeccanica-owned) allegedly paid bribes, through intermediaries, to Indian officials to win the AW101 VVIP contract signed 8 Feb 2010 (LawBeat and Gulf News: "signed on February 8, 2010"). The alleged payments are dated 2006-07 (Wikipedia, citing the CBI). That falls inside Defence Minister A K Antony's window (2006-10-26 to 2014-05-26, c036). S. P. Tyagi was Air Chief from 2004-12-31 to 2007-03-31 (c030). He overlaps the alleged payment period and the specification change. He does not overlap the 2010 signing. The narrative correctly attributes the "specification changes before his tenure" point to his side. All the sequence dates check against the sources: Orsi arrested 12 Feb 2013, CBI FIR 13 Mar 2013, contract cancelled Jan 2014, Milan appeal conviction 8 Apr 2016, Cassation annulled it 16 Dec 2016, Tyagi arrested 9 Dec 2016, chargesheet Sep 2017, Milan retrial acquittal 8 Jan 2018, final acquittal 22 May 2019 (Defense News), charges still not framed on 23 Dec 2025 (LawBeat). One phrasing fix: "after seven years" counts from Michel's arrest (Dec 2018). The FIR is now more than 12 years old.
verdicts.identityTest: The entities match. The actor is AgustaWestland: AgustaWestland International Ltd is the contracting party named in the cancellation ("breach of the Pre-contract Integrity Pact and the agreement by AWIL"), and its parent was Finmeccanica, now Leonardo. The Italian defendants were Giuseppe Orsi (Finmeccanica CEO) and Bruno Spagnolini (head of AgustaWestland). The Indian accused are the former Air Chief S. P. Tyagi, his relatives, and the intermediaries Michel, Haschke, Gerosa and Saxena. One identity gap: the 2016 Italian appeal conviction and the 2018/2019 acquittals concern the executives. Separately, AgustaWestland SpA and AgustaWestland Ltd themselves settled in Italy in 2014 (see corrections). The narrative leaves out that corporate-level record, even though the company is the claim's own actor.
verdicts.baseRate: There is no meaningful population denominator for this. Within the brief's seven cases (c093), final convictions are 0 of 7, so "no conviction" does not set AgustaWestland apart. What does set it apart, among the seven, is this combination: the government that signed the contract cancelled it for an integrity-pact breach and encashed the guarantees; the vendor's own subsidiaries paid a court-approved settlement with confiscation; and the sitting Defence Minister publicly said bribes were taken. Rafale has none of these. Bofors has a chargesheet but no corporate settlement. On symmetry, the brief's Bofors-beside-Rafale control and the UPA-beside-NDA control get identical fields (c092/c093). This is a UPA-era case that the opposition of the day (BJP) uses as a weapon, and the mirror image of Rafale. Both narratives are marked "contested". That is defensible here only because the Italian acquittals are final. As written, the strongestCase understates AgustaWestland's adverse record compared with Rafale's.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, from several parties. (1) Orsi's lawyer Ennio Amodio after the final acquittal: "the Indian authorities will have to take note of the fact that at the end of a very detailed probe it was found there had never been any corruption" (https://www.defensenews.com/industry/2019/05/22/former-leonardo-ceo-gets-final-acquittal-in-helicopter-kickback-case/). (2) Christian Michel denied wrongdoing ("never met any Gandhi") and alleged the CBI pressured him to sign a confession, which the CBI denied (Wikipedia; Gulf News 18 Feb 2025). (3) Sanjeev 'Julie' Tyagi denied any link to the deal, and S. P. Tyagi's side relies on the specification change predating his tenure (Wikipedia, Shashindra Pal Tyagi). (4) Finmeccanica: the prosecutor "discontinued investigations against Finmeccanica acknowledging the non-involvement of the Company" (https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/finmeccanica-the-italian-judge-accepts-the-requests-made-by-agustawestland-to-bring-to-an-end-the-indian-case). (5) The UPA government "initially denied all allegations" (Wikipedia). None of these were asked by us; they are on the public record.
verdicts.innocentReading: Commission payments to agents and consultants on a 556 million euro contract were described as bribes by Italian prosecutors. On the full evidence, the Italian courts found it insufficient to prove corruption: Busto Arsizio in 2014 acquitted Orsi and Tyagi of corruption; the Milan retrial acquitted in 2018; Cassation made that final in 2019; and Brescia acquitted Haschke on 30 Jun 2025. The 2014 corporate settlement (patteggiamento) is not an admission of guilt under Italian law and may have been a commercial decision to close the case. India's cancellation rested on breach of the integrity pact (undisclosed agents), which is a lower bar than proof of bribery. The Indian case is still before charge framing after 12 years, so in India nothing has been tested.
verdicts.reason: Lens A: the narrative's assertions check against its four sources. LawBeat: "Despite expiry of more than seven years after the arrest of the accused Christian Michel James, the proceedings are at initial stage and charges are yet to be decided". Gulf News: "New Delhi cancelled a deal... after allegations the firm paid bribes", with three chargesheets and the investigation "still ongoing". Wikipedia: cancellation "on grounds of breach of the Pre-contract Integrity Pact"; 8 Apr 2016 conviction; Cassation annulled it 16 Dec 2016; 8 Jan 2018 acquittal; 22 May 2019 final acquittal. Lens B: the narrative is framed as a narrative with a case and a counter, not asserted as fact. "Contested" is the right status, since the Italian acquittals are final and India has not framed charges, while documented adverse facts stand. It therefore survives. It is weakened by omissions on both sides, not refuted. The strongestCase leaves out the two strongest documented items: the minister's statement and the August 2014 corporate settlement with 7.5 million euros confiscated, which is a primary Leonardo record. The strongestCounter leaves out the October 2014 Busto Arsizio first-instance acquittal on corruption and the 2025 Haschke acquittal. The sources are all secondary (Wikipedia, plus one outlet each), so any component edge stays at alleged/reported. That matches c071 (alleged) with contra c072.
verdicts.corrections: narrative:4 strongestCase, add: "Defence Minister A K Antony, 25 Mar 2013: 'Yes, corruption has taken place in the helicopter deal and bribes have been taken' (India Today, via Wikipedia); on 28 Aug 2014 the Busto Arsizio GIP accepted a settlement in which AgustaWestland SpA paid a 80,000 euro fine and AgustaWestland Ltd a 300,000 euro fine plus 7.5 million euros confiscated (Leonardo press release); India encashed the bank guarantees and recovered about Rs 1,620 crore+ (Wikipedia)." strongestCounter, add: "Busto Arsizio acquitted Orsi and Tyagi of corruption in Oct 2014; Brescia appeals court acquitted the alleged middleman Haschke on 30 Jun 2025 (Reuters); the 2014 settlement is not an admission of guilt and the prosecutor recorded Finmeccanica's non-involvement; Michel denies wrongdoing." Change "charges were still not framed after seven years (Dec 2025)" to "charges not yet framed on 23 Dec 2025, more than seven years after Michel's arrest and over 12 years after the 2013 FIR". Change "convicted the executives in 2016" to "convicted former CEO Orsi (and Spagnolini) on 8 Apr 2016; annulled by Cassation 16 Dec 2016". srcs: add the Leonardo release https://www.leonardo.com/en/press-release-detail/-/detail/finmeccanica-the-italian-judge-accepts-the-requests-made-by-agustawestland-to-bring-to-an-end-the-indian-case and Defense News https://www.defensenews.com/industry/2019/05/22/former-leonardo-ceo-gets-final-acquittal-in-helicopter-kickback-case/. The Wikipedia URL https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._P._Tyagi is a redirect to Shashindra_Pal_Tyagi, so cite the canonical title. Keep status "contested". Do not record the uncorroborated April 2026 Delhi HC item (already excluded in c074).

verdicts.dateTest: Claim restated: BEML (DPSU), with Ministry of Defence officials, supplied Tatra all-terrain trucks to the Army through a UK-based intermediary at an alleged ~60% mark-up, and this was a Rs 750 crore scam (purchases from 1986 onward; allegations made public 2009-2012). Stated dates match the sources. Defence Minister A K Antony (26 Oct 2006 to 26 May 2014) referred the case to CBI. BEML CMD VRS Natarajan was suspended on 11 Jun 2012 (Tribune: 'The Ministry of Defence (MoD) suspended Chairman-cum-Managing-Director ... VRS Natarajan this morning'). CBI filed its closure report on 26 Aug 2014 (Oneindia). The bribe-offer FIR was filed in Oct 2012, charges were framed on 2 Aug 2019, and the Delhi HC dismissed the challenge in 2022. The Tribune dates that dismissal to 'June 2022'; the file's source is dated 22 Jul 2022, a minor inconsistency. Antony was cross-examined on 28 Sep 2022. One flag: Oneindia's 'On March 30, CBI registered a case' does not match the record. 30 Mar 2012 is the date of V K Singh's letter (Devdiscourse: 'letters of March 30 and April 10, 2012'), so 'March 30' should not be used as an FIR date. The narrative itself says only '2012', which is safe.
verdicts.identityTest: BEML = Bharat Earth Movers Ltd, the Bangalore-based DPSU (co:beml). The CMD is named in the Tribune as VRS Natarajan. The intermediary is named as 'NRI Ravi Rishi' (Tribune) and 'Vectra Group owner Ravinder Rishi' (Oneindia). Rishi died 13 Mar 2016. The narrative does not name him, which is correct. The accused in the bribe case, Lt Gen (retd) Tejinder Singh, sits below the file's public-rank threshold, and the narrative rightly calls him 'a retired Lt Gen'. Problem: the narrative's evidence mixes two cases. (1) The BEML overpricing/middleman case (FIR Jun 2012, closure report Aug 2014) is the only case the Rs 750 crore figure belongs to. (2) The Rs 14 crore bribe-offer case under s.12 of the PC Act (FIR Oct 2012, charges 2019) concerns 'procurement of 1676 HMVs including Tatra vehicles'. It is a separate case and does not test the Rs 750 crore figure. Both strongestCase (charges framed 2019) and strongestCounter (Antony's 2022 testimony) draw on case (2). The text says 'separate trial', but the field still uses case (2) as evidence for or against a figure that belongs only to case (1).
verdicts.baseRate: Final convictions are 0 of the 7 named defence cases in this file (Bofors, Rafale, AgustaWestland, Tatra, Adarsh, Sukna, Pegasus). The 7 are the brief's chosen cases, not a sample. A large headline 'scam' figure with no court finding behind it is the norm for Indian defence-procurement scandals, not a marker unique to this case. AgustaWestland (also UPA era) was run as the control with identical fields: FIR, intermediary, a retired senior officer, the then Defence Minister ordering CBI, no conviction. The lens gives the same 'contested' reading for both, and the file treats them symmetrically. The trigger is non-partisan: the then UPA Defence Minister ordered the probe, and the allegation came from the then Army Chief.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, and it is already in a source the file holds but has not used. Tribune, 12 Jun 2012 (https://www.tribuneindia.com/2012/20120612/main1.htm): 'Natarajan said the General's assessment of the trucks was incorrect and he sought an apology from the General otherwise he would sue him for defamation', and 'Natarajan today said he respected the government's decision and maintained he would come out clean.' c076 says 'BEML's own response was not retrieved'; that is wrong. CBI's own closure report (26 Aug 2014, Oneindia: 'closed its probe into the Tatra scam saying that there was insufficient evidence to file a charge sheet') is the institutional counter. In the bribe-offer case, Tejinder Singh's counsel argued that 'no offence under Section 12 ... was made out' (Devdiscourse). No response from Rishi or Vectra was located. None of the sources says BEML or Vectra was asked about the Rs 750 crore figure itself.
verdicts.innocentReading: BEML had bought Tatra trucks through Tatra Sipox UK / the Vectra-linked channel since the 1980s under licensing and distribution arrangements. The price difference may reflect that channel's licensing, localisation and after-sales structure, which predates the 2006 procurement manual. CBI could not find evidence of bribes and filed for closure. On this reading the case shows a procurement-rule question (OEM direct vs intermediary) and an unproven bribe-offer allegation, not a proven Rs 750 crore theft. The Rs 750 crore figure is an unattributed 'It was alleged that BEML officials, and the defence ministry siphoned off at least Rs 750 crore' in an Oneindia explainer. No FIR, court order or audit quantified in the opened sources gives that figure.
verdicts.reason: I could not refute the narrative as recorded, because its status is 'contested', not 'established'. That calibration holds: an FIR, the CMD's suspension and a pending bribe-offer trial stand against CBI's own 2014 closure report and zero convictions. Every factual element in strongestCase and strongestCounter is supported by the four opened sources. Quoted: Tribune 2012 'cost the Army around 60 per cent more than what the Tatra, the manufacturer, sells it to the middleman'; Oneindia 'CBI on Tuesday (August 26, 2014) closed its probe ... insufficient evidence'; Devdiscourse on the 1676 HMVs / Rs 14 crore; Tribune 2022 on Antony's 'no official complaint regarding the incident was made either to him or to the ministry'. The source check is only 'partially' confirmed for three reasons. (a) The Rs 750 crore figure, which is the narrative's headline, rests on one unattributed explainer sentence with no named source. (b) Antony's testimony and the 2019 charges belong to the separate bribe-offer case, not the overpricing case. (c) BEML's denial sits in a source the file already holds and is not used. If this were an edge, the right tier would be 'alleged', carrying its contra (c076).
verdicts.corrections:
1) Narrative strongestCase: attribute the figure. Write: 'Rs 750 crore is an unattributed figure in an Oneindia explainer ("It was alleged that BEML officials, and the defence ministry siphoned off at least Rs 750 crore"); no FIR, court or audit document in hand quantifies the loss.' Also note that the 2019 charges concern the Rs 14 crore bribe-offer case (1676 HMVs), not the overpricing/Rs 750 crore case.
2) Narrative strongestCounter: add BEML CMD Natarajan's denial from the Tribune of 12 Jun 2012 ('the General's assessment of the trucks was incorrect'; 'would come out clean'). Qualify the Antony line: he said no OFFICIAL complaint was made, but 'Mr V K Singh once told me about the case ... He mentioned the name of Tejinder Singh', and that V K Singh 'did not want to pursue the matter'. This testimony bears on the bribe-offer case only.
3) c076 'd': delete 'BEML's own response was not retrieved'. Replace it with the Natarajan quote above.
4) whatWouldChangeThis / gaps: say that reports say the Special Judge (named as Pulastya Pramachala) questioned the closure and did not accept it, calling CBI's failure to produce the pre-2006 procurement manual 'shocking'. Located only in PGurus (low credibility) and search summaries; no mainstream or court-order source was opened. Record this as a gap to fill from the Special CBI court order or a PTI report, not as fact.
5) c077 'lab': the HC dismissal is dated 22 Jul 2022 (Devdiscourse) but 'June 2022' in the Tribune. Note the discrepancy or cite the HC order directly.
6) Do not adopt Oneindia's 'On March 30, CBI registered a case'. 30 Mar 2012 is the date of V K Singh's letter.
7) Optional: one-sentence claim text 'The Tatra/BEML truck purchases involved an alleged Rs 750 crore in bribes and commissions (unattributed figure); CBI sought closure in 2014.' This keeps the circulating narrative but marks where the figure comes from.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim as actor-did-thing-when: Bombay HC (Ranjit More and R.G. Ketkar JJ) ordered the Adarsh building demolished on 29 Apr 2016 in WP 452/2012. That holds. The order is para 120: "We further direct respondents no.1 to 3 to forthwith demolish the building of the fourth respondent-Adarsh Co-operative Housing Society Ltd." Para 124 stayed it for 12 weeks. The SC halted demolition on 22 Jul 2016 (Deccan Chronicle: "asked the Centre to take over possession and to ensure that no demolition takes place"). The MoEF demolition order is dated 14.1.2011 and is cited inside the HC judgment. The HC quashed the sanction against Chavan on 22 Dec 2017 ("quashed and set aside. Writ petition is allowed"). ThePrint, 20 Apr 2024, reports the SC demolition petitions still pending. The dates are consistent. The CAG report (2011) comes before the court orders. Problem: strongestCase says "The CAG and the Bombay High Court ... ordered demolition". The CAG did not order demolition and has no power to. Wikipedia's summary says the CAG did not recommend it either.
verdicts.identityTest: The entity is correct: Adarsh Co-operative Housing Society Ltd, CTS No. 652, Block VI, Colaba Division, respondent no. 4 in WP 452/2012. But the "the Army claims the land" part of strongestCase is contradicted by the record's own primary source. The HC judgment quotes the Defence Estates Officer, Mumbai Circle (2000): "the land in question forms part of Block VI of Colaba Division (Back Bay Reclamation Scheme-VI) which belongs to the Government of Maharashtra and falls outside the Defence Boundary." It also quotes HQ Mumbai Sub Area: "the Army land does not fall in Block-VI." The Army's petition rested on the missing Defence NOC, MMRDA waiving conditions and a security threat to the Colaba Military Station (questions i–vii), not on title. So the land was state government land, not Army land. Whoever "grabbed" it, the courts did not identify them. The HC said explicitly that it would not comment on the GOCs because they were not parties.
verdicts.baseRate: Of the seven case records in this file (Bofors, Rafale, AgustaWestland, Tatra, Adarsh, Sukna, Pegasus), Adarsh is the only one with a court order to demolish or undo the asset. Final convictions are 0 of 7. The property is discriminating, not generic. Symmetry: this is a UPA-era (2010–11) matter. The central figure, former Congress CM Ashok Chavan, joined the BJP in Feb 2024 (ThePrint, 20 Apr 2024). The record should note that party change in the same fields it uses for the NDA-era cases. The lens itself is applied the same way to Rafale ("petitions dismissed"), so no asymmetry of method was found.
verdicts.denialFound: Yes, on the record. In the 2016 HC judgment the Society (Navroz Seervai) argued gross delay and laches, that all building permissions and the environment clearance were valid and unchallenged, and that the "Occupation Certificate ... is revoked without following due process of law" (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/121443544/). Chavan won the HC's quashing of the Governor's prosecution sanction on 22 Dec 2017 (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/47015928/). The Society's advocate told ThePrint (20 Apr 2024) that appeals and a regularisation plea were pending (https://theprint.in/india/demolition-regularisation-pleas-pending-chavan-moves-on-but-mumbais-adarsh-society-languishes/2048404/). The Society was not asked by this project.
verdicts.innocentReading: The boring reading that fits the court record: a co-operative society got state government land under the Maharashtra Land Revenue Code and planning permissions from MMRDA/BMC. The building was later found to need a Defence NOC it never obtained, and to pose a security concern next to the Colaba Military Station. The HC ordered demolition for those reasons: planning, NOC and security. It made no finding of a "land grab". The "grab" language comes from the CAG, and the record took it from a Wikipedia quotation, not from the report itself (the PDF was unreachable). Separately, the 2013 Judicial Commission findings (25 illegal allotments, 22 by proxy, per ThePrint) support irregular allotment of flats. But no court has finally adjudicated that, and the criminal sanction against the former CM was quashed.
verdicts.reason: The narrative joins two things that were never found together. "Land grab" is the CAG's wording, read only second-hand through Wikipedia. "Courts ordered demolished" is the HC's 2016 order, and its stated grounds were a missing Defence NOC, MMRDA waivers and a security threat, not land grab. On ownership, the HC record shows the land was state government land outside the defence boundary. Two supporting assertions are also factually wrong: that the CAG "ordered demolition", and that "the Army claims the land". The demolition-order-and-SC-stay half is documented from the primary judgment. The land-grab half is at most reported (a CAG quote via a secondary source). As written, with "well-supported" status and a strongestCase containing errors, it does not survive.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Rewrite the claim as: "The CAG (Report No. 11 of 2011, quoted via secondary sources) described Adarsh as officials subverting rules 'to grab prime government land'; the Bombay HC on 29 Apr 2016 ordered the building demolished for want of a Defence NOC and on security grounds; the SC halted demolition on 22 Jul 2016 and appeals remained pending as of Apr 2024." 2) In strongestCase, remove "The CAG ... ordered demolition". The CAG neither ordered nor recommended demolition; only the HC (and MoEF, 14 Jan 2011) did. 3) Replace "the Army claims the land" with "the Army argued no Defence NOC was obtained and the building threatens the Colaba Military Station; the Army's own DEO recorded in 2000 that the land belongs to the Government of Maharashtra, outside the defence boundary." 4) In strongestCounter, change "a valid Occupation Certificate" to "the Occupation Certificate was revoked without due process (Society's argument)". 5) Change status from "well-supported" to "partly supported": demolition order documented; land-grab characterisation reported (CAG PDF not opened). 6) Add a dated stage: ThePrint, 20 Apr 2024, reports three SC petitions against demolition plus one against MCZMA's refusal of post-facto environment clearance pending. Add that Ashok Chavan joined the BJP in Feb 2024 (symmetry field). 7) Treat the Deccan Chronicle URL slug "sc-quashes-hc-order" with care: the article body says the SC halted demolition and directed possession, not that it quashed the order.

verdicts.dateTest: PASS. Read as a claim: the two court-martialled Lt Gens (33 Corps commander P K Rath; Military Secretary Avadhesh Prakash) committed corruption over the 2009 Sukna NOC. The NOC (2009) falls inside Rath's 33 Corps tenure. Rath's GCM verdict came in Jan 2011 and the AFT acquitted him on 5 Sep 2014; Deccan Chronicle 6 Sep 2014 says "The Armed Forces Tribunal on Friday acquitted former 33 Corps chief Lt. Gen. P.K. Rath (retd.) of all charges that he had been found guilty of by an Army Court Martial in January, 2011". Prakash's GCM dismissed him. The AFT ruled on 20 Dec 2017 and the SC on 24 Jan 2019. All the rulings come after the events and are in the right order. One dating error sits in the source, not the record: the LSI summary says the case "broke out in the end of the year 2010". The record's 'end 2009/2010' is fine.
verdicts.identityTest: PASS, with one error. The 'court-martialled generals' are the two officers who were court-martialled, Rath and Prakash. The other two indicted by the court of inquiry (Halgali and Sen) faced administrative action only. Both are identified by office and by the case captions, e.g. 'Ex Lt Gen Avadhesh Prakash v. Union of India, 24 Jan 2019, Sikri/Nazeer/Shah JJ'. The error is in strongestCase, which says a GCM 'found one guilty in Jan 2011'. Both GCMs returned guilty findings. Per the SC judgment, Prakash's GCM "found the appellant guilty on charges second, third and fourth and sentenced him to 'Dismissal from Service'". Rank note: a retired Lt Gen is below the 'service chief' threshold in CONTRACT-force. The narrative text does not name them and should stay that way. They appear only in source titles, in an exculpatory court record.
verdicts.baseRate: 0 of 7 case records in this file end in a surviving final conviction (claim money-people c-series 'Final convictions in the records opened: 0 of 7'). The property 'outcome set aside or not adjudicated' is common to every case in the set, so it does not single Sukna out. That does not hurt this record, because the narrative argues against guilt, not for it. Symmetry: Sukna (UPA-II era, 2009 NOC) is set beside Rafale and Pegasus (NDA era) using the same fields. Here the 'unsupported' verdict tracks court rulings, not who was in government.
verdicts.denialFound: The accused officers' answer is the judicial record. Rath was acquitted of all charges by the AFT on 5 Sep 2014, with Rs 1 lakh costs and benefits restored at 12% interest (https://www.deccanchronicle.com/140906/nation-current-affairs/article/lt-general-p-k-rathretd-cleared-sukna-scam). The tribunal found the trial 'influenced and vitiated' and blamed then-Army chief V K Singh (https://www.ibtimes.co.in/sukna-land-deal-lt-gen-rath-acquitted-claims-vk-singh-filed-case-revenge-608445). The SC set aside Prakash's GCM on 24 Jan 2019 (https://indiankanoon.org/doc/156623410/). The other side also answered: V K Singh 'hits back' and urged MoD to appeal the AFT order (Deccan Herald, https://www.deccanherald.com/india/v-k-singh-hits-back-2205886). I found no record of an SC appeal by the Union against Rath's acquittal. I searched and that absence is unconfirmed, not proven.
verdicts.innocentReading: The NOC and MoU episode was a procedural failure: an NOC issued without authority and superiors not informed. The courts did not treat it as proven corruption. Rath's GCM reportedly dropped the 'intent to defraud' charge, though outlets conflict on this (DNA vs others). The AFT then acquitted him outright. For Prakash, the only charge the AFT upheld was 'unbecoming conduct' under Army Act s.45, not a corruption offence. The SC then voided the whole GCM because a Lt Gen was tried by members below his rank. Neither officer now stands convicted of anything.
verdicts.reason: The narrative survives. Its central point holds on primary records: neither court-martialled general stands convicted, and no corruption finding survives. Rath was acquitted on the merits by the AFT, and that is reported by two independent outlets. Prakash's GCM was declared void by a three-judge SC bench, which refused a fresh GCM ("no useful purpose would be served in remitting the case back"). But the record overstates the exoneration and miscites a source. (1) The parenthetical 'unsupported by the later AFT and SC rulings' is wrong for Prakash. The AFT on 20 Dec 2017 upheld his conviction on charge two (s.45, unbecoming conduct). The SC did not examine the merits. It voided the GCM on a composition ground and itself wrote "It is only one charge that ultimately stands established against the appellant. That charge is also not of a very serious nature." (2) The quote 'influenced and vitiated' is pinned on the Deccan Chronicle URL, which does not contain it; IBTimes does. (3) strongestCase undercounts the GCM guilty findings, which were two, not one. (4) whatWouldChangeThis proposes 'a fresh valid proceeding', but the SC expressly declined to remand. These are field fixes, not a refutation. The 'unsupported' status is right as to corruption.
verdicts.corrections: narratives[7].strongestCase: change to 'An Army court of inquiry indicted four generals; two were court-martialled and both GCMs returned guilty findings — Lt Gen Rath (Jan 2011: loss of seniority, pension service and severe reprimand) and Lt Gen Prakash (guilty on three charges, dismissal).' narratives[7].strongestCounter: change to 'AFT, 5 Sep 2014, acquitted Rath of all charges and held the trial "influenced and vitiated" [IBTimes]; for Prakash the AFT (20 Dec 2017) sustained only one charge, unbecoming conduct under s.45, not corruption, and the Supreme Court on 24 Jan 2019 voided the entire GCM because it sat below his rank, without ruling on merits, noting the one surviving charge was "not of a very serious nature" and declining a fresh GCM.' Claim text: change the parenthetical to '(no conviction survives: AFT acquittal on merits for one; SC voided the other's GCM on composition)'. narratives[7].whatWouldChangeThis: 'None available in law for Prakash, since the SC declined remand; for Rath, a Union appeal against the AFT order (none found).' srcs: add IBTimes https://www.ibtimes.co.in/sukna-land-deal-lt-gen-rath-acquitted-claims-vk-singh-filed-case-revenge-608445 for 'influenced and vitiated'. Add the primary SC judgment https://indiankanoon.org/doc/156623410/ beside or instead of the LSI summary; the LSI print URL returns 406 to curl and opens via WebFetch. Same fixes for force:case-sukna d[3]/d[4] and claim money-people:c084 (move the 'influenced and vitiated' attribution to IBTimes). c085 can go to documented with the indiankanoon link. Keep the officers unnamed in labels and text, since they are below the service-chief threshold.

verdicts.dateTest: Claim: Union of India (NDA; MeitY under Ashwini Vaishnaw, MHA under Amit Shah, from 7 Jul 2021) allegedly used Pegasus on Indian phones. The allegation dates from the Citizen Lab/Amnesty report of 15 Jun 2020 and the consortium reports of 18 Jul 2021. The SC order of 27 Oct 2021, the bench's reading of the panel report on 25 Aug 2022 and the 29 Apr 2025 hearing all fall inside the NDA window, so the dates overlap. One slip: the file (c087, from: 2021-07-18) dates the Minister's statement to Parliament as 18 Jul 2021 because the SC order says '18th July 2021'. The suo motu statement was made in the Lok Sabha on 19 Jul 2021, about the media reports of 18 Jul (PIB PRID 1736803, titled '...as reported in Media on 18th July 2021').
verdicts.identityTest: The actor is 'the Government', meaning the Union of India as respondent in WP(Crl) 314/2021 (Manohar Lal Sharma v UoI and connected petitions). The order names the Additional Secretary, MeitY, as the deponent of the 16 Aug 2021 'limited affidavit'. NSO Group is identified as Pegasus's producer in the order. No state government or agency (IB, NTRO, R&AW) is named as user in any source, and the narrative correctly names none. The identity holds at the level of 'Union of India'. It does not hold at the level of any agency.
verdicts.baseRate: Citizen Lab (2018) traced Pegasus operators to about 45 countries, and the 2021 leaked list covered more than 10 countries. India is one of several democracies (Mexico, Hungary, Poland, Spain) where government use is alleged. So 'alleged state Pegasus user' does not single India out. The narrative does not claim it does. It claims only that the question is contested, and that framing does not depend on the base rate.
verdicts.denialFound: Union: the SG reiterated the Minister's statement that unauthorised surveillance does not take place, filed only a limited affidavit and cited national security (SC order, https://indiankanoon.org/doc/39021018/: 'He reiterated the statement dated 18th July 2021 made by the Hon'ble Minister ... which ensures that unauthorized surveillance does not take place'). The narrative leaves out three more denials. (1) MoS Defence Ajay Bhatt told the Rajya Sabha in writing on 9 Aug 2021 that the 'Ministry of Defence has not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies' (https://scroll.in/latest/1002445/pegasus-row-defence-ministry-has-not-had-any-transaction-with-nso-group-says-centre). (2) After the NYT report of 28 Jan 2022, MoS V K Singh called the NYT 'Supari Media' (https://theprint.in/india/union-minister-v-k-singh-calls-nyt-supari-media-over-its-report-on-pegasus/816036/). (3) The MEA said the matter was before the SC committee and it had 'no information' (https://www.deccanherald.com/india/no-information-available-with-us-mea-on-pegasus-row-1077829.html). None of these is a sworn denial of use by the Union as a whole. MoD's denial covers MoD only.
verdicts.innocentReading: Several readings fit the evidence. Pegasus traces on Indian phones (Amnesty 2021; Amnesty/Washington Post Dec 2023) could come from a foreign government client of NSO. The 5 infected phones the committee found carried malware other than Pegasus. The Union's refusal to file a detailed affidavit could reflect a standard national-security posture that is not specific to Pegasus. Lawful interception under s.5(2) Telegraph Act/s.69 IT Act exists and does not need Pegasus. None of this is excluded, so 'contested' is the right status. 'Documented' would be too high and 'unsupported' too low.
verdicts.reason: All three cited sources say what the narrative attributes to them. The SC order quotes the 'limited affidavit', the 'free pass' line and the SG's reliance on the Minister's statement. The Tribune quotes CJI Ramana: 'In five phones some malware was found but the technical committee says it can't be said to be Pegasus', and reports that the bench quoted the panel as saying the Government did not help it. LawBeat quotes 'To have spyware, there is nothing wrong. The question is against whom it is being used' and 'we are not going to disclose a single word'. 'Contested' is an accurate status for 'the Government used Pegasus'. No court, audit or official record establishes use or non-use, the report is sealed, and the Union has neither confirmed nor specifically denied use on affidavit. The narrative makes no factual assertion beyond that status, names no one below public rank and contains no operational detail. So it is not killed and not refuted. It is incomplete on both sides, though: the strongest case leaves out the NYT purchase report and the Amnesty forensics, and the strongest counter leaves out the MoD Rajya Sabha answer and the MEA statement. The underlying claim stays 'alleged' with its contra, and the narrative stays 'contested'.
verdicts.corrections: 1. strongestCase: add the NYT report of 28 Jan 2022 that India bought Pegasus in 2017 as part of a roughly $2bn India-Israel package. It has one outlet with named sourcing, so tier it 'reported', and attach its denial. Add Amnesty Security Lab's forensic confirmation of Pegasus on Indian journalists' phones (July 2021, and 28 Dec 2023: Varadarajan and Mangnale, last infection Oct 2023, https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2023/12/india-damning-new-forensic-investigation-reveals-repeated-use-of-pegasus-spyware-to-target-high-profile-journalists/). This shows Pegasus was used against Indian citizens but does not attribute it to the Indian state. 2. strongestCounter: add the MoD written answer in the Rajya Sabha of 9 Aug 2021, 'not had any transaction with NSO Group Technologies', which is a documented Parliament answer limited to MoD. Add the MEA 'no information' statement and V K Singh's response to the NYT. 3. c087 'from': change 2021-07-18 to 2021-07-19, the date of the Lok Sabha suo motu statement (PIB PRID 1736803), and note that the SC order calls it 'statement dated 18th July 2021'. 4. Add the PIB statement as a primary source for the Minister's position. Vaishnaw's statement denies 'illegal surveillance' rather than use of Pegasus as such, and the narrative should say so explicitly. 5. whatWouldChangeThis: add 'a sworn affidavit by the Union confirming or denying procurement or use, or disclosure of procurement records'.

verdicts.dateTest: Restated, the claim is: governments of the UPA (2004-14) or NDA (1998-2004, 2014-) <presided over worse> defence scandals <in those windows>. The record makes no directional assertion. Its status is 'speculative'. Its strongestCase is a count of 4 UPA, 2 NDA and 1 earlier, and that count uses a mixed criterion ('decided OR surfaced'), which flatters whichever bucket it is applied to. AgustaWestland: the Wikipedia source confirms 'contract to purchase 12 AgustaWestland AW101 helicopters in February 2010', which is UPA. The specification history goes back to the NDA-I years, but the cited page does not cover it. Tatra/BEML: purchases ran from the 1980s through 2012 under several governments, including NDA-I. Only the surfacing (2012) and the bribe-offer allegation (22 Sep 2010) fall under UPA. Bofors: the contract was 1986 under a Congress government (Rajiv Gandhi). The Delhi HC quashed the corruption charges in Feb 2004 under NDA-I, and the 2005 Hinduja order and the 2011 withdrawal came under UPA. Calling it 'earlier' therefore hides a split decided/surfaced record. Adarsh was a Congress-NCP state matter and Sukna was an internal Army matter. Neither is a Union procurement decision. Pegasus (2021, NDA) is a surveillance matter, not a defence procurement scandal. The count's date attribution does not survive per-case testing.
verdicts.identityTest: The cases are the ones the SPEC names (force:case-bofors, case-rafale, case-agustawestland, etc.), so the case identities hold. The actor 'UPA/NDA' is a coalition label and not an office-holder. It cannot be resolved to a decision-maker per case: Adarsh was a state government, Sukna an Army court of inquiry, and Tatra spanned several governments. The comparison unit (a 'scandal') is undefined. It has no stage, amount or investigator field to compare on.
verdicts.baseRate: Non-discriminating. Every government since 1986 has a headline defence-corruption allegation: Bofors (Congress 1986); Tehelka Operation West End, the Kargil coffin case and Barak (NDA-I 2001-06); AgustaWestland and Tatra (UPA-II); Rafale (NDA-II). That is effectively 100% of governments, well above the 80% threshold. Final convictions are near 0% across all of them. The record's own counter says 'Zero final convictions in all seven'. The AW Wikipedia page confirms no Indian conviction. Tatra charges were framed on 2 Aug 2019 and the trial is ongoing, with no verdict found. The seven cases are a brief-selected sample and not a census. The SPEC's UPA-II vs NDA control cannot be run without a CBI/ED defence case list by year, and the record correctly names that as whatWouldChangeThis. Material omission: the only trial-court convictions in a defence-deal corruption case found in this check come from the NDA-I-era Tehelka sting. Jaya Jaitly, Gopal Pacherwal and Maj Gen S.P. Murgai (retd) were convicted and sentenced to 4 years in July 2020 (Tribune, Deccan Chronicle), and Bangaru Laxman was convicted in 2012. Neither conviction is final: Jaitly's is understood to be stayed on appeal, and Laxman's appeal was pending when he died. Leaving these out makes the UPA-heavy count look more lopsided than the record supports.
verdicts.denialFound: Not applicable as one party's denial, because the narrative accuses no single party. Case-level answers are carried on the other narratives: Dassault/MoD/Reliance on Rafale, the 2005 HC order on Bofors, and the Tyagi side on AgustaWestland. No response from Congress or BJP to the comparative framing was recorded. Nobody was asked.
verdicts.innocentReading: Defence procurement is large, lumpy, agent-mediated and slow. Every government inherits contracts signed under earlier ones, and allegations surface years after the decision. The count of scandals per government therefore mostly tracks when a case surfaced and how long it has had to run (older cases are resolved; newer ones are sealed or still in trial). It does not track relative probity. Courts and agencies have not produced final convictions for either side, so neither partisan reading has an adjudicated basis.
verdicts.reason: The record survives because it asserts nothing. It marks itself 'speculative', presents both directions, and names the missing census. It cannot be refuted as a claim, only corrected as framing. Its strongestCase count (4 UPA / 2 NDA / 1 earlier) does not hold up. It is a conjunction of individually true dates that together imply a UPA skew none of the sources states. It mixes 'decided' with 'surfaced'. It assigns multi-government cases (Tatra, Bofors, arguably AgustaWestland) to one side. It counts a state housing case (Adarsh), an internal Army case (Sukna) and a surveillance case (Pegasus) as defence scandals. And it omits NDA-I (Tehelka, coffin, Barak), which is where the only trial-court convictions found in this check sit. The sources are three Wikipedia pages and do not support the count itself. The tier must be analytic (our own comparison), with innocentReading attached, and not documented or reported.
verdicts.corrections: 1) Set tier to 'analytic' and add an innocentReading (the text above). 2) Consider changing status from 'speculative' to 'unsupported'. No comparative metric or census exists either way, and the record admits the sample is the brief's. 3) Rewrite strongestCase. Drop the bare 4/2/1 count, or tabulate each case by decision government and surfacing government separately: Bofors 1986 Congress / 1987, with the HC quash Feb 2004 under NDA-I; Tatra purchases from 1986 across governments, surfaced 2012 under UPA; AgustaWestland contract Feb 2010 UPA, surfaced 2012-13; Rafale IGA 2016 NDA; Adarsh state Congress-NCP; Sukna Army 2008; Pegasus reported 2021. 4) Flag that Pegasus, Adarsh and Sukna are not Union defence-procurement decisions, or move them out of the comparison. 5) Add NDA-I cases to strongestCounter: Tehelka Operation West End (2001), with trial-court convictions of Bangaru Laxman (2012) and Jaya Jaitly/Pacherwal/Murgai (Jul 2020, 4 yrs; not final). Sources: https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/tehelka-expose-jaya-jaitly-2-others-convicted-in-corruption-case-117863 and https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/300720/tehalka-expose-jaya-jaitly-two-others-sentenced-to-4-years-in-jail-f.html. Edit 'Zero final convictions in all seven' to add that trial-court convictions exist outside the sample, in an NDA-I-era sting case. 6) Replace or supplement the Wikipedia-only srcs with the case-level primary records already in narratives 2-5 (Indian Kanoon orders, CAG Report 3 of 2019). 7) Add to whatWouldChangeThis: a Parliament answer listing CBI defence-procurement FIRs and MoD debarments by year and stage, run across NDA-I, UPA-I, UPA-II and NDA-II.
